e.D-E1-55: The text says 「四月からは入り口の機械でご自分で手続きをしてください」 (From April, please do the procedure yourself at the machine at the entrance). Dictionaries and magazines stay in-library only, the number of books does not change, and the return box can still be used, so the other choices are wrong.
e.D-E1-56: The author writes that students whose hands move at the moment they feel 「大事だ」 (this is important) improve their grades. The author thinks a notebook is not something to show others but a record of one's own thinking.
e.D-E1-57: The message says 「当日使う資料は、前日の夜までに私にメールで送ってください」 (Please email me the materials you will use by the night before). Printing is done by the teacher and the room's computer is used, so Yamada only needs to email the materials.
e.D-E1-58: The text says 「どこから分からないのかがはっきりする」 (it becomes clear where you stop understanding) and 「そのうえで聞けば、相手の答えは自分の中にすっと入ってくる」 (if you ask after that, the answer sinks in easily). So thinking first makes the answer easier to remember.
e.D-E1-59: The text says 「シューズは各自で用意してください」 (Please prepare your own shoes). Rackets are lent, rainy days are spent in the gym, and the attendance card is needed only for the first month.
e.D-E1-60: The text says 「学生には好評である」 (it is popular with students) and 「平均点はむしろ少し上がった」 (the average score actually went up a little). So students like it and grades have not gotten worse.
e.D-E1-61: Just before 「この合図」 (this signal), the text says 「前の席の学生が急にペンを止め、後ろの学生が隣の人の手元をのぞく」 (a student in front suddenly stops writing, and a student behind peeks at a neighbor's notes). This is the change in students' behavior when they do not understand the explanation.
e.D-E1-62: The author gives two reasons. One is that in a classroom the students' behavior shows the signal that they do not understand; the other is that important questions come out in the ten minutes after class.
e.D-E1-63: The text says 「十七、八歳で決めた進路をそのまま歩き続けている学生は、実はそれほど多くない」 (students who keep following the path they chose at 17 or 18 are actually not that many). So not many students keep their original path.
e.D-E1-64: The author writes 「日本の学校が『変える』ための時間をあまり用意していないことだろう」 (the problem is probably that Japanese schools do not provide much time for "changing"). The problem is not deciding early, but having no time to change one's mind or hesitate.
e.D-E1-65: The text says 「困った顔をして黙る学生とは、そこから長い話が始まる」 (with a student who goes quiet with a troubled face, a long talk begins from there). The question is meant to notice students who are unsure and to start a conversation with them.
e.D-E1-66: The text says 「驚いたのは、本の量ではなく、机の多さである」 (what surprised me was not the amount of books but the number of desks). It explains that single seats line up and every seat has a power outlet, so the author was surprised by the many seats for studying.
e.D-E1-67: The author names 「お金を払わなくても誰でもそこにいていい場所」 (a place where anyone can be without paying) as what libraries have protected for a long time. So the author thinks it is meaningful even when people use it without borrowing books.
e.D-E1-68: The last sentence is 「本と、いつか読むかもしれない人のための場所」 (a place for books and for people who may read someday). Since the author thinks 「人は、そこにいる時間が長いほど、周りのものに手を伸ばす。図書館はそれを待てばいい」 (the longer people stay, the more they reach for things around them; the library can just wait), the point is that a library also waits for people who do not read now.
e.D-E2-55: The email says 「出席者は必ず目を通してから会議に出てください」 (attendees must read the materials before attending). The materials are put in the shared folder by 5 p.m. the day before, so attendees read them before the meeting.
e.D-E2-56: The author writes 「大切なのは、渡すときにどんな言葉を添えるかだ」 (what matters is what words you add when handing it over). A business card alone will not make people remember you, so a one-line explanation of your work is important.
e.D-E2-57: The author writes 「相談してよい時間をあらかじめ決めておくなど、声を出しやすくする工夫が必要だろう」 (we need ideas that make it easier to speak up, such as deciding in advance when people may ask for advice). In short, ways to make consulting easier are needed.
e.D-E2-58: The notice says 「弁当を持参する方は、これまでどおり四階の休憩室をご利用いただけます」 (people who bring a lunch box can use the 4th-floor break room as before). The sales department starts at 11:30, people can enter after the set time, and nothing is said about more kinds of dishes.
e.D-E2-59: The author writes 「しかられたのは、失敗そのものではなく、報告が遅れたことだった」 (what I was scolded for was not the failure itself but the delay in reporting). The author was scolded because telling about the mistake was late.
e.D-E2-60: The author says employees who can follow the manual have increased, but 「そこに書かれていない場面になると、急に手が止まってしまう」 (in situations not written there, they suddenly stop). The author is troubled that new employees cannot act in situations the manual does not cover.
e.D-E2-61: In the next paragraph the author writes 「悪いのは本人ではない。私たちがマニュアルを、ただ守るものとしてだけ渡してきたからだろう」 (the person is not to blame; it is because we only handed over the manual as something to obey). The author thought the problem lay in how they taught, so the author fell into thought.
e.D-E2-62: At the end the author writes 「考えるための土台にするためにあるのだと思う」 (I think it exists to serve as a foundation for thinking). A manual is not meant to remove the need to think but to be used as a base for thinking for oneself.
e.D-E2-63: The first paragraph says 「会議は予定どおりに終わり、結論も出る。それで、うまく進行できたつもりでいた」 (the meeting ended on schedule and reached a conclusion; I thought I had run it well). The author used to think a meeting that ended on time was a success.
e.D-E2-64: The author writes 「私は毎回、その時間をつぶしていたことになる」 (so every time, I had been destroying that time). "That time" is the time participants spend searching for words in their heads. So the author had been taking away the participants' time to think.
e.D-E2-65: At the end the text says 「会議の質は、進行役がどれだけ話すかではなく、どれだけ待てるかで決まる」 (the quality of a meeting is decided not by how much the facilitator talks but by how long they can wait). So it depends on how long the facilitator can wait.
e.D-E2-66: The first paragraph says 「書き出してみて、自分がこれほど多くのことを覚えていたのかと驚いた」 (when I wrote it all out, I was surprised that I remembered so much). The author was surprised at how much they had remembered.
e.D-E2-67: The second paragraph says 「意外だったのは、書けなかったことのほうが多かったという事実である」 (what was unexpected was the fact that there were more things I could not write). The author found it unexpected that unwritable things outnumbered the written ones.
e.D-E2-68: The last paragraph says 「後任が自分で判断できるようになるまで見守ることなのだろう」 (handing over is probably watching over the successor until they can judge for themselves). Handover is not passing on knowledge but watching over the successor until they can decide on their own.
e.D-E3-55: The author writes that you always forget things you cannot see, and that even if less fits, food placed where you can see it gets used up. The idea is to keep food visible and use it early.
e.D-E3-56: The email says 「お待ちいただける場合は、こちらからのご連絡は不要です」 (if you can wait, no contact is needed). A phone call is needed only when you want to cancel, so if you wait you do not have to contact them.
e.D-E3-57: The author writes that with a chart people only worried about whether it was their duty, and the habit of whoever noticed doing it quickly disappeared. People stopped acting on their own because they worried about whose duty it was, so the author stopped the chart.
e.D-E3-58: The author writes that whether something lasts depends not only on quality but also on 「自分の暮らしがこれから変わらないかどうか」 (whether my life will stay the same from now on). Things used only while children are small are chosen by price rather than quality, so the author values whether an item fits upcoming changes in life.
e.D-E3-59: The last sentence says 「近所づきあいとは、そういう小さな安心の積み重ねなのだろう」 (neighborly relations are probably an accumulation of such small reassurances). It means that just knowing a name and face through a greeting creates a small sense of security.
e.D-E3-60: The second paragraph says people who cannot throw things away cannot let go not of the object itself but of the time attached to it. In other words, they cannot give up the time linked to that object.
e.D-E3-61: The third paragraph says 「この方法のいいところは、捨てるかどうかをその場で決めなくてよいことだ」 (the good point of this method is that you do not have to decide on the spot whether to throw it away). If you put it in a box for half a year, you do not need to decide right away.
e.D-E3-62: The last paragraph says the author wants to check whether the things in the house match their present life. The purpose of reducing things is to keep only items that fit one's current life.
e.D-E3-63: At the end of the first paragraph it says 「その場で手に取って確かめられたのはありがたかった」 (I was grateful to be able to pick it up and check it on the spot). Even though it cost a little more than online, being able to check and choose on the spot was good.
e.D-E3-64: The third paragraph says that if the shop is not kept open, 「直径を測ってふたを選ぶような知識が、どこにも残らなくなる」 (knowledge like measuring the diameter and choosing a lid will remain nowhere). The owner keeps giving advice so that such knowledge does not disappear.
e.D-E3-65: The last paragraph says that if you keep choosing where to buy by price alone, 「選び方を教えてくれる場所は静かに消えていく」 (places that teach you how to choose quietly disappear), and 「いつか困るのが自分だからである」 (because it is myself who will be in trouble someday). Choosing only by low price will eventually trouble you.
e.D-E3-66: The first paragraph says 「十分近くが、何を作るかを決めるための時間だったことである」 (nearly ten minutes of it was time spent deciding what to cook). The author was surprised that deciding what to cook took so long.
e.D-E3-67: The third paragraph says that in exchange for no longer hesitating, 「その日の気分で作る物を変えることができない」 (I could not change what I cook according to my mood that day). The problem was that deciding the menu in advance made it impossible to change it by mood.

e.K-N-207:

e.K-N-208:
【Correct answer】曇：「曇る」 means the sky becomes covered with clouds so the sun can't be seen. It is written with 曇 and read 「くも（る）」. e.g. 明日は午後から曇るでしょう。（It will probably become cloudy from the afternoon tomorrow.）

e.K-N-209:
【Correct answer】ふくまれて：「含まれる」 means to be included inside. It is the passive of 「含む」, and 含 is read 「ふく（む）」. e.g. この料金には、税金も含まれています。（Tax is also included in this fee.）

e.K-N-210:
【Correct answer】むしあつい：「蒸し暑い」 means hot and humid. 蒸 is read 「む（す）」 (kun reading) and 暑 is read 「あつ（い）」. e.g. 今夜も蒸し暑くて、なかなか眠れない。（It's hot and humid tonight too, and I can't fall asleep.）
【Other choices】
× じょうしあつい：There is no such reading as 「じょうしあつい」. 「蒸し暑い」 here is read 「むしあつい」. e.g. 梅雨は、蒸し暑い日が続く。（In the rainy season, hot and humid days continue.）

e.K-N-211:
【Correct answer】へいきん：「平均」 means the average. 平 is read 「へい」 and 均 is read 「きん」. e.g. この町の平均年齢は、四十五歳だ。（The average age in this town is 45.）
【Other choices】

× へいこう：「へいこう」 is the reading of 「平行」, which means "parallel (two lines that never meet)". The word here is 「平均」, which is read 「へいきん」. e.g. この道は、線路と平行に走っている。（This road runs parallel to the railway.）
e.K-N-212:
【Correct answer】よそく：「予測」 means to predict in advance what will happen. 予 is read 「よ」 and 測 is read 「そく」. e.g. 来年の売り上げを予測して、計画を立てる。（I predict next year's sales and make a plan.）

× ようそく：There is no such reading as 「ようそく」. 「予測」 here is read 「よそく」. e.g. 予測が当たって、うれしかった。（My prediction was right, and I was happy.）
e.K-N-213:
【Correct answer】するどい：「鋭い」 means sharp (pointed), or quick and keen in thinking and perception. 鋭 is read 「するど（い）」 (kun reading). e.g. このナイフは、刃が鋭くて危ない。（This knife has a sharp blade and is dangerous.）

× すどい：There is no such reading as 「すどい」. 「鋭い」 here is read 「するどい」. e.g. 鋭い声が、静かな部屋に響いた。（A sharp voice echoed in the quiet room.）
e.K-N-214:

e.K-N-215:
【Correct answer】液：「消毒液」 is a liquid medicine that kills germs. 液 is read 「えき」 and refers to a flowing, water-like substance. e.g. この薬は、液を水でうすめて使う。（Dilute the liquid of this medicine with water before using it.）

e.K-N-216:
【Correct answer】固：「固定」 means to fasten firmly so that something doesn't move. 固 is read 「こ」. e.g. カメラを台に固定して、写真をとった。（I fixed the camera on a stand and took a photo.）

e.K-N-217:
【Correct answer】くわわった：「加わる」 means to join something that already exists and become part of it. 加 is read 「くわ（わる）」 (kun reading). e.g. 私も、その計画に加わりたい。（I want to join that plan, too.）

e.K-N-218:
【Correct answer】はなれた：「離れる」 means to become apart or distant. 離 is read 「はな（れる）」 (kun reading). e.g. 家族から離れて、一人で暮らしている。（I live alone, away from my family.）

e.K-N-220:
【Correct answer】あつりょく：「圧力」 means pressure, the force that pushes on something. 圧 is read 「あつ」 and 力 is read 「りょく」. e.g. 上司から、仕事の圧力を感じている。（I feel pressure at work from my boss.）

e.K-N-222:

e.K-N-223:
【Correct answer】了：「終了」 means to end. 了 is read 「りょう」 and carries the meaning "to finish". e.g. 試験は、あと五分で終了です。（The exam will end in five more minutes.）

e.K-N-224:

e.K-N-225:
【Correct answer】ういて：「浮く」 means to float on water or in the air without sinking. 浮 is read 「う（く）」 (kun reading). e.g. 木の葉が、池に浮いている。（A leaf is floating on the pond.）

e.K-N-226:

e.K-N-227:
【Correct answer】とちゅう：「途中」 means on the way somewhere, or partway through something. 途 is read 「と」 and 中 is read 「ちゅう」. e.g. 話の途中で、電話が切れてしまった。（The call got cut off in the middle of the conversation.）

e.K-N-228:

e.K-N-229:

e.K-N-230:

文法 Lesson 1|1: At the time of doing something (formal)

When you borrow books at the library, you need a card.
On a business trip, I met the president of a client company.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋際(に)／verb (ta-form)＋際(に)／noun＋の＋際(に)
【Point】Often used in notices, requests and explanations of procedures. More formal than 'toki'; the main clause may contain a request or an intention.
文法 Lesson 1|2: On the occasion of starting something important; used for preparations or feelings

In opening the new shop, I received help from many people.
Before going to study abroad, I prepared the necessary documents.

【Connection】noun＋に際して／にあたって／verb (dictionary form)＋に際して／にあたって
【Point】Used before starting big things such as opening a shop, entering school or signing a contract, not for small daily actions. 'ni saishite' and 'ni atatte' mean almost the same.
文法 Lesson 1|3: Right after X, something unexpected happens

The moment the train door opened, a cold wind came in.
The moment the teacher left the room, the students began to talk.

【Connection】verb (ta-form)＋とたん(に)
【Point】Used for past events. The second half cannot be the speaker's intention, request or command. The two clauses may have different subjects.
文法 Lesson 1|4: Just when I thought X, something else happened right away

He was laughing, and the next moment he got angry.
My brother came home and then went out to play again right away.

【Connection】verb (ta-form)＋(か)と思うと／(か)と思ったら
【Point】Used for past events, with a feeling of surprise at how fast things change. The second half cannot be the speaker's intention or request. Unlike 'totan', the two parts may be opposite in content.
文法 Lesson 1|5: Almost at the same time as X, the next thing happens

Almost as soon as the train stopped, the passengers stood in front of the door.
She fell asleep almost the moment she got into the futon.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋か＋verb (nai-form)＋かのうちに／verb (ta-form)＋か＋verb (nai-form)＋かのうちに
【Point】The same verb is used twice. It feels more 'almost simultaneous' than 'totan'. The main clause is a past event, not the speaker's intention.
文法 Lesson 1|6: Right in the middle of doing X, something disturbing happens

In the middle of the explanation, the microphone suddenly cut out.
While I was hanging out the laundry, it started to rain.

【Connection】verb (te iru form)＋最中だ／noun＋の＋最中だ
【Point】The main clause describes an interruption or an unexpected event. Often used as '~te iru saichuu ni'. The speaker's intention does not follow.
文法 Lesson 1|7: Doing something while the present state lasts, before it changes

I want to travel to many countries while I'm young.
Let's eat before the food gets cold.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋うちに／verb (te iru form)＋うちに／verb (nai-form)＋うちに／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋うちに／na-adjective (stem) ＋ na＋うちに／noun＋の＋うちに
【Point】The main clause is an action to be done now. '~nai uchi ni' means 'before X happens'. The feeling of 'before the state changes' is strong.
文法 Lesson 1|8: A change keeps going in the same (often bad) direction

Prices just keep rising.
In a town with poor transport, young people just keep leaving.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋ばかりだ／verb (dictionary form)＋一方だ
【Point】Used with verbs of change (increase, get worse). '~bakari da' is mostly for bad changes. Not used for deliberate actions.
文法 Lesson 1|9: About to happen any moment; right before a change

The long meeting is finally about to end.
The sun is about to set behind the mountains.

【Connection】verb (volitional form)＋としている
【Point】Also used as '~you to shite iru tokoro da'. Often used right before big changes such as seasons, eras or events.
文法 Lesson 1|10:
In this country, the number of elderly people is gradually increasing.
The economy is gradually recovering.

【Connection】verb (masu-stem)＋つつある
【Point】Used with verbs of change (increase, change, spread). A formal expression found in news and writing.
文法 Lesson 2|1:
I drank coffee while looking out the window.
Although I knew it was wrong, I ended up telling a lie.

【Connection】verb (masu-stem)＋つつ
【Point】Used when the same person does two actions at once. '~tsutsu mo' means 'although'. Common in formal writing.
文法 Lesson 2|2: Only after doing X do I realize or understand

Only after becoming a parent did I understand my mother's hardships.
Only after living abroad did I notice Japan's good points.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋はじめて
【Point】The main clause is a realization or a change in feeling (understand, notice, become able). It cannot be an intention, request or command.
文法 Lesson 2|3: After doing X; Y comes once X is properly done

I will apply after reading the materials carefully.
We decided on the hiring after careful consideration.

【Connection】verb (ta-form)＋上で／noun＋の＋上で
【Point】Describes an action after an important step such as a contract, consultation or check. The main clause can be an intention or request. A noun takes the form 'N no ue de'.
文法 Lesson 2|4: As soon as X is finished, do Y

I'll contact you as soon as I arrive at the airport.
It will be usable as soon as the construction is completed.

【Connection】verb (masu-stem)＋次第／noun＋次第
【Point】The main clause is the speaker's intention, request or plan. It cannot be used for past events. Different from 'N shidai da' (depends on N).
文法 Lesson 2|5: From a certain time until now, it has continued

Since I started studying abroad, I have written a diary every day.
I haven't met my teacher since graduating from university.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋以来／このかた／noun＋以来
【Point】The main clause is something that has continued until now. Not used for one-time actions. '~te kono kata' is slightly old and formal.
文法 Lesson 2|6: Unless you do X first, you cannot do Y

I can't reply until I check with my boss.
I can't serve the food to others until I taste it.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋からでないと／からでなければ
【Point】The main clause is negative (cannot, impossible). Used when the order of actions matters.
文法 Lesson 2|7: Starting with X (a representative example), and many others of the same kind.

Many citizens, starting with the mayor, took part in the ceremony.
All the executives, including the president, toured the new factory.

【Connection】Noun＋をはじめ(として)／Noun＋をはじめとする＋Noun
【Point】Usually followed by も or など; it implies there are others of the same kind. To modify a noun, use をはじめとする＋noun.
文法 Lesson 2|8: Judging even from one small point (the first thing you notice), the whole is clearly so.

That shop looks upscale from the entrance alone, so it is hard to go in.
I couldn't believe his story, starting from the very first word.

【Connection】Noun＋からして
【Point】Means "since even the first point is like this, the rest naturally is too." Often used for negative judgments, followed by a judgment.
文法 Lesson 2|9: Over a wide range of time, space or number of times (throughout).

Because of the typhoon, heavy rain continued over three days.
He announced the results of ten years of research.

【Connection】Noun (period/range)＋にわたって／Noun＋にわたる＋Noun
【Point】Used for a large range. Also takes the forms にわたる＋noun and にわたり. Not suited to short times or small ranges.
文法 Lesson 2|10: (1) Throughout a period. (2) Via or through a person or medium.

The temperature in this area hardly changes throughout the year.
I learned about my current company through a senior from university.

【Connection】Noun＋を通じて・を通して
【Point】In the "period" sense it follows words like a year or summer; in the "via" sense it follows a person, thing or experience. を通して is the same.
文法 Lesson 3|1: To the very limit of ability or range (as much as possible; as far as the eye can see).

If you have any trouble, I will help as much as I can.
The players fought with all their strength.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form)＋限り／Noun＋の＋限り
【Point】Mostly fixed phrases such as できる限り, 見渡す限り, 力の限り. It conveys going all the way to the limit.
文法 Lesson 3|2: As much as one can, wants or likes; up to the full amount.

You may eat as much as you like.
Before the meeting, I looked into it as much as I could.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form)＋だけ／Verb (tai-form)＋だけ／Verb (potential form)＋だけ／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋だけ／na-adjective (stem)＋な＋だけ
【Point】Often repeats the same verb (食べたいだけ食べる). Common in sentences of permission or offering.
文法 Lesson 3|3: Only for a specific person, time or case (as a special exception).

A souvenir will be given to the first ten customers only.
Only today, all items are sold at 20 percent off.

【Connection】Noun＋に限り
【Point】What follows is a special favor such as a discount, permission or service. It is not used for unlucky coincidences.
文法 Lesson 3|4: As long as a state continues; 〜ない限り means "unless" / "as long as ... not".

As long as I am healthy, I will protect my family.
As long as it does not rain, the game will be held.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form)・Verb (nai-form)＋限り(は)／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋限り(は)／na-adjective (stem)＋である＋限り(は)／Noun＋である＋限り(は)
【Point】What follows is an unchanging fact, resolve, promise or advice. 〜ない限り is close to "unless ... not".
文法 Lesson 3|5: As far as I know, saw or checked (within the range of one's information).

As far as I know, this town has only three hospitals.
As far as I checked, no problem was found in the documents.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form)・Verb (ta-form)・Verb (te-iru form)＋限りでは
【Point】Preceded by verbs of information such as know, see, hear, check. A judgment or guess follows.
文法 Lesson 3|6: (1) Of all times, something bad happens just then. (2) "That person, at least, would never..." (trust).

The train is delayed on exactly the days when I am in a hurry.
My child, of all people, would never do such a thing.

【Connection】Noun＋に限って
【Point】(1) After a day or time, followed by an unlucky coincidence. (2) After a person, as in うちの子に限って, followed by a negative.
文法 Lesson 3|7: Not only X, but also others (it applies more widely).

This anime is popular not only with children but also with adults.
This shop is crowded not only on weekends but also on weekdays.

【Connection】Noun＋に限らず
【Point】Followed by も, showing the range is wider. Usable in both speech and writing.
文法 Lesson 3|8: A formal way of saying "not only ... but also"; used in writing, news and reports.

This problem is attracting attention not only in Japan but also overseas.
He is not only excellent but also has a wonderful personality.

【Connection】Noun＋のみならず／Verb (plain form)・i-adjective (plain form)＋のみならず／na-adjective (stem)＋である＋のみならず
【Point】Followed by も or まで. Rarely used in conversation. Can follow nouns, verbs and adjectives.
文法 Lesson 3|9: Not only ..., but even (a further, stronger thing).

Not only did he forget the promise, he did not even apologize.
This town is not only inconvenient for transport, it also has few shops.

【Connection】Verb (plain form)・i-adjective (plain form)＋ばかりか／na-adjective (stem)＋な（である）＋ばかりか／Noun＋ばかりか
【Point】Followed by も, まで or さえ. Commands, requests and statements of intention cannot follow.
文法 Lesson 3|10: Needless to say A, and B too.

This town has many tourists in winter as well, not to mention summer.
He can speak Chinese as well, not to mention English.

【Connection】Noun＋はもとより
【Point】Follows nouns only. も follows, giving a surprising example or wider range. Common in writing.
文法 Lesson 4|1: In addition to ...; adds another point in the same direction (good+good or bad+bad).

This restaurant is not only cheap, the food is also delicious.
This room is quiet, and on top of that, close to the station.

【Connection】Verb (plain form)・i-adjective (plain form)＋上(に)／na-adjective (stem)＋な＋上(に)／Noun＋の＋上(に)
【Point】Both parts are good things or both are bad. Note the forms noun＋の上に and な-adjective＋な上に.
文法 Lesson 4|2: about, concerning; marks a topic or theme

Citizens asked questions about the new system.
I read materials on environmental problems and wrote a report.

【Connection】noun＋に関して／noun＋に関する＋noun
【Point】Marks a topic or theme; slightly more formal than について. Before a noun, use に関する+noun. No special restriction on the sentence ending.
文法 Lesson 4|3: over, surrounding an issue; debate or conflict arises

Residents' opinions are divided over the redevelopment in front of the station.
The siblings' quarrel over money ended up in court.

【Connection】noun＋をめぐって／noun＋をめぐる＋noun
【Point】Used for an issue that causes debate, conflict or competition; not for neutral topics. Before a noun, use をめぐる+noun.
文法 Lesson 4|4: when it comes to an ability or skill, second to none

When it comes to speed of calculation, she is the best in the class.
When it comes to cooking, my father doesn't lose even to the restaurant's cooks.

【Connection】noun＋にかけては
【Point】Used to praise ability, skill or knowledge in a field. The clause that follows is a positive evaluation, never a negative one.
文法 Lesson 4|5: toward a person or thing; also contrasts two things ('whereas')

You must not speak rudely to customers.
My older brother is sociable, whereas my younger brother likes being alone.

【Connection】noun＋に対して／noun＋に対する＋noun／plain form (na-adjective/noun + な)＋のに対して
【Point】Used for an attitude or action directed at a person or thing (に対する before a noun). 〜のに対して contrasts two things.
文法 Lesson 4|6: in response to someone's expectation or request

Responding to the fans' calls, the singer sang one more song.
In response to parents' requests, the school made the lunch break longer.

【Connection】noun＋にこたえて／noun＋にこたえる＋noun
【Point】Acting to meet someone's expectation, request or voice. The preceding noun expresses what others want (期待, 要望, 声, ...).
文法 Lesson 4|7: using facts or materials as a starting point to create something new

I wrote a novel based on my grandmother's experience.
I estimated next month's sales based on the figures in the materials.

【Connection】noun＋をもとに(して)／noun＋をもとにした＋noun
【Point】Used when taking facts, experiences or survey results as raw material to make or devise something new. The form をもとにした+noun is also common.
文法 Lesson 4|8: based on rules, facts or data as grounds for judgment or action

The company pays its employees in accordance with the law.
Measures were decided based on the survey results.

【Connection】noun＋に基づいて／noun＋に基づく＋noun
【Point】Used when judgment, action or reports rest on rules, facts or data as their basis. Before a noun: に基づく / に基づいた + noun.
文法 Lesson 4|9: along a line, or following a policy, plan or manual without deviating

A narrow road continues along the sea.
I assembled the machine following the instruction sheet.

【Connection】noun＋に沿って／noun＋に沿った＋noun
【Point】Along a line such as a road or river; or acting without deviating from a policy, plan or manual. Before a noun: に沿った + noun.
文法 Lesson 4|10: under the guidance, influence or condition of something

I want to study Japanese under an excellent teacher.
Under the president's instructions, everyone worked for the new plan.

【Connection】noun＋のもとで／noun＋のもとに
【Point】Doing something within the sphere of a leader, influence or condition. Often follows a person (teacher, president) or a condition. のもとに is used in a similar way.
文法 Lesson 5|1: made or prepared for a particular group of people

This magazine is aimed at women in their twenties.
Since it's a program for children, the language is easy.

【Connection】noun＋向けだ／noun＋向けの＋noun／noun＋向けに＋verb
【Point】Says that a product, program or book was made for a specific group. Different from 向きだ (naturally suited to). 向けの+noun and 向けに+verb are also used.
文法 Lesson 5|2: as one thing gradually changes, another changes with it

As the night deepened, the wind grew stronger.
As one gets older, physical strength declines.

【Connection】verb dictionary form＋につれて／にしたがって／noun＋につれて／にしたがって
【Point】For gradual, continuing changes; both clauses express change. Not suited to sudden changes or one-time events.
文法 Lesson 5|3: another change occurs together with a change; とともに can also mean 'together with'

Along with the population increase, the housing problem grew.
With the arrival of spring, the cherry blossoms in the park began to bloom.

【Connection】noun＋に伴って／とともに／verb dictionary form＋に伴って／とともに／noun＋に伴う＋noun
【Point】A change occurring together with another change; に伴う+noun also exists. とともに can also mean 'together with a person' or 'at the same time'.
文法 Lesson 5|4: that is the situation (closes an explanation); noun + 次第だ means "depends on the noun"

I am writing this letter because I would like to hear everyone's opinions.
Whether we can win the match depends on the amount of practice.

【Connection】verb dictionary form＋次第だ／verb ta-form＋次第だ／verb te-iru form＋次第だ／noun＋次第だ
【Point】In polite writing or speech, closes an explanation of the circumstances (〜た次第です). Noun + 次第だ is a different use meaning 'depends on that noun'.
文法 Lesson 5|5: adjusting the response according to the situation or person

The amount of tax changes according to income.
You can choose the room size according to the number of guests.

【Connection】noun＋に応じて／noun＋に応じた＋noun
【Point】When a situation, state or person changes, the response changes accordingly. Before a noun: に応じた + noun.
文法 Lesson 5|6: whenever one sees, hears or thinks of something, the same feeling arises

Whenever I see this photo, I remember my old friends.
Whenever I see young people doing well, I think I should try hard too.

【Connection】verb dictionary form＋につけ（て）／i-adjective dictionary form＋につけ（〜につけ〜につけ）
【Point】Attaches to verbs such as 見る/聞く/考える: whenever that happens, the same feeling arises. The following clause expresses thoughts or feelings (remember, worry, ...).
文法 Lesson 5|7: this and that: many things piling up

Before moving, I was busy sorting my belongings and doing paperwork.
Passing the exam, I was happy and relieved at once, and tears came.

【Connection】Noun + やら + Noun + やら / Verb dictionary form + やら + Verb dictionary form + やら / i-adjective dictionary form + やら + i-adjective dictionary form + やら
【Point】Used when many things pile up, such as busyness, trouble or mixed feelings, often as 〜やら〜やらで. It feels more troublesome than 〜とか〜とか.
文法 Lesson 5|8: or rather… (listing ways to put it)

His opinion is distinctive, or let's say unique; you can't forget it.
The room was spacious, or rather empty; it was a house with nothing in it.

【Connection】Plain form + というか + plain form + というか / Noun, na-adjective stem + というか
【Point】Used when you can't find the exact word, listing several ways to put it. Mostly spoken; it can also be used once to rephrase, as in 〜というか〜.
文法 Lesson 5|9: whether A or B / even if A

Whether you agree or disagree, please state your reason clearly.
Even if you are busy, you should at least reply.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form, i-adjective dictionary form, noun (+ である) + にしても / にしろ / にせよ
【Point】In the pair 〜にしても〜にしても it means 'whichever the case'; used once it means 'even if'. The speaker's opinion or judgment follows. にしろ and にせよ are slightly more formal.
文法 Lesson 5|10:
Many foreigners live in big cities such as Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya.
He doesn't seem to have any hobby worth mentioning.

【Connection】Noun (, Noun) + といった + Noun
【Point】Gives examples and means 'such as'. Similar to など, but a noun follows. Forms like これといった〜はない mean 'nothing in particular'.
文法 Lesson 6|1:
This company hires motivated people regardless of educational background.
There is a line at that shop every day, regardless of the season.

【Connection】Noun (gender, age, day/night, season, presence/absence, etc.) + を問わず
【Point】Means 'regardless of'. It attaches to nouns with opposite meanings or that show a range of types, and is often followed by expressions like 'anyone' or 'anytime'.
文法 Lesson 6|2:
The same salary is paid regardless of nationality.
Whether you like it or not, you have to study every day.

【Connection】Noun + にかかわらず (にかかわりなく) / Verb dictionary form + verb nai form + にかかわらず / Plain form + かどうか + にかかわらず
【Point】Means 'unaffected by …, the same either way'. Close to 〜を問わず, but it is also often used with opposite pairs such as 行く行かない. The speaker's judgment or a rule follows.
文法 Lesson 6|3:
He was talking loudly on the phone, not caring who was around.
She calls her friends in the middle of the night without regard for the time.

【Connection】Noun + もかまわず / Verb dictionary form + のもかまわず
【Point】Does something without caring about what one would normally care about. An actual action follows; the speaker's volition or a command does not usually come after it.
文法 Lesson 6|4:
Price aside, the service at this shop is the best.
Whether I go or not aside, let's at least check the schedule.

【Connection】Noun + はともかく(として) / Plain form + かどうか + はともかく / Noun + ならともかく
【Point】Sets X aside and speaks of something more important. 〜ならともかく means 'it would be understandable if it were X, but (otherwise it is a problem)'.
文法 Lesson 6|5:
Greetings aside, let's get right to the main topic.
Whether we can win or not aside, I intend to fight with all my strength.

【Connection】Noun + はさておき / Plain form + かどうか + はさておき
【Point】Means 'leaving X aside for now' and moves on to another matter first. Close to 〜はともかく, but it feels more like moving the conversation forward.
文法 Lesson 6|6:
There's no way he would say something so terrible. He's a kind person.
There's no way you'll get good without practicing even once.

【Connection】Plain form (na-adjective: 〜な, noun: 〜の or 〜な) + わけがない (わけはない)
【Point】Strongly denies something for a reason: 'there is absolutely no way'. Close to 〜はずがない; in speech 〜わけない is also used.
文法 Lesson 6|7: no time for X / far from X

There was a big earthquake, so sleeping was out of the question.
Far from apologizing, he got angry and went home.

【Connection】Noun / Verb dictionary form + どころではない / Noun, plain form + どころか
【Point】〜どころではない means 'far too busy or troubled to do it'. 〜どころか means 'far from X; in fact the opposite (or even more) is true', stating something contrary to expectation.
文法 Lesson 6|8:
I won't lose to the likes of him!
He's no genius. He's just a hard worker.

【Connection】Plain form (na-adjective: 〜な, noun: 〜な) + ものか (もんか in speech)
【Point】Expresses strong denial. Mainly spoken, with anger or defiance, often as 誰が〜ものか. Not suited to polite or formal writing.
文法 Lesson 6|9:
It's not that I think Japanese is difficult, but I'm weak at kanji.
It is not the case that all international students are rich.

【Connection】Plain form (na-adjective: 〜な, noun: 〜な) + わけではない / Noun, plain form + というわけではない
【Point】Does not deny everything, only part of it: 'not necessarily'. It is often followed by が or けど and the real situation.
文法 Lesson 6|10:
It's not the case that the more expensive the medicine, the better it works.
It's not enough just to work long hours. The quality of work matters too.

【Connection】Plain form (noun and na-adjective take だ) + というものではない / というものでもない
【Point】Used against a commonly held idea: 'that is not necessarily so'. A slightly formal way of stating an opinion.
文法 Lesson 7|1: Explains the meaning of a word; also expresses surprise at something unexpected

"Chikoku" means not being on time for the set time.
I never thought that quiet person would shout in anger.

【Connection】Noun＋とは／Plain form＋とは
【Point】In "A to wa B no koto da", it explains what A means. In the surprise use, the speaker's feeling follows.
文法 Lesson 7|2: Mentions something associated with the topic word, or a related topic

Speaking of Kyoto, many people think of temples.
Speaking of trips, I am going to Hokkaido with a friend next month.

【Connection】Noun＋といえば／Plain form＋といえば
【Point】In "A to ieba B", B is what comes to mind from A. It is also used to shift the topic.
文法 Lesson 7|3: Checks what a word means; "to ittara" stresses an extreme degree

The tastiness of this ramen is beyond words.
By "the new teacher", do you mean the tall person?

【Connection】Noun＋というと／といえば／といったら／Plain form＋というと
【Point】"A to iu to" is used to check what A is. "A to ittara ... nai" shows strong feeling, and is often followed by "nai/nakatta" or "hodo da".
文法 Lesson 7|4: When it comes to that matter, one's manner or reaction differs from usual

When it comes to soccer, he keeps talking until late at night.
When money comes up, everyone gets a serious look.

【Connection】Noun＋となると／Noun＋のこととなると／Plain form＋となると
【Point】It says that one acts differently from usual when A comes up. "No koto" is often added for people or events. A description or judgment follows.
文法 Lesson 7|5: Despite ~; the result is not what one would expect (formal)

Despite the rain, a large crowd gathered.
Even though he was busy, he helped us.

【Connection】Noun＋にもかかわらず／Verb (dictionary form)＋にもかかわらず／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋にもかかわらず／na-adjective (stem)＋な／である＋にもかかわらず
【Point】The content before and after is opposite. It is used in news, letters and greetings. The speaker's wish or an order rarely follows.
文法 Lesson 7|6: Although ~; in reality it does not turn out as expected or as said

I took medicine, but my fever did not go down.
I like English, but speaking it is hard for me.

【Connection】Verb (ta-form)＋ものの／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋ものの／na-adjective (stem)＋な＋ものの／Noun＋である＋ものの／Plain form＋とはいうものの
【Point】It admits the first part and then says "but it is not enough". A fact or the speaker's feeling follows. "To wa iu mono no" can also begin a sentence.
文法 Lesson 7|7: While doing ~ (at the same time); "nagara mo" means "although"

He is talking on the phone while walking.
Small though it is, it is our happy home.

【Connection】Verb (masu-stem)＋ながら(も)／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋ながら(も)／na-adjective (stem)＋ながら(も)／Noun＋ながら(も)
【Point】Verb masu-stem + nagara means one person does two things at once. "Nagara (mo)" also attaches to adjectives and nouns and means "although".
文法 Lesson 7|8: Although doing ~ (contrary result); "tsutsu aru" means a change is progressing

Although I thought I should go to bed early, I ended up looking at my phone until midnight.
The town is gradually becoming quiet.

【Connection】Verb (masu-stem)＋つつ(も)
【Point】It attaches only to the verb masu-stem and is formal. "Tsutsu mo" is contrary; "tsutsu aru" says a change is gradually progressing.
文法 Lesson 7|9: Although one says so, in reality it is not that much

I can cook, but only things like rolled omelets.
It is a city, but away from the station it is quiet.

【Connection】Plain form＋といっても／Noun＋（だ）＋といっても／na-adjective (stem)＋（だ）＋といっても
【Point】Used to say that reality differs from the degree the first words suggest. The second part explains that the degree is low.
文法 Lesson 7|10: Just because ~, it is not always the case

Just because someone is Japanese does not mean they can read all kanji.
Just because something is cheap, you should not buy just anything.

【Connection】Plain form＋からといって／Noun＋（だ）＋からといって
【Point】A negative follows, such as "to wa kagiranai", "wake dewa nai" or "te wa ikenai". It says a reason alone does not naturally lead to the conclusion.
文法 Lesson 8|1: If we suppose ~, a thought or judgment is stated on that premise

If a thousand students are coming, the venue should be bigger.
If he is the culprit, what could the motive be?

【Connection】Plain form＋としたら／とすれば／とすると／Noun＋（だ）＋としたら／Noun＋となったら／となれば／となると
【Point】Regardless of whether it is true, it supposes something and states a thought. Judgment, guess or suggestion usually follows; plain facts rarely do. "To naru to" is also used when a situation changes.
文法 Lesson 8|2: If it were possible to ~ (in reality it is hard); a wish or desire to try

If I could meet him once more, I would like to thank him.
If I could win, I would love to try.

【Connection】Verb (potential / dictionary form)＋ものなら
【Point】It supposes something hard to realize and states a wish such as "~tai" or "~te mitai" afterward. The first part is a potential or dictionary form.
文法 Lesson 8|3: If one were to ~, a bad result would follow right away

If I were to break Grandfather's precious bowl, there would be serious trouble.
If you tried to lie, you would be seen through at once.

【Connection】Verb (volitional form)＋ものなら
【Point】A bad result or serious trouble follows. It supposes something one would not want to do.
文法 Lesson 8|4: Unless ~ happens, the next thing cannot be done or known

Unless I actually see it, I cannot tell what kind of thing it is.
Unless you are healthy, you cannot even keep working.

【Connection】Verb (nai-form)＋ことには／Noun＋でない＋ことには
【Point】Unless the first thing happens, the second cannot hold. A negative or minus content such as "cannot/do not know" follows.
文法 Lesson 8|5: Without ~, something cannot be discussed or done

This movie cannot be discussed without its music.
Without my family's cooperation, there would have been no success.

【Connection】Noun＋を抜きにしては／Noun＋を抜きにして
【Point】It strongly says that something cannot be considered with an important thing left out. A negative such as "cannot be discussed/imagined/hold" follows.
文法 Lesson 8|6: Even if ~, the later judgment does not change; "A ni seyo B ni seyo" means either way

Even if you fail, it will be good experience.
Whether by train or bus, it takes an hour.

【Connection】Plain form＋としても／にしても／にしろ／にせよ／Noun＋（だ・である）＋としても／na-adjective (stem)＋（だ・である）＋にしても
【Point】Even granting the first part, the later judgment stays the same, often the speaker's opinion. "A ni shiro B ni shiro / A ni seyo B ni seyo" means "in either case".
文法 Lesson 8|7: Shows cause, means, the doer in a passive, or variation by case

Customs differ depending on the country.
The river overflowed because of the heavy rain.

【Connection】Noun + によって
【Point】'X によって differ/change' means the result varies from case to case. In a passive sentence it marks the doer. It can also give a cause; the main clause then states a fact.
文法 Lesson 8|8: Gives the reason for an unintended result; often an excuse

I was in a hurry, so I left something behind.
He is so kind that I ended up asking him for help.

【Connection】Verb / i-adjective plain form + ものだから／ものですから／もので／もの
　　　　Na-adjective stem + な / Noun + な + ものだから
【Point】Used to explain a reason or make an excuse. ものですから is polite; sentence-final 〜んだもの is for close friends. A command or request cannot follow.
文法 Lesson 8|9: おかげ: cause of a good result (thanks to). せい: cause of a bad result (because of)

Thanks to my friend helping me, I finished early.
I can't concentrate on work because of lack of sleep.

【Connection】Verb / i-adjective plain form + おかげだ／せいだ
　　　　Na-adjective stem + な / Noun + の + おかげだ／せいだ
【Point】おかげ carries gratitude and goes with a good result. せい carries blame or complaint and goes with a bad result. The forms 〜のおかげで／〜のせいで can link to the next clause.
文法 Lesson 8|10: A feeling or state is so strong that an unusual result follows

In her sadness, she couldn't speak.
I was so busy that I had no time even to eat.

【Connection】Noun + の + あまり (i-adjective: stem + さ + の + あまり) / Verb dictionary or た form + あまり
　　　　あまりの + Noun + に
【Point】A feeling or state is so strong that an extreme action or result follows. The main clause reports what actually happened; a wish or command cannot follow. あまりの〜に expresses surprise at the degree of a noun.
文法 Lesson 9|1: Gives a reason in notices; also means 'per ~'

Because the seats are full, we must decline admission.
Parking costs 300 yen per hour.

【Connection】Noun + につき
【Point】Used on signs and notices to give a reason politely (e.g. 工事中につき). After a noun of quantity it means 'per ~' (e.g. 1人につき). Rarely used in speech.
文法 Lesson 9|2: Mentions a reason lightly, leading to a proposal or decision

It's Sunday, so let's sleep in.
Now that the children have grown, I'm thinking of buying a new house.

【Connection】Verb / i-adjective plain form + ことだし
　　　　Na-adjective stem + な / Noun + の／である + ことだし
【Point】Like 〜し, it lightly mentions one reason among others. The main clause usually has the speaker's intention, proposal or judgment (〜しよう, 〜ませんか).
文法 Lesson 9|3: Knowing the person's character, I judge that surely ~

Since Yamaguchi is careful, he must have checked it many times.
My sister loves food, so she surely knows a good restaurant.

【Connection】Noun for a person + のことだから
【Point】Because you know the person's character or habits well, you guess or judge 'surely ~'. The main clause is a conjecture or expectation. It can also be used for companies or towns whose nature you know.
文法 Lesson 9|4: Precisely because ~, all the more / as befits ~

Having lived in Japan for a long time, he knows Japanese honorifics well too.
Being a pro athlete, his running form is beautiful.

【Connection】Verb / i-adjective plain form + だけに
　　　　Na-adjective stem + な / Noun (+ である) + だけに
【Point】Because of an expectation, experience or position, the result is stronger or only natural. It is used for both good and bad results; the main clause often means 'all the more' or 'as expected'.
文法 Lesson 9|5: Just because of ~, a bad result occurred (regret)

Just because I spoke honestly, I ended up hurting my friend.
Just because I'm slow, I wasn't chosen as a representative.

【Connection】Verb / i-adjective plain form + ばかりに
　　　　Na-adjective stem + な / Noun + である + ばかりに
【Point】Expresses regret: 'just because of that one thing, a bad result occurred'. A bad result follows; it is never used for a good result. The first part is often a small cause.
文法 Lesson 9|6: Since ~ has been decided or done, naturally one will / must ~

Since I'm going to play, I want to win.
Now that I'm a working adult, I must take responsibility for my actions.

【Connection】Verb plain form + からには／以上(は)／上は
【Point】Because of an irreversible fact (you decided, promised or took on something), states responsibility, resolve or the natural conclusion. The main clause is like 〜なければならない, 〜つもりだ or 〜べきだ; a mere statement of fact cannot follow. 上は is read うえは.
文法 Lesson 9|7: Very hard to ~ (emotionally or by nature); almost impossible

Memories of childhood are hard to forget.
Unfortunately, it is hard to adopt his proposal.

【Connection】Verb ます-stem + がたい
【Point】Mostly with verbs of thinking and feeling such as 信じる, 理解する, 受け入れる, 忘れる. It is a formal expression (信じがたい, 忘れがたい, 許しがたい). It is not used for physical actions such as 食べる or 行く.
文法 Lesson 9|8: Cannot ~ because of circumstances, duty or social norms

I can't refuse a request from someone important to me.
My boss invited me, so I can't help going to the drinking party.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + わけにはいかない／わけにもいかない
　　　　Verb ない-form + わけにはいかない (= must do)
【Point】'Cannot do it because of a social or moral reason', not because of lack of ability. 〜ないわけにはいかない means 'must do it by all means'. わけにもいかない adds 'and also'.
文法 Lesson 9|9:
I'm sorry, but I'm unable to answer about personal information.
I can't decide by myself.

【Connection】Verb ます-stem + かねる
【Point】A polite, soft way to say 'I can't', common in business and shops (判断しかねる, 賛成しかねる, お答えしかねます). The form is affirmative but the meaning is negative. Do not confuse it with 〜かねない ('might well happen', usually something bad).
文法 Lesson 9|10:
I don't know the name or address, so there's no way to look for him.
It's too old; there's no way to repair it.

【Connection】Verb ます-stem + ようがない
　　　　Noun + の + しようがない
【Point】'There is no means, so it cannot be done.' Different from 〜わけにはいかない, which is about circumstances or duty. 〜ようもない is also used (連絡しようがない, 直しようがない).
文法 Lesson 10|1: It is possible / not possible that ~

It can happen to anyone, so let's be careful.
I can't imagine him telling a lie.

【Connection】Verb ます-stem + 得る／得ない
【Point】得る (read うる or える) means 'it is possible to ~'; the negative 得ない (えない) means 'it is impossible to ~'. Mostly formal set phrases: あり得る, 考え得る, 起こり得る. Not used with ordinary will-based actions such as 食べ得る.
文法 Lesson 10|2: The result is different from what you would expect from the first part.

He looks young for his age.
This restaurant is tasty considering how cheap it is.

【Connection】Noun＋の＋わりに / Verb or i-adjective (plain form)＋わりに / Na-adjective (stem)＋な＋わりに
【Point】Used when the result is better or worse than conditions such as effort or price would lead you to expect. An evaluation follows; the speaker's will or commands do not.
文法 Lesson 10|3: Considering a certain standard or status, the state or result is not what you would expect.

He speaks Japanese well for a foreigner.
It turned out well for something made for the first time.

【Connection】Noun＋にしては / Verb (plain form)＋にしては
【Point】Takes a status or fact such as 'foreigner' or 'first time' as the standard and says that the result is not what you expected. An evaluation follows; it can be positive or negative.
文法 Lesson 10|4: You admire that something is, as expected, excellent and worthy of the position or experience.

Having studied abroad for ten years, she is (as you would expect) good at English.
It is a famous shop for good reason. The taste is excellent.

【Connection】Noun / Verb (plain form) / i-adjective＋だけ(のことは)ある / Na-adjective (stem)＋な＋だけ(のことは)ある
【Point】Often used with 'sasuga'. Used only to admire a good result that fits the preceding fact; it cannot be used for bad evaluations. It is also used in the form '〜だけあって'.
文法 Lesson 10|5: Shows a standpoint, qualification or role: 'in the capacity of ...'.

I came to Japan as an international student.
I feel my responsibility as a teacher.

【Connection】Noun＋として (to modify a noun: Noun＋としての＋Noun)
【Point】'〜として' shows a role or qualification, while '〜にとって' shows a person's view or evaluation. An action or state follows.
文法 Lesson 10|6: States an evaluation or judgment from the standpoint of that person or organization.

For me, family is the most important thing.
For children, play is as important as study.

【Connection】Noun (person or organization)＋にとって (は / も / の)
【Point】An evaluation or judgment such as 'important' or 'difficult' follows. '〜として' is about a role, while '〜にとって' is about the standpoint of thoughts and feelings.
文法 Lesson 10|7: Putting yourself in that person's position, it says how they would feel.

From a parent's point of view, a child is always a child.
From his side, he probably meant it as a joke.

【Connection】Noun (person)＋にしたら / にすれば / にしてみれば / にしても
【Point】Attaches to a noun for a person and then says that person's feelings or thoughts. Compared with '〜にとって', it suits imagining their feelings. A sentence of pure fact rarely follows.
文法 Lesson 10|8: When you tried something, a finding or result came out afterwards.

When I asked the teacher, I found out that next week is a day off.
When I went to the library, it turned out to be closed today.

【Connection】Verb ta-form＋ところ
【Point】An unexpected discovery or result (past) follows. The speaker's will or commands do not follow. It differs from '〜たところだ' (just did).
文法 Lesson 10|9: After doing something, there is no change and nothing else happens afterwards.

He left home and has not come back.
Since she collapsed last year, my grandmother has been bedridden.

【Connection】Verb ta-form＋きり (noun form: 寝たきり)
【Point】A negative sentence or a sentence in which the same state continues follows. As in 'went and never came back', it often expresses worry or regret.
文法 Lesson 10|10: After a long time, much trouble or hesitation, things ended in a bad result.

After hesitating for a long time, I bought nothing.
After two hours of argument, the meeting was cancelled.

【Connection】Verb ta-form＋あげく / Noun＋の＋あげく
【Point】Words expressing time or hardship, such as 'worrying for a long time' or 'discussing many times', come before it. What follows is mostly a regrettable result, in a past sentence.
文法 Lesson 11|1: After thinking or making an effort for a long time, a conclusion or result finally came out.

After agonizing, I decided to study abroad.
After three years of effort, he made his dream come true.

【Connection】Verb ta-form＋末(に) / Noun＋の＋末(に)
【Point】The result can be positive or negative. A word for a long process, such as 'worry' or 'discussion', comes before it, and a decision or result follows.
文法 Lesson 11|2: Something bad was about to happen, but in fact it did not.

I was almost run over by a car.
I almost went home leaving my important documents behind.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form or nai-form＋ところだった
【Point】Often used with 'ayauku' or 'mō sukoshi de'. Used when something bad nearly happened; it shows that it did not actually happen.
文法 Lesson 11|3: Something you meant to do ended up never being done.

I was busy and never got to meet my friend.
I graduated without ever apologizing to him.

【Connection】Verb nai-form (〜ない→〜ず)＋じまい (する→せずじまい)
【Point】The sentence ends in the form '〜ずじまいだ / だった / になった'. It expresses regret that you meant to do it but could not.
文法 Lesson 11|4: Shows a degree by using an example. It can also belittle something as no big deal.

I was so happy that I almost cried.
At least say hello on your own initiative.

【Connection】Noun＋ぐらい / Verb dictionary form or nai-form＋ぐらい / i-adjective＋ぐらい / Na-adjective (stem)＋な＋ぐらい
【Point】A degree is described by a concrete example, as in 'so happy I want to cry'. It can also mean belittling, as in 'at least greet people yourself'.
文法 Lesson 11|5: Gives an example, belittles something, or expresses surprise that it is unexpected.

Someone like me could never become president.
I never thought the results would come so quickly.

【Connection】Noun＋など / なんか / なんて; Verb or sentence (plain form)＋なんて
【Point】'Nanka' and 'nante' are spoken. '〜なんて〜ない' expresses strong denial or surprise. 'Watashi nanka' is a way of putting oneself down.
文法 Lesson 11|6: Doing something extreme that people would not normally do.

There is no need to go into debt to buy designer clothes.
Did he want money so badly that he would even deceive his friends?

【Connection】Noun＋まで / Noun＋までして / Verb te-form＋まで
【Point】An extreme action comes before it. What follows tends to be a negative evaluation such as 'there is no need to...' or 'I don't want to...'.
文法 Lesson 11|7: Not even one (person, time, etc.). There is absolutely no exception.

In the class, not a single person agreed with his opinion.
She has never broken a promise even once.

【Connection】One＋counter (一つ, 一人, 一度, 一日, etc.)＋として＋negative / Question word＋one＋counter＋として＋negative
【Point】A negative sentence always follows. It strongly denies everything, and is often used in written or formal speech.
文法 Lesson 11|8: Gives an extreme example to say that the rest is the same. In '〜さえ〜ば', it says that one condition alone is enough.

I'm so busy that I don't even have time to eat.
Even an elementary school student can solve this problem.

【Connection】Noun＋さえ / Noun＋でさえ / Verb masu-stem＋さえ(し) / Verb te-form＋さえ
【Point】'Jikan sae nai' means that even something basic like time is lacking. 'Okane sae areba' means that money alone would be enough.
文法 Lesson 11|9: No matter how hard the thing you have to do, you want to achieve your goal.

If it is to see him, I will go even if I have to walk a long way.
I want to study abroad even if I have to borrow money.

【Connection】Verb te-form＋でも / Noun＋をしてでも
【Point】A sentence of strong determination, hope or request follows. '〜てまで' tends to be negative, while '〜てでも' expresses a strong wish to make it happen.
文法 Lesson 11|10: it seems / it looks as if (a guess from what one sees)

All the flowers in the garden have withered. It seems nobody watered them for a long time.
It must have been cold this morning; the water on the road is frozen.

【Connection】Plain form of verb / い-adjective / な-adjective / noun + とみえる / とみえて
【Point】A guess based on what the speaker sees. 〜とみえて links a guessed reason to the next clause. It is not used for the speaker's own feelings or will.
文法 Lesson 12|1:
If you drink that much, you could ruin your health.
That person might well forget an important appointment.

【Connection】Verb stem (ます-form without ます) + かねない
【Point】Says a bad result is quite possible. Not used for good results. Do not confuse it with 〜かねる (cannot do).
文法 Lesson 12|2: there is a risk that something bad will happen (news, writing)

Because of the heavy rain, the river may overflow.
There is a risk of a tsunami, so please do not go near the sea.

【Connection】Noun + の + おそれがある / Verb dictionary form・ない-form + おそれがある
【Point】Used in news and writing for a risk of something bad. Not used for good things. おそれ can also be written 恐れ.
文法 Lesson 12|3:
I will never go to that shop again.
Isn't this result a coincidence?

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + まい (ichidan verbs: ない-form + まい; する → すまい/しまい) / Noun・な-adjective + ではあるまいか / Plain form + のではあるまいか
【Point】まい expresses a negative will (I will not ~) or negative guess (probably not ~). ではあるまいか is a formal way of saying "isn't it ~?" to state one's opinion softly.
文法 Lesson 12|4: 'must be ~' — a strong conviction based on grounds

He is so late that he must have had an accident.
This painting is undoubtedly the work of a famous painter.

【Connection】Plain form of verb / い-adjective; な-adjective stem; noun + に違いない / に相違ない
【Point】Used when you strongly believe something is true for a reason. に相違ない is more formal. Not used for your own actions or for things you already know.
文法 Lesson 12|5: 'of course it's ~' — a strong, colloquial assertion

If you prepare nothing, you will fail for sure.
Hokkaido in winter is cold, obviously.

【Connection】Plain form of verb / い-adjective; な-adjective stem; noun + に決まっている
【Point】A colloquial, emphatic "of course it is so". It reflects the speaker's firm belief and is more casual than に違いない. Rarely used in formal writing or reports.
文法 Lesson 12|6: a general truth, deep feeling, or a fond memory (〜たものだ)

When people get older, they tend to remember the past.
When I was young, I often stayed up all night.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form・た-form / い-adjective / な-adjective (+な) + ものだ
【Point】Expresses a general truth, deep feeling, or (with 〜たものだ) a fond memory of something done often in the past.
文法 Lesson 12|7: 'that is exactly what ~ is' — states one's own judgment firmly

Not listening to other people's opinions is just being selfish.
Wanting only the result without effort is simply too convenient.

【Connection】Plain form (な-adjective・noun without だ) + というものだ
【Point】States the speaker's own judgment firmly: "that is exactly what ~ is". Different from ということだ (hearsay / restating).
文法 Lesson 12|8:
This is merely my personal opinion.
He only listened to his subordinates' opinions.

【Connection】Plain form of verb / い-adjective; な-adjective (な/である); noun (である) + にすぎない
【Point】Says "it is merely ~", treating something as small or unimportant. It shows the speaker's view that it is less than it may seem.
文法 Lesson 12|9: 'nothing other than ~' — firmly names the real reason or identity

This accident is nothing other than a mistake caused by forgetting to check.
He was able to win precisely because he practiced every day.

【Connection】Noun + にほかならない / Plain form + からにほかならない
【Point】Declares "it is nothing other than this". The form 〜からにほかならない, giving a reason, is very common. Suited to formal writing.
文法 Lesson 12|10: 'it is best to ~' — if possible, that is better

When traveling abroad, it is best to have insurance.
It is best to arrive a little early for an appointment.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form / い-adjective / な-adjective (である) / noun (である) + に越したことはない
【Point】Says "it is best to ~ if possible". The form 〜ないに越したことはない is also common. It suggests it is not required but safer or better.
文法 Lesson 13|1:
Now that we have come this far, we have no choice but to see it through.
The train stopped, so I had no choice but to walk home.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + しかない / よりほかない / ほかない
【Point】Used when there is no other way. しかない is common in speech; よりほかない and ほかない are more formal.
文法 Lesson 13|2:
Students should put study first.
You should not make other people's privacy public without permission.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + べきだ / べきではない (する can be すべき)
【Point】A strong way of saying "it is right to do so" (duty or reason). Because it is strong, it is used mostly for opinions and general statements, not directly to a person.
文法 Lesson 13|3:
Let us all join forces and protect this town.
Let us try to do our best until the end.

【Connection】Volitional form of verb + (よ)うではないか
【Point】A formal, earnest call to others, used in speeches and meetings. In ordinary conversation, 〜(よ)う is used instead.
文法 Lesson 13|4:
If you want to stay healthy, walk every day.
If you do not want to fail, do not overdo it.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form・ない-form + ことだ
【Point】Gives advice: "you should ~". Not used much to superiors. It is often preceded by a condition such as 〜たければ or 〜なら.
文法 Lesson 13|5: common sense: 'it is natural to ~' / 'one should ~'

When you meet someone for the first time, you should greet them politely.
One should not speak ill of others.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form・ない-form + ものだ / Verb dictionary form + ものではない
【Point】Says what is normal or proper by social common sense: "one does ~" / "one should not ~". Distinguish it from the feeling/memory ものだ of Lesson 23.
文法 Lesson 13|6:
Email is enough, so you do not need to come to the office in person.
There is no need to be so discouraged by one small mistake.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + ことはない
【Point】Says "there is no need to ~". Used to ease the listener's worry or reserve. The form そんなに〜ことはない is also common.
文法 Lesson 13|7: 'should I ~ or not?' — hesitating over a decision

I will never make such a mistake again.
I am thinking about whether or not to study abroad.

【Connection】Verb dictionary form + まい (ichidan: ない-form + まい; する → すまい/しまい) / Volitional form + か + dictionary form (ichidan: ない-form) + まいか
【Point】まい expresses a negative will (I will not ~). 〜(よ)うか〜まいか is used when hesitating over doing or not doing something.
文法 Lesson 13|8: a feeling or bodily sensation is so strong that one cannot bear it

When I think I will see my family for the first time in a long while, I am so happy I can hardly stand it.
When I think about tomorrow's match, I am so nervous I can't stand it.

【Connection】verb te-form＋しかたがない／しょうがない／たまらない / i-adjective (-kute form)＋しかたがない／しょうがない／たまらない / na-adjective (stem)＋で＋しかたがない／しょうがない／たまらない
【Point】Used for one's own feelings or physical sensations (happy, sleepy, worried, etc.). No commands or intentions follow. "たまらない" is often used for bodily sensations.
文法 Lesson 13|9: a feeling wells up naturally and cannot be suppressed

Lately I cannot help being reminded of my hometown.
I cannot help worrying about my child's future.

【Connection】verb te-form＋ならない（思われて／気がして／気になって など） / i-adjective (-kute form)＋ならない / na-adjective (stem)＋で＋ならない
【Point】Often used with feelings that arise naturally, such as 思われる, 気がする, 気になる. More literary than てしかたがない, and rarely used for sensations like sleepy or painful.
文法 Lesson 13|10: cannot help doing it, however much one tries to resist

I watched a moving movie and could not help crying.
When I see a friend in trouble, I cannot help but help.

【Connection】verb nai-form＋ないではいられない / verb nai-form without "ない"＋ずにはいられない（する→せずにはいられない）
【Point】Used when one's feelings are so strong that one acts naturally. する becomes せずには. For other people's actions, add expressions such as ようだ.
文法 Lesson 14|1: because of the circumstances, one must do it

If my boss asks me, I cannot refuse to take it on.
It is an important promise, so I cannot not go.

【Connection】verb nai-form＋ないわけにはいかない
【Point】Used when social position or circumstances make something obligatory. It is the negative of 〜わけにはいかない (cannot do), so be careful not to confuse the meanings.
文法 Lesson 14|2: there is no other choice but to do it

The rain is so bad that we have no choice but to postpone the trip.
If it is the company's order, we have no choice but to obey.

【Connection】verb nai-form without "ない"＋ざるを得ない（する→せざるを得ない）
【Point】Used when one does not really want to but has no other option. する becomes せざるを得ない. Used in writing and formal speech.
文法 Lesson 14|3:
I would love to try pizza in Italy, its home, at least once.
I wish young people would read more books.

【Connection】verb masu-stem (without "ます")＋たいものだ / verb te-form＋ほしいものだ
【Point】Used to express one's own strong wish with feeling. 〜てほしいものだ is for what you want others to do. Often for wishes that are hard to realize.
文法 Lesson 14|4: expresses a strong wish that it could somehow be done

I wonder whether there is some way to solve this problem easily.
Isn't there some way I could meet him?

【Connection】verb nai-form＋ないものか／ないものだろうか
【Point】Used when strongly wishing that something difficult could somehow be done. ないものだろうか is more polite and literary.
文法 Lesson 14|5: there is something about it (impressive, moving, etc.); gives an evaluation

There is something in his performance that draws people in.
Her idea is a little old-fashioned, but there is something convincing in it.

【Connection】verb dictionary form＋ものがある / i-adjective dictionary form＋ものがある / na-adjective (stem)＋な＋ものがある
【Point】Used to evaluate people or works by saying "I feel something like that". Usually preceded by words of evaluation such as attractive, surprising, thought-provoking.
文法 Lesson 14|6: expresses how very much (happy, sad, etc.) it must be or was

Coming to a foreign country alone, how anxious he must have been.
How delighted the family was at the news of the pass!

【Connection】verb dictionary form＋ことだろう／ことか / verb ta-form＋ことだろう／ことか / i-adjective dictionary form＋ことだろう／ことか / na-adjective (stem)＋な＋ことだろう／ことか
【Point】Used with どんなに, どれほど, なんと to express strong emotion. ことだろう is conjecture, ことか is exclamation. Na-adjectives: 〜なことだろう.
文法 Lesson 14|7: judging from ~; from the standpoint of ~

Judging from his expression, the exam results seem to have been good.
From my standpoint, I cannot agree with that opinion.

【Connection】noun＋からすると／からすれば
【Point】Has two uses: judging on the basis of ~, and seeing from the standpoint of ~. A judgment or conjecture follows.
文法 Lesson 14|8: even though ~ (criticism or dissatisfaction toward someone)

You know it, so why won't you tell me?
Even though he is a child, he talks like an adult.

【Connection】plain form＋（な形容詞→な、名詞→の）＋くせに
【Point】Criticizes or complains that two facts about the same person do not match. Rarely used about oneself, and rude toward superiors.
文法 Lesson 14|9: looks as if ~; a feeling shows in one's face or manner

The old man was looking at the sky with sad eyes.
He proudly showed me his certificate.

【Connection】i-adjective stem＋げ（な／に） / na-adjective (stem)＋げ（な／に）
【Point】Describes how another person looks; not used for one's own feelings. Mostly fixed words like 悲しげ, 寂しげ, 得意げ, 不安げ, often in the forms 〜げな顔 / 〜げに.
文法 Lesson 14|10: does not even ~; does not ~ at all

He left without even looking at me.
I believed what I was told without even checking it.

【Connection】verb masu-stem (without "ます")＋もしない（する→しもしない） / noun＋もしない
【Point】A strong negation meaning "does not even ~", carrying the speaker's complaint or surprise. する becomes しもしない. Also used as Nもしない.
文法 Lesson 15|1:
My sister does the housework and, at the same time, also works as a translator.
The economy has improved, but on the other hand, prices have also risen.

【Connection】plain form＋（な形容詞→な／である、名詞→である）＋一方（で）
【Point】Has two uses: doing two things at once, and contrasting two aspects. It states another side of the same topic. For simply comparing A and B, 一方 alone is used.
文法 Lesson 15|2: thanks to the effort, a good result came

Thanks to the care we gave him, my grandfather recovered.
Our hard practice paid off, and we were able to win the tournament.

【Connection】verb ta-form＋かいがあって / noun＋の＋かいがあって
【Point】Used when effort or care is rewarded. A good result follows. When the effort brought no result, use かいもなく.
文法 Lesson 15|3:
A problem this hard — there is no way a child can solve it.
I think there is no way that person will apologize.

【Connection】verb masu-stem (without "ます")＋っこない
【Point】Colloquial form used when the speaker strongly thinks "impossible". Similar to わけがない and はずがない, but more casual. Not used in writing.
文法 Lesson 15|4: states what ~ is like in general

Friendship does not change, even as time passes.
Words can hurt people, depending on how they are used.

【Connection】noun＋というものは
【Point】States the general nature of the topic or the speaker's view. Used for generalizations, not for one specific thing. In speech, というのは is also used.
文法 Lesson 15|5:
Without the jokes, please tell me the truth.
The system cannot be considered without the tax issue.

【Connection】Noun + を抜きに（して）
【Point】Often used as 'N を抜きにしては…ない', meaning 'it cannot be ... without N'.
文法 Lesson 15|6:
Now that I've taken it on, I intend to take responsibility to the end.
As a working adult, you must be punctual.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form) + 以上 / Verb (ta-form) + 以上 / Verb (nai-form) + 以上 / i-adjective (dictionary form) + 以上 / na-adjective (stem) + である以上 / Noun + である以上
【Point】The clause that follows expresses responsibility, obligation or resolve (must, intend to, should), not a plain fact.
文法 Lesson 15|7:
When I was in hospital, a friend came with flowers.
At the graduation ceremony, I received some words from my teacher.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form) + 折に / Verb (ta-form) + 折に / Noun + の + 折に
【Point】The main clause is often a greeting, thanks or request. In casual speech, ときに sounds more natural.
文法 Lesson 15|8: at least ~ / better than the worse alternative

I lost my wallet, but at least there wasn't much money in it.
The room is small, but at least it's close to the station.

【Connection】Plain form + だけまし（だ） / na-adjective (stem) + な＋だけまし（だ）
【Point】Used to console oneself that it could have been worse. Not for praising a good result.
文法 Lesson 15|9:
His talk is argumentative and a bit tiring.
Some people become short-tempered as they age.

【Connection】Noun + っぽい / Verb (masu-stem) + っぽい / i-adjective (stem) + っぽい
【Point】Attaches to nouns, verbs and i-adjectives, often with a slightly negative nuance (子供っぽい, 忘れっぽい). It conjugates like an i-adjective.
文法 Lesson 15|10: isn't there some way to ~? / I wish I could ~

Isn't there some way to stop this noise?
I wonder if I could somehow get my child to like vegetables.

【Connection】Verb (nai-form) + ものか（と思う） / Verb (nai-form) + ものだろうか／ものでしょうか
【Point】Expresses a wish to somehow achieve something difficult; often followed by と思う / と考える.
文法 Lesson 16|1:
An explanatory meeting was held for residents before the construction began.
Before the entrance ceremony, the principal explained some points.

【Connection】Noun + に先立って / Verb (dictionary form) + のに先立って
【Point】The main clause is usually a preparation, greeting or check. Also 〜に先立ち.
文法 Lesson 16|2:
Whatever the result, I want to praise him for trying to the end.
Whether we can win or not, we intend to fight with all our strength.

【Connection】Noun + はともかく（として） / Plain form + かどうかはともかく
【Point】In 'A はともかく B', B is what really matters; A is set aside for now.
文法 Lesson 16|3: when it comes to ~ (a person acts differently)

When it comes to fishing, my father becomes lively from early morning.
When it comes to her boyfriend, she can't see what's around her.

【Connection】Noun + の + こととなると / Verb (dictionary form) + こととなると
【Point】Mostly 〜のこととなると; the main clause describes someone changing from usual behavior (becoming eager, etc.).
文法 Lesson 16|4:
Only by experiencing it yourself will you understand its real meaning.
It is only because my family supports me that I can keep going.

【Connection】Verb (te-form) + こそ
【Point】A positive evaluation follows (is worthwhile, can truly ..., is meaningful). Not used for bad results.
文法 Lesson 16|5:
My younger brother plays games, sleeps, wakes up and plays games again.
She spent the day looking at the sea and sighing again and again.

【Connection】Verb (te-form) + は（〜ては）
【Point】In 'A しては B する', two actions alternate repeatedly; verbs of action follow.
文法 Lesson 16|6: I'll definitely ~ (show you) / demonstrate by doing

Next year I will definitely climb Mt. Fuji.
My older brother performed a difficult trick in front of everyone.

【Connection】Verb (te-form) + みせる
【Point】In the resolve sense it often occurs with 必ず/絶対; the subject is the speaker.
文法 Lesson 16|7: it's not that I can't / not impossible

I'm busy, but it's not that I can't help.
It's not that it isn't cold today, but I don't think a coat is needed.

【Connection】Verb (nai-form) + こともない / i-adjective (stem) + くないこともない
【Point】Used to admit something with reservation; often followed by が/けど and an opposite feeling.
文法 Lesson 16|8: triggered by ~ / taking ~ as an opportunity

Triggered by the big earthquake, awareness of disaster prevention rose in this town.
I changed my daily rhythm after moving house.

【Connection】Noun + を契機に（して） / Verb (dictionary form) + のを契機に（して） / Verb (ta-form) + のを契機に（して）
【Point】The main clause is a significant change (life, thinking, situation), usually after a past event. In speech 〜をきっかけに is also used.
文法 Lesson 16|9: after a long ~, (in the end, usually bad)

After changing jobs many times, he ended up losing his job.
After a long argument, the meeting ended with nothing decided.

【Connection】Verb (ta-form) + あげく（に） / Noun + の + あげく（に）
【Point】A bad result usually follows; no expression of the speaker will. Also あげくの果て.
文法 Lesson 17|1:
He kept making efforts without giving up on his dream.
My grandmother passed away peacefully, never losing her smile to the end.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form) + ことなく
【Point】More formal/written than 〜ずに; what follows continues unchanged. Not used with nouns.
文法 Lesson 17|2:
Unless you take action yourself, nothing will change.
The game will not start unless the rain stops.

【Connection】Verb (nai-form) + 限り / i-adjective (stem) + くない限り / na-adjective (stem) + でない限り / Noun + でない限り
【Point】Typically followed by a negative: the situation will not change as long as the condition is not met.
文法 Lesson 17|3:
Responding to readers' voices, we created a new section.
Living up to his parents' expectations, he became a doctor.

【Connection】Noun + に応えて
【Point】Attaches to nouns showing people's wishes (期待, 要望, 声援, リクエスト). Different from 〜に応じて (according to).
文法 Lesson 17|4: can ~ completely (~きれない: cannot ~ all the way)

I can't finish reading this book in one day.
I can't thank him enough for his kindness.

【Connection】Verb (masu-stem) + きれる／きれない
【Point】Mostly used as 〜きれない (cannot do it all). 〜きる means to do something completely.
文法 Lesson 17|5:
I hear a new department store is going to open in front of the station.
I heard Mr. Yamada has been in hospital since last week.

【Connection】Plain form + とか
【Point】Placed at sentence end to relay something heard without certainty; casual, also in letters.
文法 Lesson 17|6:
It's not a serious injury, so there's no need to go to the hospital.
No need to worry. I'll take care of everything.

【Connection】Verb (dictionary form) + には及ばない / Noun + には及ばない
【Point】Tells someone it isn't necessary to go that far; polite form 〜には及びません.
文法 Lesson 17|7: as if ~ (though it's not actually so)

She greeted us with a smile as if nothing had happened.
The child used difficult words as if he were an adult.

【Connection】Plain form + かのように / na-adjective (stem) + である／だった＋かのように / Noun + である／だった＋かのように
【Point】Often with まるで/あたかも. Nouns and na-adjectives take である/だった. Stronger sense of "not actually so" than plain ように.
文法 Lesson 17|8:
The role of women in companies has changed greatly.
We discussed the problem of bullying at school.

【Connection】Noun + における＋名詞
【Point】Form 'A における B' modifies a noun B (problem, role, change...). The related 〜において can modify a verb/clause.
文法 Lesson 17|9:
If the trains have stopped, it means I can't go to the office today.
That he says nothing probably means he agrees.

【Connection】Plain form + ということは
【Point】Followed by a conclusion or confirmation (〜ということだ, 〜わけだ). Different from 〜というのは, which gives a reason or definition.
文法 Lesson 18|1: It is best to ~; nothing beats ~.

It never hurts to prepare early.
The higher the salary, the better.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋にこしたことはない／verb (nai-form)＋にこしたことはない／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋にこしたことはない／na-adjective (stem)＋である＋にこしたことはない／noun＋である＋にこしたことはない
【Point】Used to state a general view that something is safer or better even if not strictly necessary. It is not used for strong orders.
文法 Lesson 18|2: Excessively; to an extreme degree (surprise or trouble).

I was so extremely busy that I did not even have time to eat.
The news was so sudden that no one could reply.

【Connection】adverb (placed before a verb or adjective)
【Point】Often followed by a result or reason (node, te, tame). Stronger than totemo; it feels that the degree has gone too far.
文法 Lesson 18|3: Because it is such a (special) X, ~ (the same noun is repeated).

Since the other person was who he was, I spoke carefully so as not to be rude.
Given what time of year it is, we should refrain from traveling.

【Connection】noun＋が＋noun＋だけに
【Point】The same noun is used twice, as in koto ga koto dake ni. The result describes extra care or difficulty because the matter is special.
文法 Lesson 18|4: As expected of ~; living up to ~ (a good result).

Being a professional chef, he is skilled at using a kitchen knife.
As the long practice deserved, the presentation was perfect.

【Connection】noun＋だけあって／verb (dictionary form)＋だけあって／verb (ta-form)＋だけあって／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋だけあって／na-adjective (stem)＋な＋だけあって
【Point】The first part gives a status or effort; the second part gives a good result that fits it. It is not used for bad results (unlike dake ni).
文法 Lesson 18|5: A state resulting from an action; a continuing state or a habit.

A wallet is lying on the road.
My older sister works at a company in Tokyo.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋いる
【Point】Intransitive verb + teiru shows a present state. Tearu shows the result of someone's intentional action (transitive verbs); teoku means doing something in advance.
文法 Lesson 18|6: As for ~ (switching the topic to contrast with the previous one).

My older brother studies a lot. As for my younger brother, he does nothing but play games every day.
Tokyo is hot in summer. As for Hokkaido, it is surprisingly cool.

【Connection】noun＋はというと
【Point】The following part describes a different or opposite situation from what was just mentioned. A contrasting statement is needed before it.
文法 Lesson 18|7: If ~ continues, I cannot stand it.

If the neighbors keep making noise this late every night, I cannot stand it.
If the rent is this high, I cannot manage.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋はかなわない／i-adjective (-ku form)＋てはかなわない／na-adjective (stem)＋では＋かなわない
【Point】Expresses that the speaker is troubled or annoyed. In casual speech: chaka nawanai. It looks like temo kamawanai but means the opposite.
文法 Lesson 18|8: It is all right to ~; no problem if ~ (formal).

You may leave your luggage here.
You may contact us by phone or by e-mail.

【Connection】verb (te-form)＋もさしつかえない／i-adjective (-ku form)＋てもさしつかえない／na-adjective (stem)＋でもさしつかえない／noun＋でもさしつかえない
