【Point】Used to give or ask for permission. More polite than kamawanai; the form sashitsukae arimasen is common.
文法 Lesson 18|9:
Rather than ride a packed train, I would prefer to walk.
If you are not going to say anything, you had better not come at all.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋くらいなら／verb (nai-form)＋くらいなら
【Point】Pattern: kurai nara, ... hou ga ii / mashi da. The first part is something unpleasant or extreme; the second is what the speaker prefers.
文法 Lesson 19|1:
Whether you can enter the school you want depends on your grades.
Depending on how you explain, the way the other person takes it changes greatly.

【Connection】noun＋次第で／noun＋次第だ
【Point】Means the result changes depending on N. Usually followed by kawaru, kimaru, chigau. Different from shidai ni (gradually) and V-masu + shidai (as soon as).
文法 Lesson 19|2:
Judging from the way he keeps looking at his watch, his appointment must be near.
Judging from the fact that the light in the room is off, he seems to have gone home already.

【Connection】plain form＋ところをみると
【Point】The second part is a conjecture (darou, rashii, ni chigainai) based on what was seen or heard. No volition or command follows.
文法 Lesson 19|3:
It is dangerous to look at a phone while walking.
Unfortunately, I cannot take part this time.

【Connection】verb (masu-stem)＋ながら／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋ながら(も)／na-adjective (stem)＋ながら(も)／noun＋ながら(も)
【Point】The simultaneous nagara attaches only to the V-masu stem. The contrastive nagara(mo) attaches to adjectives, nouns, and -te iru, and the two parts contrast.
文法 Lesson 19|4:
He fought to the very end and protected his own shop.
After agonizing for a long time, I decided to quit the company.

【Connection】verb (masu-stem)＋抜く／verb (masu-stem)＋抜いて
【Point】Attaches to a V-masu stem (kangaenuku, yarinuku, taenuku): to carry through to the end despite difficulty. Usually used with verbs involving effort.
文法 Lesson 19|5:
Not keeping a promise is terrible, isn't it?
Everyone, let us do our best to the end!

【Connection】plain form＋ではないか／verb (volitional form)＋ではないか
【Point】In speech: janai ka. Used for surprise or a strong claim, or for inviting others (you dewanaika). It comes at the end of the sentence.
文法 Lesson 19|6:
Please make today's lunch without wasabi.
Let us skip the formal greetings and get straight to the main topic.

【Connection】noun＋抜きで／noun＋抜き
【Point】As in chokushoku nuki de or joudan nuki de: leaving out something that would normally be there. Opposites: komi de, tsuki de.
文法 Lesson 19|7: Explains a reason or situation; emphasizes the speaker's feeling (~n desu).

I am going home early today. My child has a fever.
This is my precious book. I want you to give it back.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋のだ／verb (ta-form)＋のだ／i-adjective (dictionary form)＋のだ／na-adjective (stem)＋な＋のだ／noun＋な＋のだ
【Point】Noun and na-adjective present forms take na no da. In speech: n da / n desu. Often used to answer a "why" question.
文法 Lesson 19|8: Even for ~ / even if it is ~ (the result is the same).

Even experts cannot know the future exactly.
Even if we hurry from now, we will not make it.

【Connection】noun＋にしたところで／verb (dictionary form)＋にしたところで／verb (ta-form)＋にしたところで
【Point】The second part is a negative or contrary-to-expectation judgment (impossible, unchanged, difficult). No wishes or commands follow. Nearly the same as ni shite mo.
文法 Lesson 19|9: I should have ~ (regret about not doing it).

I should have asked the teacher more questions back then.
I should not have said such a thing.

【Connection】verb (dictionary form)＋んだった／verb (nai-form)＋んだった
【Point】Close to ~ba yokatta: regret in casual speech. The verb is the action that should (or should not) have been done.
語彙 Lesson 1|1: A national holiday set by the government.
Next Monday is a national holiday, so the office is closed.
休日 means any day off; 祝日 is only a day set by the nation.
語彙 Lesson 1|2: Originally a shrine festival day; now used almost like 祝日 (public holiday).
Banks are closed on public holidays too.
語彙 Lesson 1|3: A day without work or school, such as weekends and holidays.
On days off, I often watch movies at home.
語彙 Lesson 1|4: A person born in the year 2000 is already in their twenties.
Different from the Japanese era names (和暦) like 令和.
語彙 Lesson 1|5: On the morning of New Year's Day, my family went to a shrine for the first visit of the year.
元日 is the whole day of Jan 1; 元旦 is the morning.
語彙 Lesson 1|6: January 1st; the first day of the year.
Many shops are closed on New Year's Day.
語彙 Lesson 1|7: The first ten days of a month (also called 初旬).
I have a business trip in the first ten days of next month.
Often used as 上旬ごろ or 上旬まで.
語彙 Lesson 1|8: The middle ten days of a month (about the 11th to 20th).
Cherry blossoms start to bloom around mid-March.
The month is divided into 上旬, 中旬, and 下旬.
語彙 Lesson 1|9: The last ten or so days of a month (from about the 21st).
The end of this month looks like it will be busy.
月末 is the last few days; 下旬 is a longer span.
語彙 Lesson 1|10: Please pay the rent by the end of the month.
Often used as 月末までに.
語彙 Lesson 2|1: An ordinary weekday, not a weekend or holiday.
I'm busy with work on weekdays, so I shop on weekends.
語彙 Lesson 2|2: I'm meeting a friend the day after tomorrow.
Also written 明後日. Different from 後日 (some later day).
語彙 Lesson 2|3: Three days from today (the day after the day after tomorrow).
Summer vacation starts three days from now.
語彙 Lesson 2|4: Daytime; the bright hours from morning to evening.
In summer it is very hot during the day, so I don't want to go outside.
Used as the opposite of 夜中.
語彙 Lesson 2|5: The middle of the night; late at night.
There was an earthquake in the middle of the night, and I woke up.
Not used for evening or early night.
語彙 Lesson 2|6: Because the rain got heavy, the game was temporarily suspended.
Also 一時的. Unlike 同時, it means only for a while.
語彙 Lesson 2|7: A moment; a very short time.
His face darkened for a moment.
Used as 一瞬のこと or 一瞬で; it focuses on the shortness of time.
語彙 Lesson 2|8: The very moment when something happens.
The moment the door opened, the dog ran out.
Common as 〜た瞬間 or 〜の瞬間. We say 一瞬のこと but not usually 瞬間のこと.
語彙 Lesson 2|9: Some later day; a few days from now.
I will contact you with the result at a later date.
Used when the day is not fixed, as in 後日お知らせします.
語彙 Lesson 2|10: Right away; acting immediately after something happens.
I bought the book, so I tried reading it right away.
Used for actions. Not used for states like busy or kind.
語彙 Lesson 3|1: If you book in advance, you can get in right away.
Used as 事前に連絡する or 事前の準備. Opposite of 当日.
語彙 Lesson 3|2: Lately, I've been trying to go to bed early.
About the recent past up to now. Not used for the future.
語彙 Lesson 3|3: I plan to go and see my teacher soon.
Only for the future. Different from 近頃 (recent past to now).
語彙 Lesson 3|4: At last; finally, after a long time or much effort.
At last, the house was completed.
Close to やっと. Often used for a long-awaited result.
語彙 Lesson 3|5: He always speaks with a smile.
語彙 Lesson 3|6: The two of them raised their hands at the same time.
Often 同時に. Don't confuse with 一時 (for a while).
語彙 Lesson 3|7: Just as ~; right after one action, something unexpected happens.
The moment I got on the train, my phone rang.
Form: V-ta + 途端(に). The second part can't be your own will or a request.
語彙 Lesson 3|8: We will arrive at the station soon.
Often used in station or theater announcements.
語彙 Lesson 3|9: A schedule; which things will be done on which days.
Please tell me once the itinerary for the trip is decided.
Different from 日付 (the date) and 日時 (date and time).
語彙 Lesson 4|1: Flowers are blooming here all year round.
Also said 年じゅう. Often used for bad things that keep happening.
語彙 Lesson 4|2: I got home before the date changed.
Does not include time. 日時 includes both date and time.
語彙 Lesson 4|3: The meeting is next Tuesday at 2 p.m.
Often written together with the place in notices.
語彙 Lesson 4|4: A period or season when something is done or happens.
This is the busiest time of the year.
A stretch of time, as in 桜が咲く時期. Not a single date.
語彙 Lesson 4|5: When I graduated from university, I was working at a small company.
語彙 Lesson 4|6: The day itself (the day that was decided).
It rained on the day, so the sports day was canceled.
Opposite of 事前. Often used for exam or event days.
語彙 Lesson 4|7: This trip was more fun than the last one.
Learn with 前回 and 次回.
語彙 Lesson 4|8: Today; the present age (more formal than きょう).
Read こんにち it means the present age; きょう means today only.
語彙 Lesson 4|9: Let's start by learning the words used in everyday life.
Often used as 日常会話 or 日常生活.
語彙 Lesson 37|1: My hobby is reading; I read a book every night before bed.
読書 is reading books; it is not usually used for newspapers or manga.
語彙 Lesson 37|2: Taking care to look stylish in clothes and hairstyle.
Today I have a date, so I dressed up more than usual and went out.
Used as in "a stylish shop" or "to dress up".
語彙 Lesson 37|3: Collecting things you like; the collection itself.
My grandfather treasures his collection of old stamps.
語彙 Lesson 37|4: Films and TV programs made with moving drawings.
I studied Japanese by watching Japanese anime.
A shortened form of アニメーション.
語彙 Lesson 37|5: A picture used to illustrate a book or an ad.
This book has many cute illustrations.
語彙 Lesson 37|6: Writing that freely expresses your thoughts or experiences.
After reading my favorite writer's essay, I wanted to travel.
語彙 Lesson 37|7: A short Japanese poem of 17 sounds (5-7-5).
In class we made haiku and learned seasonal words.
語彙 Lesson 37|8: Japanese flower arrangement in a vase or similar.
My mother studies ikebana and always decorates the entrance with flowers.
語彙 Lesson 37|9: A play in which actors tell a story through speech and action.
I once went to see a play with my family as a child.
語彙 Lesson 37|10: A building for plays and performances.
I saw a famous play at the theater near the station.
語彙 Lesson 37|11: Acting: playing a role by moving and speaking.
For acting practice, I make facial expressions in front of the mirror every day.
語彙 Lesson 37|12: Taking photos or shooting film or video.
Photography is prohibited inside this museum.
A more formal way to say 写真をとる.
語彙 Lesson 38|1: My friend set the poem I wrote to music.
Writing the lyrics of a song is called 作詞.
語彙 Lesson 38|2: Repeated practice of dance, music, sports etc. to improve.
It has been three months since I started going to tea ceremony lessons.
Written 稽古 in kanji. Often used for practicing lessons such as tea or dance.
語彙 Lesson 38|3: Art: painting, music, drama, etc., and works that express beauty.
He is interested in art such as music and painting.
語彙 Lesson 38|4: A work created by a person (painting, novel, music...).
His works are highly regarded abroad too.
語彙 Lesson 38|5: A person who has just started and is not yet used to it.
This class is for beginners, so you can join with peace of mind.
素人 is a non-professional; 初心者 is someone who has just started.
語彙 Lesson 38|6: Creating something new yourself (novel, art, music).
She writes fiction on her days off.
It feels more like bringing something new into being than 作る.
語彙 Lesson 38|7: Putting things out in order to show them.
Photos introducing the town's history are displayed inside the station.
語彙 Lesson 38|8: Making books or magazines and putting them on sale.
The teacher's new book will be published next month.
語彙 Lesson 38|9: Enjoying and appreciating art, music, film, etc.
My hobby is watching films, and I often go to the cinema on weekends.
It means savoring art, more than just seeing or hearing. It is not normally used for sports.
語彙 Lesson 38|10: A person who is not a professional in that field.
Because it is a book for laypeople, it uses no technical terms.
The opposite of プロ. Close to アマチュア, but 素人 can sound slightly condescending.
語彙 Lesson 38|11: A person who does it for love, not as a job.
He is an amateur player, but he won the tournament.
語彙 Lesson 39|1: A professional; a person who earns a living in the field.
In the future I want to become a professional soccer player.
A shortened form of プロフェッショナル.
語彙 Lesson 39|2: Many people take part in the city's events every year.
Also called 催し物. Often used with 開かれる or 行われる.
語彙 Lesson 39|3: Thinking of something new and making a plan for it.
An event planned by the students was a great success.
It carries the sense of coming up with a new idea, more than 計画.
語彙 Lesson 39|4: A gathering of people; a meeting.
Tonight there is a gathering of the neighbors.
The noun of 集まる. 集まりが悪い means few people come.
語彙 Lesson 39|5: A talk on a theme given in front of many people.
There was a lecture about the environment at the civic hall.
講演会 is the event where people listen to such a talk.
語彙 Lesson 39|6: Activities enjoyed for fun outside work or study.
In summer many people enjoy leisure at the sea or in the mountains.
語彙 Lesson 39|7: My father likes mountain climbing and goes to the mountains of Hokkaido every summer.
語彙 Lesson 39|8: Swimming and playing in the sea in summer.
My family went to the beach and swam all day.
語彙 Lesson 39|9: Working for people or society without pay; such a person.
On my day off, I took part in volunteer work cleaning the town.
語彙 Lesson 39|10: Writing your own name on a document.
I signed the contract and sent it to the company.
署名運動 is a campaign collecting many people's signatures for a cause.
語彙 Lesson 39|11: A march in which many people walk the streets to state an opinion.
Yesterday there was a big demonstration in town and the road was impassable.
A shortened form of デモンストレーション.
語彙 Lesson 40|1: National / public (prefecture or city) / private schools.
Private schools often cost more in tuition than national or public ones.
国立 is run by the nation, 公立 by a prefecture or city, and 私立 by private bodies.
語彙 Lesson 40|2: The pupils are playing energetically on the schoolyard.
Elementary pupils are 児童, junior/senior high pupils are 生徒, and university students are 学生.
語彙 Lesson 40|3: A person in the same year or class as you.
Among my classmates, I was the tallest.
Almost the same meaning as クラスメート.
語彙 Lesson 40|4: They plan to tear down the old school building and build a new one.
語彙 Lesson 40|5: The open ground in a school used for sports and play.
I played soccer on the schoolyard at lunch break.
語彙 Lesson 40|6: I go to school by bicycle.
Going to a workplace is 通勤, and going to a hospital is 通院.
語彙 Lesson 40|7: At the cinema you can watch a bit cheaper with the student discount.
A shortened form of 学生割引.
語彙 Lesson 40|8: A private school for extra lessons outside regular school.
After school, my younger brother goes to cram school every day.
語彙 Lesson 40|9: Graduate school, where you study more deeply after university.
After university, I want to go on to graduate school and continue my research.
語彙 Lesson 40|10: A faculty: a large division of a university by field.
My brother is in the Faculty of Economics and I am in Law.
A 学部 contains several 学科.
語彙 Lesson 41|1: A department: a smaller field within a faculty.
Within the Faculty of Engineering there are mechanical and electrical departments.
A 学部 is larger; a 学科 is a division inside it.
語彙 Lesson 41|2: A set program of study; also a route.
I chose the Japanese course with evening classes.
語彙 Lesson 41|3: The main field you study in depth at university.
My major is psychology and I study how the human mind works.
Used like 経済を専攻する (to major in economics).
語彙 Lesson 41|4: A student who does research at a university before formal enrollment.
International students often enter a university first as research students.
語彙 Lesson 41|5: Taking leave from school for a while (e.g., illness); you remain enrolled.
Because of illness, I took a half-year leave from university.
With 休学 you can return later; 退学 means leaving for good.
語彙 Lesson 41|6: Some students drop out of university for financial reasons.
Unlike 休学, you lose student status.
語彙 Lesson 41|7: Learning by actually doing, not only in class.
In cooking practice, I cooked together with the teacher.
語彙 Lesson 41|8: A class being cancelled (e.g., because of the teacher's absence).
The bulletin board said, "This afternoon's class is cancelled."
休学 is when a student takes leave; 休講 is when a class is cancelled on the teacher's side.
語彙 Lesson 41|9: A board where notices are posted for everyone.
The exam schedule is posted on the school bulletin board.
There are also online bulletin boards (掲示板) on the internet.
語彙 Lesson 41|10: What you know through study or experience.
Before the trip, I increased my knowledge of that country's history.
Used like 知識がある or 知識を身につける.
語彙 Lesson 42|1: A group of people with a shared hobby, e.g., at a university.
I belong to a tennis club at university.
クラブ is closer to a school club activity; サークル is a looser gathering.
語彙 Lesson 42|2: A small class where students and a teacher discuss and study together.
From my third year, I joined Professor Yamada's seminar.
A shortened form of ゼミナール.
語彙 Lesson 42|3: Systematic knowledge learned at school; also the act of learning.
He devoted his whole life to the study of history.
語彙 Lesson 42|4: The science of matter, motion, force, light and heat.
If you study physics, you understand why things fall.
語彙 Lesson 42|5: Fields like physics, chemistry and biology that study nature.
Natural science includes physics, chemistry and biology.
Often contrasted with 社会科学 (social science) and 人文科学 (humanities).
語彙 Lesson 42|6: Giving opinions on the good and bad points of something.
A review of the film released last month was in the newspaper.
批判 mainly points out bad points strongly; 批評 covers both good and bad points.
語彙 Lesson 42|7: A chart showing numbers with lines or bars.
I made a graph so that the change in sales is easy to see.
語彙 Lesson 42|8: We conducted a questionnaire survey of passers-by in front of the station.
語彙 Lesson 42|9: Putting scattered things in order or tidying them up.
Before writing the report, I organized the materials I had collected.
語彙 Lesson 42|10: Breaking something down and examining it in detail.
I want to analyze the cause of the failure and make use of it next time.
Used like: analyze data collected in a survey.
語彙 Lesson 43|1: Using another person's words or text within your own writing.
I quoted figures from a newspaper article and wrote them in my report.
The rule is to write where the quoted material came from.
語彙 Lesson 43|2: Handing in documents or reports to a designated person or place.
Before submitting the documents, I checked the name once more.
語彙 Lesson 43|3: An exam where you write answers on paper.
Before the interview there is a one-hour written exam.
Often contrasted with 実技試験 (practical test) and 面接 (interview).
語彙 Lesson 43|4: I memorize ten kanji each day.
語彙 Lesson 43|5: Recommending a person or thing as good to others.
My friend recommended this restaurant, so I came for the first time.
推薦入学 is a way of entering a school on a teacher's recommendation.
語彙 Lesson 43|6: The real ability a person actually has.
This test made my real ability very clear.
Used like 実力を出す (show one's real ability) or 実力がつく.
語彙 Lesson 43|7: I was happy to pass the Japanese Language Proficiency Test.
語彙 Lesson 43|8: A set limit in extent or content.
I will help within the range I can manage.
Used like 試験の範囲 (exam range) or できる範囲で (as far as I can).
語彙 Lesson 43|9: Debating a theme by exchanging opinions.
In the second half of class, we split into groups and discussed.
It suggests people with different opinions talking it out.
語彙 Lesson 44|1: Getting a job at a company etc.
After graduating, I want to get a job at a local bank.
Used as 会社に就職する. Actually joining the company is 入社.
語彙 Lesson 44|2: Activities such as info sessions and interviews to get a job.
Many students start job hunting from the winter of their third year.
語彙 Lesson 44|3: A company looking for workers; also the notice.
Every week I check job listings online.
語彙 Lesson 44|4: Calling publicly for people (or things) to join or apply.
Recruitment for people joining next year has started.
The company 募集する; the person 応募する.
語彙 Lesson 44|5: Urgent recruitment; needing people right away.
The shop manager put out an urgent-hire ad because they were short-staffed.
語彙 Lesson 44|6: To ask by phone or email in order to check something.
Please email the office to ask for details.
The noun is 問い合わせ. 問い合わせがある means to receive an inquiry.
語彙 Lesson 44|7: Applying in response to a call for applicants.
I entered the photo contest but wasn't chosen.
Used not only for jobs but also for contests.
語彙 Lesson 44|8: A document with your name, education and work history, submitted to a company.
On a resume, write your education in addition to your name and address.
語彙 Lesson 44|9: A company choosing a person to hire; also adopting an idea.
My idea was adopted by the company.
語彙 Lesson 44|10: To pay someone to work for you.
Because we are busy, we decided to hire two part-timers.
雇う is said by the employer. The worker says 雇われる.
語彙 Lesson 44|11: Joining a company and starting to work there.
I joined the company last April and work in sales.
就職 is getting a job; 入社 is actually entering the company.
語彙 Lesson 44|12: Requirements for something; in work, pay, hours, etc.
I'm looking for a job with good conditions in both pay and hours.
語彙 Lesson 45|1: Money a company pays to workers; salary.
Salary is transferred to the bank on the 25th each month.
A formal way to say 給料, often used in documents.
語彙 Lesson 45|2: The monthly salary is 200,000 yen, and there is a bonus too.
語彙 Lesson 45|3: In many shops the hourly wage is higher at night.
Used like 時給千円 (1,000 yen per hour).
語彙 Lesson 45|4: Cost of riding trains, buses, etc.
Commuting costs me as much as 10,000 yen a month.
語彙 Lesson 45|5: Providing money or goods (e.g., by a company).
From next month, meal allowances will be provided to employees.
Often seen in job ads as 交通費支給.
語彙 Lesson 45|6: He has a high ability to lead people and suits being a leader.
語彙 Lesson 45|7: It does not matter; any ... is fine.
Experience is not required, so first-timers are welcome too.
In job ads it often appears as 不問, e.g., 経験不問.
語彙 Lesson 45|8: A limit set by age (e.g., from X to Y years old).
This part-time job has an age limit, up to 30 years old.
語彙 Lesson 45|9: Learning a job by watching seniors; also that person.
During the apprenticeship, the pay is a bit lower.
語彙 Lesson 45|10: To follow a good example and try to become like that person.
I would like to follow my senior's careful way of working.
You do not say 見習う for a bad example.
語彙 Lesson 45|11: My sister has worked at city hall for ten years.
Used like 勤務時間 (working hours) or 勤務先 (workplace).
語彙 Lesson 46|1: A person who lives on part-time jobs without joining a company.
After graduating from university, I worked as a part-timer for two years.
A shortened form of フリーアルバイター.
語彙 Lesson 46|2: Nurses working at hospitals have night duty several times a month.
The opposite is 日勤 (day shift).
語彙 Lesson 46|3: A schedule of work hours and days for staff.
I handed my shifts for next week to the manager.
シフトに入る means to work on that day.
語彙 Lesson 46|4: Work done with the hands or body.
At the factory I kept doing the same work from morning till night.
語彙 Lesson 46|5: Being moved to a different workplace within the same company.
My father may be transferred to Fukuoka next year.
The company stays the same. Changing companies is 転職.
語彙 Lesson 46|6: Changing to a different company or job.
The pay is low, so I'm thinking of changing jobs.
語彙 Lesson 46|7: My father retired at 60 and now lives leisurely.
Used both for quitting by choice and for retiring at the set age.
語彙 Lesson 46|8: Losing a job; being without work.
Because of the recession, the number of unemployed people is increasing.
It suggests losing work rather than quitting by choice.
語彙 Lesson 46|9: The kind of work one does for a living.
In the occupation field of the form, I wrote "company employee."
When asking a person, お仕事は？ sounds softer.
語彙 Lesson 46|10: Work or activity done to make money.
Opportunities to use English in business have increased.
Used like ビジネスマン or ビジネス文書.
語彙 Lesson 46|11: A company cutting staff to reduce costs.
The company's finances got difficult and layoffs were carried out.
Short for リストラクチャリング.
語彙 Lesson 47|1: Boss; a person above you at work.
I reported my work progress to my boss.
語彙 Lesson 47|2: A person older or higher in rank than you.
I speak politely to people senior to me.
Often used as 目上の人. The opposite is 目下.
語彙 Lesson 47|3: A subordinate; someone who works under your direction.
The manager is a person who listens well to his subordinates' opinions.
語彙 Lesson 47|4: A co-worker of about the same position.
I went to eat lunch with a co-worker.
Used for people with no senior-junior relationship.
語彙 Lesson 47|5: To get ahead; to rise to a high position.
He got ahead while young and became a section chief.
出世 is getting ahead in general; broader than 昇進, which the company decides.
語彙 Lesson 47|6: To be promoted to a higher post in a company.
It was decided that I will be promoted to section chief next month.
A rise in post decided by the company; pay often goes up too.
語彙 Lesson 47|7: An employee who has just joined the company.
The training for new employees is held for one month from April.
Usually means people in their first year at the company.
語彙 Lesson 47|8: The person in charge who holds responsibility.
I consulted the person in charge of the construction about safety.
Carries more responsibility than a 担当者 (person in charge of a task).
語彙 Lesson 47|9: A person working at a company or shop, including part-timers.
Twenty employees work in this shop.
Has a wider meaning than 社員 (regular staff).
語彙 Lesson 47|10: The way a company organizes its work and people.
The company's structure changed and a new department was created.
体制 means a structure or system; also used for countries and schools.
語彙 Lesson 47|11: To belong to an organization such as a company.
He belongs to a large organization and continues his research.
〜に属する means being a member of a group.
語彙 Lesson 48|1: Our company; a formal way to say one's own company.
Let me introduce our company's new product.
Used among colleagues or in formal situations.
語彙 Lesson 48|2: This company; used to refer to one's own company to outsiders.
Our company will start a new service next month.
Used in letters, emails and company brochures.
語彙 Lesson 48|3: Staff; the people on a work team.
A staff member of the shop kindly showed me the way.
Often used for people at shops or events.
語彙 Lesson 48|4: My new workplace is a five-minute walk from the station.
It can also mean the human relations there, not only the place.
語彙 Lesson 48|5: This building has the offices of many companies.
Almost the same as 事務所.
語彙 Lesson 48|6: A meeting where people discuss work.
We confirm today's schedule at the morning meeting.
More casual than 会議; used for small gatherings.
語彙 Lesson 48|7: A talk to settle how to proceed with work in advance.
We will have a meeting in the afternoon about preparing for the exhibition.
Used as 打ち合わせをする.
語彙 Lesson 48|8: The numbers did not match because of a calculation mistake.
Often used as ミスをする or ミスが多い.
語彙 Lesson 48|9: An idea. 案を出す means to put forward an idea.
A good idea came to me, and I made a note right away.
アイデアを出す and 案を出す are often used in meetings.
語彙 Lesson 48|10: To put forward your idea for others to consider.
I proposed a new menu to the shop manager.
It is offering an idea before the other person decides.
語彙 Lesson 49|1: To consider carefully whether something is good or not.
My family is considering whether to move.
Used when you think carefully without deciding right away.
語彙 Lesson 49|2: To actually carry out what was planned or decided.
I carry out the plan I made properly every day.
Often used as 計画を実行する.
語彙 Lesson 49|3: To focus only on the work, not on anything else.
I concentrated on my work in a quiet room.
集中する means directing your mind and energy to one thing.
語彙 Lesson 49|4: To deal with work or a problem by a set method.
I have to process the piled-up documents today.
Also used for documents, data and garbage.
語彙 Lesson 49|5: To agree on binding terms, usually in a document.
I signed a one-year contract with a new company.
The noun is 契約. You say 契約を結ぶ.
語彙 Lesson 49|6: To tell someone clearly how or in what order to do things.
The teacher instructed the students to open to the next page.
Used from a higher person to a lower one, as in 上司の指示に従う.
語彙 Lesson 49|7: To adjust things so they fit together without conflicts.
I looked at everyone's schedule and arranged the meeting date.
Often used for schedules, time and opinions.
語彙 Lesson 49|8: To respond to visitors or callers in words.
The receptionist dealt politely with the visitors.
Used for dealing with customers. 対応 can be used for things other than people.
語彙 Lesson 49|9: To take a job as your own duty.
I am in charge of guiding new customers.
The noun is 担当. 担当者 is the person in charge.
語彙 Lesson 49|10: To change something that was already decided.
We will change the departure time because of rain.
Often used for plans, times and places.
語彙 Lesson 50|1: To tell a superior the result or state of your work.
I reported the survey results to the section chief.
Information goes from lower to higher. Often paired with 連絡 and 相談.
語彙 Lesson 50|2: To accept a job you were asked to do.
At a friend's request, I took on being the host of the party.
引き受ける carries the feeling of taking responsibility.
語彙 Lesson 50|3: To feel motivated to do something.
If you are motivated, please raise your hand.
The opposite is やる気がない. やる気が出る is also common.
語彙 Lesson 50|4: To pass an incoming call to the person asked for.
I put the customer's call through to the manager right away.
語彙 Lesson 50|5: To put a call on hold without hanging up.
I put the call on hold while I checked.
保留 means leaving something undecided or as it is.
語彙 Lesson 50|6: To be away from one's desk.
He is away from his desk now, so I will call you later.
On the phone, people often say 席をはずしております.
語彙 Lesson 50|7: To take a short rest in the middle of work.
I had worked for two hours, so I took a ten-minute break.
休暇 is days off; 休憩 is a short break.
語彙 Lesson 50|8: To skip what you should do and idle instead.
I skipped class and went to see a movie.
Spoken word. Close to 怠ける, but さぼる centers on skipping.
語彙 Lesson 50|9: To stay up all night without sleeping.
I stayed up all night yesterday to write my report.
Used as 徹夜で勉強する.
語彙 Lesson 50|10: Days off from work or school; a vacation.
I will take a week's vacation in summer and go back to my country.
Often used as 休暇を取る.
語彙 Lesson 51|1: This school puts effort into raising its students' academic ability.
It is ability from study, not inborn ability.
語彙 Lesson 51|2: The worth or usefulness something or someone has.
I hear this old painting is worth a lot.
Used as 価値がある/高い. Applies to more than money.
語彙 Lesson 51|3: A standard used for comparing or deciding.
The standard for passing is 60 points or more.
Often used as 基準を満たす or 基準に合う.
語彙 Lesson 51|4: The ordinary level; the average that most things center on.
His height is a little above the Japanese average.
基準 is a set rule; 標準 is the ordinary level.
語彙 Lesson 51|5: The outcome after something is done.
The test results will be known next Monday.
Used as 結果が出る or 結果として.
語彙 Lesson 51|6: The final answer reached after discussion or thought.
After a long meeting, a conclusion was finally reached.
Often used as 結論を出す or 結論が出る.
語彙 Lesson 51|7: To have good grades or marks.
My younger sister has good grades in math, so the teacher praised her.
The opposite is 成績が悪い.
語彙 Lesson 51|8: That restaurant has a bad reputation because of its poor service.
The opposite is 評判がいい. Used for people and shops.
語彙 Lesson 51|9: To say beforehand what you think will happen.
Experts predict that the economy will improve next year.
Close to 予想, but 予測 is often based on data.
語彙 Lesson 51|10: To measure length, weight or temperature with an instrument.
I had my height and weight measured in the nurse's office.
A more formal way of saying 測る.
語彙 Lesson 52|1: To mark tests and give scores.
The teacher was marking tests until late at night.
採点 gives scores; 評価 can include more than scores.
語彙 Lesson 52|2: To state clearly the good and bad points of a work or person.
That movie was harshly reviewed in the newspaper.
It is not only pointing out bad points; good points too.
語彙 Lesson 52|3: To judge the worth of a thing or person.
The president thinks highly of his work.
Often used as 高く評価する or 評価が高い.
語彙 Lesson 52|4: To think things over and decide what to do.
I looked at the situation and judged right away.
Used like 正しいかどうかを判断する.
語彙 Lesson 52|5: To compare two or more things to see differences.
I compared the prices at three shops and bought at the cheapest.
Used as AとBを比較する.
語彙 Lesson 52|6: To break something down and examine it in detail.
I analyzed from the data the cause of the drop in sales.
Used when examining data, causes or results.
語彙 Lesson 52|7: To choose and use a person or an opinion.
That company hired ten new employees this year.
Used both when a company hires people and when it adopts opinions.
語彙 Lesson 52|8: Regrettable; so close to success but missed.
It was a close match; we missed the win by only one point.
Also used as 惜しいところで and 惜しくも. Also for the regret of losing something valuable.
語彙 Lesson 52|9: Effective; or still valid under rules.
This ticket is valid for three days from the date of sale.
The opposite is 無効. There is also the word 有効期限 (expiry date).
語彙 Lesson 52|10: Disadvantageous; likely to cause a loss.
Without Japanese, you are at a disadvantage in looking for work.
語彙 Lesson 53|1: Dissatisfaction; feeling unhappy because things did not go your way.
Many employees are dissatisfied with the low pay.
Used as 不満を言う or 不満がある.
語彙 Lesson 53|2: Satisfaction; feeling that things are good enough.
The new room is spacious and bright, and I am very satisfied.
The opposite is 不満. Forms: 満足する, 満足な, 満足に.
語彙 Lesson 53|3: Subtle; delicate and hard to state clearly.
The difference between the two colors is subtle and hardly noticeable.
In conversation, it can also mean 'hard to say; not very good'.
語彙 Lesson 53|4: Excellent; with very good grades or ability.
He graduated from university with excellent grades.
Used as 優秀な学生 or 成績が優秀だ.
語彙 Lesson 53|5: Capable; able and useful at work.
She is a capable secretary and is relied on by the people in the company.
Mainly talks about ability at work.
語彙 Lesson 53|6: Clever; smart and quick to understand.
This dog is clever and learns what I teach right away.
Often used for children and animals. Almost the same as 賢い.
語彙 Lesson 53|7: This clock tells us the exact time.
Forms such as 正確さ and 正確に also exist.
語彙 Lesson 53|8: Splendid; so excellent that it impresses people.
He played the difficult piece splendidly.
Often used as 見事に or 見事な.
語彙 Lesson 53|9: The food at this shop has a reputation for high quality.
The opposite is 質が低い.
語彙 Lesson 54|1: That player has real ability, so he will surely win.
Also used as 実力を出す or 実力がつく.
語彙 Lesson 54|2: To have a natural talent for something.
My teacher told her she has a talent for painting.
Unlike 実力, which is learned, it feels more inborn.
語彙 Lesson 54|3: Absurd; pointless and not worth taking seriously.
It is absurd to believe a rumor like that.
Also said as ばかばかしい. Better not used toward people outside your friends.
語彙 Lesson 54|4: An ideal; the best form one can imagine.
I visited many companies searching for my ideal job.
The opposite is 現実. The form 理想的 also exists.
語彙 Lesson 54|5: To treat people unfairly by nationality, gender, etc.
You must not discriminate against people because of country or gender.
The noun is 差別. It refers to unfair treatment.
語彙 Lesson 54|6: To use others' opinions or examples to help your own thinking.
I used my senior's story as a reference to plan my job hunt.
Two forms: 参考になる and 参考にする.
語彙 Lesson 54|7: To respect and value someone's thoughts and feelings.
We talked it over as a family, respecting the child's opinion too.
Often used as 相手の意見を尊重する.
語彙 Lesson 54|8: To believe a person or story is true or reliable.
I trust him because he is a person who keeps promises.
The noun is 信用. Also used as 信用を失う or 信用できる.
語彙 Lesson 54|9: To recommend a person or thing you think is good.
My teacher recommended me as a candidate for the scholarship.
Often used when recommending a person to a school or company.
語彙 Lesson 55|1: A website; a set of pages viewed on the internet.
You can see the new products on this company's website.
語彙 Lesson 55|2: Visiting a web page; also, how to get to a place.
A popular news story came out and accesses to the site surged.
On a map page, アクセス means how to get there.
語彙 Lesson 55|3: To look up what you want to know on the internet.
I looked up a word I did not know on my phone.
Used as ネットで検索する and 検索結果.
語彙 Lesson 55|4: A favorite; online, a saved page to see again later.
I put the sites I often visit into my favorites.
Also used for liked things, as in お気に入りの店.
語彙 Lesson 55|5: To join two things so they are linked.
I connected the printer to the computer and printed.
Also used in 手をつなぐ and 電話をつなぐ. The intransitive verb is つながる.
語彙 Lesson 55|6: If you connect your phone to Wi-Fi, you can view pages fast.
A more formal way than つなぐ.
語彙 Lesson 55|7: A blog; an online diary-like page of one's thoughts and events.
I post my trip photos on my blog.
Used as ブログを書く or ブログを更新する.
語彙 Lesson 55|8: A secret code of letters or numbers only you know, for logging in.
I forgot my password and could not log in.
Used as パスワードを入力する or パスワードを変える.
語彙 Lesson 55|9: Voice or sound produced by a person or machine.
The sound of the video is quiet, so I cannot hear well.
Used for the audio side, compared with 画像 or 映像.
語彙 Lesson 55|10: A still picture such as a photo or drawing shown on a screen.
I found a beautiful image and used it as my wallpaper.
A still picture. A moving one is 映像.
語彙 Lesson 56|1: Moving pictures shown on TV or in movies.
The video from this camera is very clear.
画像 is still; 映像 is moving.
語彙 Lesson 56|2: To bring data from the internet onto your own device.
I downloaded a free app onto my phone.
The opposite is アップロード (upload).
語彙 Lesson 56|3: Numbers or information used for research or work.
I keep a copy so that my important data will not be lost.
Often used as データを集める or データを分析する.
語彙 Lesson 56|4: To type letters or numbers into a computer.
Please enter your name and email address.
語彙 Lesson 56|5: To keep something so it will not be lost.
I saved the document I wrote as a file.
On a computer, you press the 保存 button. Also used for food.
語彙 Lesson 56|6: To make something visible on a screen or paper.
An error message was displayed on the screen.
Often used as 画面に表示される.
語彙 Lesson 56|7: To change something into another form.
I converted hiragana to kanji and sent the email.
Used when turning hiragana into kanji on a computer.
語彙 Lesson 56|8: Copy and paste: copying text and pasting it elsewhere.
You must not copy and paste text from the internet and use it.
語彙 Lesson 56|9: If you click here, the next page opens.
ダブルクリック means pressing twice in a row.
語彙 Lesson 56|10: The subject line of an email.
In the subject line of an email, write the point briefly.
Said as 件名を入れる.
語彙 Lesson 57|1: To send a received email on to another person or place.
I forwarded the meeting notice email to a co-worker.
Often used as メールを転送する.
語彙 Lesson 57|2: To attach a file to an email.
I attached a photo to the email and sent it.
The word 添付ファイル (attachment) also exists.
語彙 Lesson 57|3: Software; programs that run on a computer.
After I installed new software, my work became faster.
The opposite is ハード(ウェア), hardware.
語彙 Lesson 57|4: A harmful program that enters computers; also a cause of disease.
I opened a suspicious email and a virus got in.
Using antivirus software gives peace of mind.
語彙 Lesson 57|5: For a virus or disease to spread to you.
I caught a cold virus from a friend.
Often used as ウイルスに感染する.
語彙 Lesson 57|6: A machine that prints letters or photos on paper.
The printer at home is old and the colors do not come out well.
Used as プリンターで印刷する.
語彙 Lesson 57|7: Colored liquid used for printing or writing with a pen.
The ink has run out, so I am going to buy new ink.
Said as インクが切れる or インクがなくなる.
語彙 Lesson 57|8: To run out of paper for printing.
The paper ran out, so I brought some from the office.
〜が切れる means something that was there is gone.
語彙 Lesson 57|9: The screen where letters and pictures appear.
My phone screen cracked, so I sent it for repair.
Used as 画面を見る or 画面が暗い.
語彙 Lesson 58|1: When an explanation is hard, drawing a diagram makes it easier to understand.
In books and documents it is used like 「図1」 (Figure 1).
語彙 Lesson 58|2: In math class we calculated the areas of various shapes.
語彙 Lesson 58|3: This university ranked third in the country.
Attach it after a number, e.g., 1位, 第2位.
語彙 Lesson 58|4: I made a table of the population by gender and showed it to the teacher.
Used like 年齢別 (by age) or 国別 (by country).
語彙 Lesson 58|5: The employment rate of this school exceeds 90 percent every year.
Attach it after another word, like 合格率 (pass rate) or 増加率 (growth rate).
語彙 Lesson 58|6: Two tenths (20%) of the students in the class have part-time jobs.
語彙 Lesson 58|7: People aged 20 and over can enter this room.
It includes that number: 20歳以上 includes 20-year-olds.
語彙 Lesson 58|8: Children 140 cm or shorter cannot ride this attraction.
It includes that number; 未満 does not.
語彙 Lesson 58|9: People under 18 cannot see this movie.
It does not include that number: 18歳未満 excludes 18-year-olds.
語彙 Lesson 59|1: From April on, we will carry out the work in a new way.
Used with times and dates: 午後9時以降.
語彙 Lesson 59|2: We asked customers to fill out a questionnaire about the store's service.
Used as アンケートをとる / アンケートに答える.
語彙 Lesson 59|3: This coupon is a service aimed at students.
Often used as 〜を対象に / 〜が対象だ.
語彙 Lesson 59|4: According to the statistics, the number of children in this town decreases every year.
Used like 国の統計 or 統計によると.
語彙 Lesson 59|5: In the library, books are classified by content.
Used as 〜を〜に分類する / 分類される.
語彙 Lesson 59|6: Starting next month, the city will put a new way of separating garbage into practice.
Used as テストを実施する / 実施される. A formal way of saying 行う.
語彙 Lesson 59|7: Imported goods account for half of the store's products.
Used as 〜を占める; very common when talking about proportions.
語彙 Lesson 59|8: This company has a high proportion of female employees.
Used as 割合が高い/低い, 〜の割合.
語彙 Lesson 59|9: The average life expectancy of Japanese people is long even by world standards.
Used as 平均点, 平均して.
語彙 Lesson 60|1: I compared the services of two companies and chose the cheaper one.
Used as 〜と〜を比較する; related: 〜に比べて.
語彙 Lesson 60|2: to rank next to, to follow
Mt. Kita is the second highest mountain in Japan, next to Mt. Fuji.
Used as 〜に次いで / 〜に次ぐ. Different from 継ぐ and 注ぐ, which are read the same.
語彙 Lesson 60|3: A and B had equal scores; both got 80 points.
A formal word. Used as AとBは等しい, 等しく.
語彙 Lesson 60|4: The cherry blossoms in this town will be at their peak this weekend.
Used as ピークを迎える / ピークをすぎる.
語彙 Lesson 60|5: A little over a thousand people gathered at the venue.
1000人強 is a bit more than 1,000. The opposite is 弱.
語彙 Lesson 60|6: It takes a little under ten minutes to walk to the station.
10分弱 is slightly less than 10 minutes. The opposite is 強.
語彙 Lesson 60|7: The number of tourists from abroad is increasing year by year.
語彙 Lesson 60|8: The number of children in this town is decreasing.
語彙 Lesson 60|9: I hear today's high will exceed 35 degrees.
Used as 〜を超える. Distinguish from 越える (e.g., crossing a mountain).
語彙 Lesson 61|1: The temperature reached 30 degrees around noon.
Used as 〜に達する. Note the particle に.
語彙 Lesson 61|2: This athlete ran in a time that equals the world record.
It also means "to line up". Here it means "to be on a par".
語彙 Lesson 61|3: This store's sales have grown greatly since last year.
Used as 売り上げが伸びる, 身長が伸びる.
語彙 Lesson 61|4: As you get older, your physical strength tends to decline.
Often used for changes in a bad direction: 学力が低下する.
語彙 Lesson 61|5: Last month A was behind B, but this month the ranking reversed.
Used as 逆転勝ち, 順位が逆転する.
語彙 Lesson 61|6: With the spread of smartphones, the number of internet users increased sharply.
語彙 Lesson 61|7: Prices have been almost flat for the last half year.
Used as 横ばい状態, 横ばいが続く.
語彙 Lesson 61|8: When night came, the rain gradually got stronger.
Almost the same as 徐々に.
語彙 Lesson 61|9: After taking the medicine, the pain gradually went away.
Almost the same as 次第に. Common in news and the like.
語彙 Lesson 62|1: I just can't accept that price.
Often used as 納得できる / 納得できない.
語彙 Lesson 62|2: My older sister has been absorbed in yoga lately.
Used as 〜に熱中する. Almost the same as 夢中.
語彙 Lesson 62|3: My grandfather has liked eating Japanese food since long ago.
Often used as 好んで〜. More formal than 好き.
語彙 Lesson 62|4: I felt relieved to hear that you arrived safely.
Used when a good result makes your heart feel lighter.
語彙 Lesson 62|5: The moment the victory was decided, everyone in the venue got excited.
It can be used for both joy and anger.
語彙 Lesson 62|6: I got injured and gave up my dream of becoming a player.
Also used as あきらめずに, あきらめがつかない.
語彙 Lesson 62|7: I'm tired of this game, so I want to buy another one.
Used as 〜にあきる, あきてしまう. In kanji: 飽きる.
語彙 Lesson 62|8: My younger brother is reluctant to eat vegetables.
Used for other people's feelings. For yourself, use いやだ.
語彙 Lesson 62|9: The long meeting dragged on, and everyone looks fed up.
A stronger feeling of dislike than あきる.
語彙 Lesson 62|10: If you fear failure, you cannot do anything new.
Used as 〜を恐れる. More formal than こわがる.
語彙 Lesson 63|1: I failed the exam and was depressed for a whole week.
It can also mean falling into a hole.
語彙 Lesson 63|2: I still regret what I said then.
Almost the same as 後悔する; more formal.
語彙 Lesson 63|3: to despise, to look down on
I despise people who tell lies.
A very strong word. It is better not to use it about people casually.
語彙 Lesson 63|4: She was hesitating to say her opinion.
Used as 〜をためらう, ためらわずに.
語彙 Lesson 63|5: I have been worrying about my future path for a long time.
語彙 Lesson 63|6: As time ran short, the more I rushed, the more mistakes I made.
In kanji: 焦る. あわてる is being flustered by something sudden.
語彙 Lesson 63|7: I noticed my wallet was missing and hurried back home in a panic.
Often used as あわてて〜する.
語彙 Lesson 63|8: When I passed in front of my old school for the first time in a long while, I felt nostalgic.
It expresses a pleasant feeling of remembering the past.
語彙 Lesson 63|9: to be in a good mood
My mother is in a very good mood today, so she is easy to talk to.
The opposite is 機嫌が悪い.
語彙 Lesson 63|10: The procedure was a hassle, so I gave up making a card at the store.
There is also 面倒を見る (to look after).
語彙 Lesson 64|1: It keeps raining, and it's gloomy.
It is also said うっとおしい.
語彙 Lesson 64|2: I got an easy question wrong, and I'm frustrated.
A feeling you have when your own ability was not enough.
語彙 Lesson 64|3: It is very painful to be apart from my friends.
Used when body or mind is suffering. Also written 辛い.
語彙 Lesson 64|4: I can't help hating the man who deceived my friend.
Used as 〜が憎い. Different from 〜にくい (hard to do) as in 食べにくい.
語彙 Lesson 64|5: His always overconfident face looked irritating.
Not as strong as 憎い; a feeling of irritation when looking at something.
語彙 Lesson 64|6: Having lost my wallet and walking alone in the rain was miserable.
語彙 Lesson 64|7: My younger brother is crazy about soccer and doesn't study.
Used as 〜に夢中だ, 夢中になる.
語彙 Lesson 64|8: He did not drop his assertive attitude in the negotiation.
Used as 強気な発言. The opposite is 弱気.
語彙 Lesson 64|9: You must not lose your nerve before a match.
Used as 弱気になる. The opposite is 強気.
語彙 Lesson 65|1: My work is done, so I feel at ease.
Used as 気が楽だ, 気が楽になる. The opposite is 気が重い.
語彙 Lesson 65|2: After a morning walk, I feel good.
機嫌がいい is how one appears to others; 気分がいい is how one feels.
語彙 Lesson 65|3: This month I have no spare money to go on a trip.
Used as 時間に余裕がある, 心の余裕.
語彙 Lesson 65|4: Overtime every day made me sick of my job.
語彙 Lesson 65|5: Thinking about tomorrow's interview makes me feel heavy-hearted.
語彙 Lesson 65|6: A part-time job I started casually has now become an important job.
Used as 軽い気持ちで〜する. It is often used in a negative sense.
語彙 Lesson 65|7: The train stopped, so being late can't be helped.
There is also the form やむを得ず.
語彙 Lesson 65|8: Whether this method will really succeed is questionable.
Used as 疑問が残る, 疑問に思う.
語彙 Lesson 65|9: It's strange that he, who was fine until a moment ago, is absent.
Used as 不思議な話, 不思議に思う.
語彙 Lesson 66|1: I have admired pilots since I was a child.
Used as 〜に憧れる, for both people and jobs.
語彙 Lesson 66|2: I am truly grateful to my family, who always help me.
Used as 〜に感謝する. A formal way of saying ありがとう.
語彙 Lesson 66|3: The coach expects great things from that player.
Used as 〜に期待する, 期待に応える.
語彙 Lesson 66|4: This book gave courage to many people.
Used as 影響を与える, 印象を与える.
語彙 Lesson 66|5: My mother left everything about the kitchen to me.
Used as 〜に〜を任せる, おまかせください.
語彙 Lesson 66|6: A senior advised me on how to do the interview.
Used as 〜にアドバイスする, アドバイスをもらう.
語彙 Lesson 66|7: A stranger spoke to me at the station to ask for directions.
語彙 Lesson 66|8: to be amazed, to be disgusted
I'm disgusted with him for forgetting a promise three times.
Used as 〜にあきれる, for bad behavior.
語彙 Lesson 66|9: The section chief made a sarcastic remark to the colleague who came late.
語彙 Lesson 67|1: The customer complained that the clerk's attitude was bad.
語彙 Lesson 67|2: You should stop speaking ill of others.
語彙 Lesson 67|3: to be considerate, to pay attention
Out of consideration for my neighbor who just moved in, I keep quiet at night.
Used as 〜に気をつかう. Unlike 気をつける (be careful), it is consideration for people.
語彙 Lesson 67|4: When driving, you must follow the traffic rules.
Used as 〜に従う; 〜に従って is also common.
語彙 Lesson 67|5: The president apologized to the customers about the accident.
More formal than あやまる. In kanji: 詫びる.
語彙 Lesson 67|6: I apologize for causing you trouble.
Used when you apologize to customers or superiors.
語彙 Lesson 67|7: My grandmother dotes on the cat that comes to her garden.
Used for animals, children and juniors.
語彙 Lesson 67|8: He loves his family and comes home early every day.
Used as 〜を愛する; formal. In conversation 好き is more common.
語彙 Lesson 67|9: The new section chief is a person everyone relies on.
語彙 Lesson 68|1: I believed my friend's words and lent him money.
Used as 〜を信じる, 〜と信じる.
語彙 Lesson 68|2: Having worked together for a long time, I trust him.
Stronger than 信じる: trust built from seeing someone's work or character over time.
語彙 Lesson 68|3: to respect, to look up to
I respect my father, who always makes an effort.
Used as 〜を尊敬する. 尊重 is valuing someone's idea.
語彙 Lesson 68|4: My mother didn't allow me to come home late.
It has two meanings: 'to permit' and 'to forgive'.
語彙 Lesson 68|5: I invited my friend to a movie, but was turned down.
Used as 〜を〜に誘う. 招く is having someone come to your place.
語彙 Lesson 68|6: We invited many relatives to the wedding.
Used as 友達を家に招く. It can also mean to bring about (bad results).
語彙 Lesson 68|7: If you spoil a child too much, he'll become a selfish adult.
Often used in a negative sense: 甘やかしすぎる.
語彙 Lesson 68|8: I envy my friend who works overseas.
The adjective form うらやましい is more common.
語彙 Lesson 68|9: いじめ is the noun. The passive いじめられる is also common.
語彙 Lesson 69|1: Stop blaming only yourself and look ahead.
Used as 〜を責める; 自分を責める is also common.
語彙 Lesson 69|2: In the train, a drunk man was shouting at the station staff.
語彙 Lesson 69|3: It is not good to deceive a child by telling lies.
The passive だまされる is also common.
語彙 Lesson 69|4: Everyone laughed, making fun of the way I talk.
It is a strong, negative word, so be careful.
語彙 Lesson 69|5: The clerk seems to suspect that I stole it.
Used as 〜を疑う. The opposite is 信じる.
語彙 Lesson 69|6: to rely on, to depend on
Even without a map, I got to the station by myself without relying on others.
Used as 〜に頼る. 頼りにする is relying with trust and expectation.
語彙 Lesson 69|7: Please stop scaring the child by speaking like that.
In kanji: 脅かす. Can be used even for jokes or pranks.
語彙 Lesson 69|8: to tease, to make fun of
My older brother always teases me about my hairstyle.
Used as 〜をからかう. If the other person dislikes it, it becomes bullying.
語彙 Lesson 69|9: We all comforted our friend who failed the exam.
Used as 〜をなぐさめる. In kanji: 慰める.
語彙 Lesson 5|1: I set the plates on the dining table before dinner.
Often used as 'shokutaku o kakomu' (sit around the table). A study desk is not a shokutaku.
語彙 Lesson 5|2: washroom (place to wash face and brush teeth)
I wash my hands in the washroom and then eat.
A separate place from the toilet and bath. Used at home and at work.
語彙 Lesson 5|3: I put two beds in the bedroom.
A room for a different purpose than a children's room or living room.
語彙 Lesson 5|4: unit bath (bath, toilet and sink in one small room)
This apartment has a unit bath, so the toilet and bath are in the same room.
Common in cheap apartments for one person.
語彙 Lesson 5|5: A neighbor gave me some vegetables.
'Moyori' is the single nearest place; 'kinjo' is the wider area near home.
語彙 Lesson 5|6: housing; a house where people live
There are many houses around here, so it is quiet.
Often used in 'jutakugai' (residential area). Not for shops or offices.
語彙 Lesson 5|7: I do my work at home.
Used in work or formal situations. For others' homes, use 'otaku'.
語彙 Lesson 5|8: I warmed the cold rice in the microwave.
The tool for cooking rice is a 'suihanki'.
語彙 Lesson 5|9: I turned on the rice cooker in the morning and went out.
A microwave only reheats; a rice cooker cooks from raw rice.
語彙 Lesson 5|10: I boiled water in the kettle and made tea.
Put on a flame to boil water; usually not electric.
語彙 Lesson 6|1: I chopped the vegetables finely with a kitchen knife.
Used as 'hocho de kiru' (cut with) or 'hocho o togu' (sharpen).
語彙 Lesson 6|2: I had the real estate agency find a room near the station.
An agency that introduces rooms. The building's owner is the 'oya'.
語彙 Lesson 6|3: rental; renting a house or room
Renting is easier than buying a house.
The opposite of buying. The monthly money is 'yachin'.
語彙 Lesson 6|4: I pay the rent by the end of every month.
語彙 Lesson 6|5: Used for real estate. Not for ordinary things.
語彙 Lesson 6|6: This room gets lots of sun and is warm even in winter.
Said as 'hiatari ga ii / warui' (good / poor).
語彙 Lesson 6|7: This house has a layout that is easy to use.
Shown as '1LDK', '2LDK'. It is about arrangement, not size.
語彙 Lesson 6|8: Shown as 'chiku ~ nen' for a building's age. Not for people or objects.
語彙 Lesson 6|9: Popular in Japan for good sunlight. The opposite is 'kitamuki'.
語彙 Lesson 6|10: A north-facing room is dark even in the daytime.
Often has poor sunlight, so rent may be cheaper.
語彙 Lesson 7|1: 2 bedrooms plus living, dining and kitchen
There are three in the family, so we rented a 2LDK.
The number is the number of rooms. 3LDK has three rooms.
語彙 Lesson 7|2: A five-story apartment building was built in front of the station.
Describes the building's height. '5-kai' is the floor where a room is.
語彙 Lesson 7|3: The room comes with an air conditioner, so summer is fine.
'~tsuki' means something is included from the start, like 'kagu-tsuki'.
語彙 Lesson 7|4: It is a five-minute walk to the nearest station.
Often used as 'moyori no eki'. It comes before a noun.
語彙 Lesson 7|5: I live ten minutes on foot from the station.
Seen often in room ads. Does not include cars or bicycles.
語彙 Lesson 7|6: landlord, owner of a rented building
I paid the rent to the landlord.
The building's owner. A 'kanrinin' looks after it and is not always the owner.
語彙 Lesson 7|7: I left the package with the building manager.
Does cleaning and receives packages. Not the owner.
語彙 Lesson 7|8: A security camera is installed at the entrance.
'Bohan' means preventing crime; 'bosai' means preventing disasters.
語彙 Lesson 7|9: This room does not allow pets.
'~fuka' means not allowed. The opposite is 'pet-ka'.
語彙 Lesson 7|10: It is a furnished room, so I can move in right away.
'Kagu' means furniture such as desks and beds.
語彙 Lesson 70|1: admiration; a person one looks up to
My brother is the person I look up to.
Noun form of the verb 憧れる. Often used as 憧れの + noun.
語彙 Lesson 70|2: A meeting was held to get rid of bullying at school.
いじめ is the noun form of the verb いじめる.
語彙 Lesson 70|3: a gift or celebration for something happy
I sent a wedding gift to my friend.
祝い is the noun form of 祝う, as in 出産祝い and 入学祝い.
語彙 Lesson 70|4: I asked my family to receive the delivery.
Used like 受け取りにサインする (sign for receipt).
語彙 Lesson 70|5: My friend suspected me of lying.
〜の疑いがある means it may be so.
語彙 Lesson 70|6: The delay in preparations has become a big problem.
遅れ is the noun form of 遅れる; 〜の遅れ states how late something is.
語彙 Lesson 70|7: My grandfather's teaching still stays in my heart.
教え means the ideas or content one was taught.
語彙 Lesson 70|8: I have no memory of buying such an expensive thing.
Often used as 〜した覚えがない.
語彙 Lesson 70|9: When I reach a stopping point at work, I plan to take time off.
区切り is the noun form of 区切る. 区切りをつける means to bring something to an end yourself.
語彙 Lesson 70|10: This furniture is easy to assemble.
Also used before other nouns, as in 組み立て式 and 組み立て工場.
語彙 Lesson 71|1: Every day is a repetition of practice.
Can also be used like an adverb, as in 繰り返し〜する.
語彙 Lesson 71|2: This dog is a support for my grandmother, who lives alone.
Often used as 〜の支えになる.
語彙 Lesson 71|3: A big earthquake became an obstacle to the construction.
Often used as 〜の妨げになる.
語彙 Lesson 71|4: Someone collapsed at the station and it caused a bit of a commotion.
Used as 騒ぎになる or 騒ぎを起こす.
語彙 Lesson 71|5: I could not refuse my friend's request and helped with the move.
頼みをきく means to do what someone asked.
語彙 Lesson 71|6: Whatever worry you have, please talk about it instead of thinking alone.
Often used as 悩みを相談する or 悩みがある.
語彙 Lesson 71|7: There is still hope that he will be saved.
望みがある means there is a chance; 望みがない means there is none.
語彙 Lesson 71|8: I like going on trips on a whim.
思いつきで〜する means to do something without thinking much.
語彙 Lesson 71|9: This machine is difficult to handle.
取り扱い注意 on a package means handle with care.
語彙 Lesson 72|1: To cancel an order, please contact us as soon as possible.
Noun form of 取り消す; also used for button labels.
語彙 Lesson 72|2: Used as 取り外しができる or 取り外しが簡単.
語彙 Lesson 72|3: mismatch of feelings; passing each other
There was a small mismatch of feelings between the two.
Noun form of すれ違う; すれ違いざま means just as people pass each other.
語彙 Lesson 72|4: to become diluted or weaker (by itself)
After the rain, the dirt in the river water became diluted.
薄まる changes by itself; 薄める is done by a person, for example by adding water.
語彙 Lesson 72|5: I dilute strong juice with water before drinking.
Used as Aを薄める, when you change something yourself.
語彙 Lesson 72|6: If you put pudding in the fridge, it sets.
固まる changes by itself; 固める is done by a person.
語彙 Lesson 72|7: to harden; to firm up (a decision)
The president firmed up his decision to sell the company.
Used for things (油を固める) and for feelings (決意を固める).
語彙 Lesson 72|8: I regret not having said anything at that time.
Used when you think afterward, I should have done that.
語彙 Lesson 72|9: My grandfather likes spicy things more than sweet things.
好む carries the nuance of liking something and often choosing it.
語彙 Lesson 73|1: Because of the rain, the departure was moved up by a day.
早まる happens by itself; 早める is done by a person.
語彙 Lesson 73|2: to move up; to speed up
I was tired, so I went to bed earlier than usual.
語彙 Lesson 73|3: The reputation of the new shop spread all over town.
広まる spreads by itself; 広める is done by a person.
語彙 Lesson 73|4: The storm passed and the sea calmed down.
静まる means becoming quiet by itself; use 静める when a person makes it quiet.
語彙 Lesson 73|5: On summer nights I like to cool off on a chair in the garden.
Used when you yourself get cool; for making things cold use 冷やす or 冷ます.
語彙 Lesson 73|6: よろしければ is the polite form of よければ.
語彙 Lesson 73|7: The teacher takes a walk every morning.
Used for the actions of a superior, never for your own.
語彙 Lesson 73|8: The president is in the meeting room now.
It covers three meanings: go, come and be.
語彙 Lesson 73|9: Please have a seat on that chair.
Means sitting on a chair; usually in the form おかけください.
語彙 Lesson 74|1: I prayed for my family's health at the shrine.
祈る is for asking a god or similar; 願う can be used even without a god.
語彙 Lesson 74|2: I ask for your cooperation, everyone.
Used as a formal way of saying お願いする, in letters and meetings.
語彙 Lesson 74|3: I looked for my lost key in my bag.
Used for things you want to find, such as a lost item, a room or a job.
語彙 Lesson 74|4: In the dark room I felt around for the switch with my hand.
探す is for finding something you want; 探る is for gradually checking what is hidden, or someone's feelings.
語彙 Lesson 74|5: I store up food in preparation for winter.
Can be used for knowledge and strength too; for money or goods 貯める is also fine.
語彙 Lesson 74|6: I save money every month for a trip.
Often used for money, water and points.
語彙 Lesson 74|7: This juice has bits of fruit mixed in it.
Gives the sense of becoming one whole; 混じる gives the sense of something else being included.
語彙 Lesson 74|8: A small stone was mixed in with the rice.
Used as AにBが混じる. It is intransitive, so you cannot say Bを混じる.
語彙 Lesson 74|9: My mother is fussy about test scores.
Used not only for sound but also for a person who is picky.
語彙 Lesson 75|1: On festival days the town is noisier than usual.
Describes a restless scene with many people; also used when society is unsettled.
語彙 Lesson 75|2: The dog's barking is so loud that the neighbors are troubled.
Almost the same as うるさい but a little stronger.
語彙 Lesson 75|3: It can sound rude to say to a superior or directly to the person; use お気の毒 then.
語彙 Lesson 75|4: I am sorry to hear that. I hope you get better soon.
Can be used with superiors, often as お気の毒に or お気の毒です.
語彙 Lesson 75|5: I will get in touch again sooner or later.
A little more formal than そのうち.
語彙 Lesson 75|6: soon, before long, one of these days
The rain will stop before long.
Common in conversation, when no definite date is decided.
語彙 Lesson 75|7: The sun set and before long the stars came out.
Used in writing and stories to describe the passage of time.
語彙 Lesson 75|8: Before, there was not a single shop on this street.
Also used as 以前の〜 or 以前に〜.
語彙 Lesson 75|9: This town once flourished as a port.
A formal word for a past that is different from now.
語彙 Lesson 76|1: With autumn, the mountain scenery became even more beautiful.
Gives the feeling of moving up one level compared with before.
語彙 Lesson 76|2: From now on I will make even more effort.
A little more formal than 一段と.
語彙 Lesson 76|3: The rain became even stronger at night.
Usable in speech and writing; it can also mean in addition.
語彙 Lesson 76|4: He did not answer my question at all.
Followed by a negative such as ない; used to state something strongly and firmly.
語彙 Lesson 76|5: I cannot read kanji at all.
Used with negatives; also used positively, as in 全く同じ.
語彙 Lesson 76|6: Before I knew it, the cherry blossoms were out.
Expresses surprise at noticing something afterward.
語彙 Lesson 76|7: Without my noticing, my wallet was gone.
Almost the same meaning as いつの間にか.
語彙 Lesson 76|8: At this rate we will probably not make it in time.
More formal than たぶん; used with だろう or でしょう.
語彙 Lesson 76|9: Common in conversation; almost the same as おそらく.
語彙 Lesson 77|1: I was deeply moved by the teacher's warm words.
Often used for someone's kindness or an unexpectedly happy event.
語彙 Lesson 77|2: to be moved, to be impressed
I was deeply moved by the documentary.
Used when seeing or hearing something wonderful such as a film, music or a story.
語彙 Lesson 77|3: We placed an advertisement for the new book in the newspaper.
Often means paying to place it in newspapers or on TV.
語彙 Lesson 77|4: They are promoting the new movie on TV.
Almost the same as 広告 but often refers to the whole activity of informing people.
語彙 Lesson 77|5: After hearing the explanation I finally understood the mechanism.
語彙 Lesson 77|6: I heard that tomorrow is a day off and said OK.
Used at work to mean understood; to a superior use 承知しました.
語彙 Lesson 77|7: Growing and reaching a higher level, as with the body, ability or technology.
語彙 Lesson 77|8: This town developed around its port.
Used for larger social movements such as towns, economies and companies.
語彙 Lesson 77|9: Borrowing money from someone you have just met is shameless.
Almost the same as 図々しい; used to criticize someone's behavior.
語彙 Lesson 77|10: I know it is a bold request, but could you lend me a little?
Almost the same as 厚かましい; common in speech.
語彙 Lesson 78|1: I am busy this week preparing for exams.
The ordinary word for having a lot to do.
語彙 Lesson 78|2: The days before moving were hectic.
Stronger than 忙しい in the feeling of being restless and pressed for time.
語彙 Lesson 78|3: The bus was slow and I was late for the meeting.
Can refer to speed and to time of day.
語彙 Lesson 78|4: The service at that shop is sluggish.
Often used negatively about a person's movement or the progress of work.
語彙 Lesson 78|5: Young people are bringing energy to the town.
Used for young adults, not for small children.
語彙 Lesson 78|6: When I was little, I often played at my grandmother's house.
若い can describe adults, but 幼い is for very small children.
語彙 Lesson 78|7: My child is late coming home and I am worried.
心配する is the verb form and 心配だ is the adjective form.
語彙 Lesson 78|8: Until the exam results came out, every day was uneasy.
A feeling toward an unclear future; more about one's own feelings than 心配.
語彙 Lesson 78|9: He listened to the story with a serious face.
Means one's attitude or feelings at the moment are in earnest.
語彙 Lesson 78|10: Describes a person's reliable character; 真剣 describes attitude at a given moment.
語彙 Lesson 79|1: When I tried it, it was unexpectedly delicious.
Almost the same as 意外に; usable for good or bad surprises.
語彙 Lesson 79|2: That teacher is kinder than I expected.
Almost the same as 案外; there is also an adjective form, as in 意外な結果.
語彙 Lesson 79|3: I hear tomorrow's weather will be sunny.
The everyday word for the weather of the day.
語彙 Lesson 79|4: Please do not push yourself when the weather is bad.
A more formal word than 天気, used in news and writing.
語彙 Lesson 79|5: Let us take a 30-minute break and then start again.
A short rest; often used as 休憩時間 or 休憩する.
語彙 Lesson 79|6: Please get plenty of rest until your cold is gone.
Rest for recovering the body or mind.
語彙 Lesson 79|7: There was a complaint about how garbage is put out.
A formal complaint made to a shop, company or neighbor.
語彙 Lesson 79|8: He is always complaining about food.
Used as 文句を言う; a spoken word.
語彙 Lesson 79|9: I told my friend my grievances about work.
Used as 不平を言う or 不平不満.
語彙 Lesson 80|1: This plan has a major flaw.
Can be used for both people and things.
語彙 Lesson 80|2: In the interview I was asked about my weak points.
The opposite of 長所; mainly used for a person's character.
語彙 Lesson 80|3: This town has a large sports facility.
The building or place itself, such as a hospital, school or gym.
語彙 Lesson 80|4: On days off I want to walk in nature.
As 自然に, it also means by itself.
語彙 Lesson 80|5: This area gets a lot of snow in winter.
A stretch of land of no fixed size.
語彙 Lesson 80|6: In the city you can live without a car.
Describes a lively place; the opposite of 地方 or 田舎.
語彙 Lesson 80|7: Osaka is the second largest city in Japan.
A city seen in terms of politics and economy; 都会 stresses liveliness.
語彙 Lesson 80|8: His work is highly valued within the company.
Deciding the value of a person or thing; used as 評価する or 評価が高い.
語彙 Lesson 80|9: That restaurant has a reputation for delicious food.
What people around say; 評価 is decided by oneself or an expert.
語彙 Lesson 81|1: We will extend the business hours by one hour.
Also used in 'extend a deadline' and 'extra time (in a game)'.
語彙 Lesson 81|2: The construction period will be shortened.
語彙 Lesson 81|3: We will break up here, so please go home on your own.
Also used for disbanding a company or group.
語彙 Lesson 81|4: Please gather in front of the station at 9 a.m.
語彙 Lesson 81|5: I enlarged the map and checked the road.
語彙 Lesson 81|6: The company decided to reduce the number of its shops.
語彙 Lesson 81|7: Demand for air conditioners rises in summer.
語彙 Lesson 81|8: I got the teacher's permission and used the room.
語彙 Lesson 81|9: Cars are prohibited from using this road.
語彙 Lesson 82|1: The president strongly denied the rumor.
語彙 Lesson 82|2: I agree with my younger brother's plan.
語彙 Lesson 82|3: My mother is against my living alone.
Also means 'opposite', as in 'the opposite side'.
語彙 Lesson 82|4: The development of the new medicine succeeded.
語彙 Lesson 82|5: My cooking failed; I put in too much salt.
語彙 Lesson 82|7: Also a noun: 'an abnormality was found'.
語彙 Lesson 82|8: I could solve this problem easily.
語彙 Lesson 82|9: Climbing a mountain alone is difficult.
語彙 Lesson 82|10: The mechanism of this machine is simple.
Used about a person, it can mean 'shallow-minded'.
語彙 Lesson 83|3: Indirect lighting is easy on the eyes.
語彙 Lesson 83|4: I told my friend the content of the letter.
語彙 Lesson 83|5: Please write the report in the set format.
語彙 Lesson 83|6: The cause of the fire was a cigarette.
語彙 Lesson 83|7: Reality was harsher than I had thought.
語彙 Lesson 83|8: This shop is run by an individual.
語彙 Lesson 83|9: If you book as a group, the fee becomes cheaper.
語彙 Lesson 83|10: In a match, even yesterday's friend becomes an opponent.
語彙 Lesson 84|1: ally; supporter; being on one's side
When I am in trouble, my brother is always on my side.
Also used as the verb 'mikata suru'.
語彙 Lesson 84|4: Thank you for the other day.
語彙 Lesson 84|5: I went to bed early the day before the exam.
語彙 Lesson 84|6: I drank too much, and my head hurt the next day.
語彙 Lesson 84|7: I put Japanese-style dressing on the salad.
語彙 Lesson 84|8: This house is Western-style and has a big garden.
語彙 Lesson 84|9: I slept on a futon in the Japanese-style room of the inn.
語彙 Lesson 84|10: I like Western-style rooms better than Japanese-style rooms.
語彙 Lesson 85|1: For rooms and the body, 'atatameru' is usually written 暖める.
語彙 Lesson 85|2: to warm up (a room, the body)
I warm the room with a heater.
語彙 Lesson 85|3: to show; to be expressed (feelings, results)
語彙 Lesson 85|4: A dog suddenly appeared on the dark road.
語彙 Lesson 85|5: to appear in a photo or image
My grandmother is also in this photo.
語彙 Lesson 85|6: Next month we will move to a new office.
語彙 Lesson 85|7: to be reflected; to appear on a screen
The moon is reflected in the quiet pond.
語彙 Lesson 85|8: The king ruled this country for a long time.
語彙 Lesson 85|9: to put away; to obtain (a result)
I put all the baggage into the box.
Often used in 'seikou o osameru' (to achieve success).
語彙 Lesson 86|1: I held the paper down with my hand so the wind would not blow it away.
Also used in 'to grasp the key points'.
語彙 Lesson 86|2: I held back my anger and spoke quietly.
語彙 Lesson 86|3: I answered up to the last question in the exam.
語彙 Lesson 86|4: I replied by e-mail to the company's question.
語彙 Lesson 86|5: to take up (a job, a post)
He took up a teaching job last year.
語彙 Lesson 86|6: The plane arrived at the airport as scheduled.
語彙 Lesson 86|7: to be lit; to turn on (light)
When night comes, the lights of the town come on.
語彙 Lesson 86|8: My friend poked my back with a finger.
語彙 Lesson 86|9: to stick; to be stained or marked
A coffee stain got on the white shirt.
語彙 Lesson 87|1: to make an effort; to strive
I make an effort to stay healthy every day.
語彙 Lesson 87|2: My sister served as the organizer of the class reunion.
語彙 Lesson 87|3: My father has worked at a bank for thirty years.
語彙 Lesson 87|4: I let a friend who came from far away stay at my home.
語彙 Lesson 87|5: I pin the poster to the wall.
語彙 Lesson 87|6: The light turned red, so I stopped my bicycle.
'Parking a car' is sometimes written 停める.
語彙 Lesson 87|7: I measure the length of the paper with a ruler.
語彙 Lesson 87|8: to weigh; to measure an amount
Before cooking, I weigh the sugar.
語彙 Lesson 87|9: I time the run with a stopwatch.
語彙 Lesson 88|1: to branch off; to be divided
語彙 Lesson 88|2: I parted from my friend at the station and went home.
語彙 Lesson 88|3: In the second half, the team attacked actively.
語彙 Lesson 88|4: The number of young people fell, and the shop closed.
語彙 Lesson 88|6: This pond is an artificial pond.
語彙 Lesson 88|7: This garden is symmetrical around the center line.
語彙 Lesson 88|8: The distinctive feature of this dog is its long ears.
Can be used for good or bad points.
語彙 Lesson 88|9: The strong point of this vacuum cleaner is that it is quiet.
Used only in a positive sense.
語彙 Lesson 89|1: It is impossible to read it all in one day.
語彙 Lesson 89|2: That smile was a little unnatural.
語彙 Lesson 89|3: I work nights, so my life is irregular.
語彙 Lesson 89|4: Young people's indifference to politics has become a problem.
語彙 Lesson 89|5: Not keeping a promise is irresponsible.
語彙 Lesson 89|6: I was lost in thought and unknowingly walked faster.
Often used as 'muishiki no uchi ni'.
語彙 Lesson 89|8: You must not tell others unconfirmed information.
語彙 Lesson 89|9: People with no experience are welcome for this job.
語彙 Lesson 89|10: Talking loudly on the train is rude.
語彙 Lesson 90|1: Reading a hundred books in a month is an unrealistic plan.
語彙 Lesson 90|2: not open to the public; private
This document is not open to people outside the company.
語彙 Lesson 90|4: A new building went up in the redevelopment of the station area.
語彙 Lesson 90|5: I met an elementary-school friend again after ten years.
語彙 Lesson 90|7: The minimum charge at this shop is 500 yen.
語彙 Lesson 90|8: Last month I moved into a newly built apartment.
語彙 Lesson 90|9: The newlywed couple went on a trip abroad.
語彙 Lesson 91|1: Please come in person to apply.
語彙 Lesson 91|2: He was smiling, but he seems to have been sad in his heart.
語彙 Lesson 91|3: I called the head office in Tokyo, not the branch.
語彙 Lesson 91|4: I am looking for a high-paying part-time job.
語彙 Lesson 91|5: This shop sells only high-quality fruit.
語彙 Lesson 91|6: The famous product of this town is sweet mandarin oranges.
語彙 Lesson 91|7: In the final, I ran with all my strength.
語彙 Lesson 91|8: The total of this month's spending was 200,000 yen.
語彙 Lesson 91|9: Each newspaper company reported this incident prominently.
語彙 Lesson 92|1: The person in charge of this matter is off today.
語彙 Lesson 92|2: We listened to consumers' voices and improved the product.
語彙 Lesson 92|3: The applicants exceeded one hundred people.
語彙 Lesson 92|4: the writer; the author (of the text)
What does the writer most want to say in this passage?
語彙 Lesson 92|5: An earthquake expert explained on TV.
語彙 Lesson 92|6: I heard from the doctor how to take the medicine.
語彙 Lesson 92|7: Lawyers know a lot about the law.
語彙 Lesson 92|8: My sister is a public servant working at city hall.
語彙 Lesson 92|9: I had a lot of work today and worked overtime until night.
語彙 Lesson 93|1: I used the air conditioner too much, and the electricity bill went up.
語彙 Lesson 93|2: The tuition at this school is 30,000 yen a month.
語彙 Lesson 93|3: When I sent money at the bank, a fee was charged.
語彙 Lesson 93|4: I work part-time and pay my school expenses myself.
語彙 Lesson 93|5: The watch I bought did not work, so I had it exchanged as defective.
語彙 Lesson 93|6: This shop has many imported goods from abroad.
語彙 Lesson 93|7: My younger brother can play various instruments.
語彙 Lesson 93|8: I spend carefully according to a plan so I will not run out of travel money.
語彙 Lesson 93|9: In this town, earthquakes are an everyday event.
語彙 Lesson 94|1: Very soon; about to happen at any moment.
The old bridge looks like it could fall at any moment.
語彙 Lesson 94|2: At last; the long-awaited moment is finally here.
Summer vacation finally starts next week.
Can also mean 'more and more', like ますます.
語彙 Lesson 94|3: I took medicine, so the fever will go down soon.
Used mostly in speech. Close to まもなく.
語彙 Lesson 94|4: Unfortunately; as bad luck would have it.
Unfortunately, the shop was closed today.
Used when you cannot meet someone's expectation.
語彙 Lesson 94|5: At least; the minimum one wishes for.
I want to rest at least for one day.
Often in the form せめて~たい / ~てほしい.
語彙 Lesson 94|6: Carelessly; by mistake because of inattention.
I carelessly rode past my stop on the bus.
Close to the opposite of わざと.
語彙 Lesson 94|7: Overtime this month is ten hours at the most.
Used when you do not expect much.
語彙 Lesson 94|8: Please be sure to; repeatedly asking.
Please be sure to give them my best regards.
A polite expression used in letters and greetings.
語彙 Lesson 94|9: For now; for the time being.
I feel relieved for now, so let's have some tea.
語彙 Lesson 94|10: Might you have forgotten your key?
Used with ~かもしれない / ~ではないか.
語彙 Lesson 95|1: At the signal, the birds all took off at once.
語彙 Lesson 95|2: Mother laid the baby gently on the bed.
語彙 Lesson 95|3: The bag is packed full of books.
Also used when a schedule is full.
語彙 Lesson 95|4: Eating Mom's cooking, I deeply felt how precious family is.
Used with 感じる, 思う, etc.
語彙 Lesson 95|5: In a long row; lined up.
Taxis are lined up in a row in front of the station.
語彙 Lesson 95|6: Because of the weak yen, imported goods are getting more and more expensive.
Used when the current trend is already under way.
語彙 Lesson 95|7: Steadily; step by step as planned.
He is steadily making progress studying for the certificate.
Used when things progress in a good direction.
語彙 Lesson 95|8: Fanned by the wind, the fire spread in an instant.
Used for sudden change. The opposite of 次第に.
語彙 Lesson 95|9: Now that it's autumn, the days have become noticeably shorter.
Often used with 減る, 寒くなる, 弱る.
語彙 Lesson 95|10: This dictionary is fairly light and easy to carry.
Also said わりに. Spoken style.
語彙 Lesson 96|1: All the more; more than necessary.
If you rush, you are all the more likely to make mistakes.
余計な (Unit 28) is the adjective form.
語彙 Lesson 96|2: On the contrary; contrary to expectations.
I took a shortcut and it ended up taking more time.
Often used when the result is unwelcome.
語彙 Lesson 96|3: I like fish rather than meat.
語彙 Lesson 96|4: He seemed to be quite tired yesterday.
語彙 Lesson 96|5: Tonight let's eat a lot and drink a lot.
語彙 Lesson 96|6: I have great expectations for my new job.
語彙 Lesson 96|8: If it's only a little rain, the game will be held.
語彙 Lesson 96|9: On the map, the station is slightly to the right.
語彙 Lesson 96|10: I carried all the luggage I was given to the room.
語彙 Lesson 97|1: The teacher just went out a moment ago.
Often as たった今~したところだ.
語彙 Lesson 97|2: My brother made a loud noise on purpose to wake me.
The opposite of うっかり.
語彙 Lesson 97|3: Going out of one's way to.
Thank you for going out of your way to deliver it in the rain.
Different in meaning from わざと.
語彙 Lesson 97|4: So to speak; as it were.
He is, so to speak, like an older brother in this class.
語彙 Lesson 97|5: So this is what is called online shopping.
語彙 Lesson 97|6: Hearing my name called suddenly, I turned around without thinking.
