語彙 Lesson 97|7: I made up my mind and cut my hair short.
語彙 Lesson 97|8: On earth; what in the world.
Who on earth sent this package?
語彙 Lesson 97|9: I pulled the car over to the side of the road for a moment.
語彙 Lesson 98|1: Not at all; entirely (usually with a negative).
He never talks about work at all.
語彙 Lesson 98|2: Even if you work hard, you can't say you will necessarily succeed.
Used as 必ずしも~とは限らない / ~ない.
語彙 Lesson 98|3: Even looking at the map, I have no idea where the road is.
語彙 Lesson 98|4: Not particularly; not very (with a negative).
語彙 Lesson 98|5: I don't know him at all.
語彙 Lesson 98|6: Anyway; in any case (result won't change).
If you're going to throw it away anyway, give it to me.
Often carries a feeling of resignation.
語彙 Lesson 98|7: It seems we took the wrong road.
語彙 Lesson 98|8: Admittedly, this shop is cheap, but the taste is ordinary.
語彙 Lesson 98|9: Having gone to the trouble; since it's a rare chance.
Since we came all this way, let's look around a bit more.
せっかくなのに expresses disappointment.
語彙 Lesson 99|1: Strong-willed; not easily giving way to others.
My older sister is strong-willed and never apologizes, even in a fight.
The opposite of 気が弱い.
語彙 Lesson 99|2: Timid; unable to say no to others.
He is timid, so he is bad at speaking in front of many people.
語彙 Lesson 99|3: My father is quick-tempered and gets angry right away if kept waiting in a restaurant.
気が長い means the opposite.
語彙 Lesson 99|4: My greedy younger brother ate two whole cakes.
The verb form is 欲張る.
語彙 Lesson 99|5: Stingy; reluctant to spend money or give things.
He is stingy, so he always splits the bill.
語彙 Lesson 99|6: Please don't trouble your junior by asking mean questions.
語彙 Lesson 99|7: Gentle; mild and kind in character.
Mr. Yamada is gentle by nature and gets along with everyone.
Used as praise for a person.
語彙 Lesson 99|8: Scatterbrained; careless and prone to mistakes.
My scatterbrained grandfather often looks for his glasses while wearing them.
語彙 Lesson 99|9: Patient; able to endure hardship for a long time.
She is patient and never complains, however busy she is.
語彙 Lesson 100|1: Trustworthy; someone or something you can rely on.
I left the important documents with a person I can trust.
語彙 Lesson 100|2: Since starting her new job, my mother has had a lively look on her face.
Also used as 生き生きと.
語彙 Lesson 100|3: My grandfather lives a leisurely life in the countryside.
Can also be used as just のんびり.
語彙 Lesson 100|4: You must not go to an interview in sloppy clothes.
語彙 Lesson 100|5: My sister is handy and quickly learned both sewing on buttons and cooking.
語彙 Lesson 100|6: Clumsy; not good with one's hands.
I'm clumsy, so I can't wrap presents well.
Also used for being awkward in life or manner.
語彙 Lesson 100|7: Clever; wise; able to judge well.
A clever dog quickly learns its owner's words.
Also used for judgment, as in 賢い選択 (wise choice).
語彙 Lesson 100|8: I took a walk, breathing the fresh morning air.
Used for impressions of people, weather and air.
語彙 Lesson 100|9: Ugly; unpleasant to look at or in heart.
Deceiving people shows an ugly heart, I think.
This is a strong word; avoid using it about people's looks.
語彙 Lesson 101|1: That woman has very refined table manners.
語彙 Lesson 101|2: Talking loudly while eating is considered vulgar.
語彙 Lesson 101|3: When I call my chatty friend, two hours go by.
Can also imply a person who cannot keep secrets.
語彙 Lesson 101|4: A sarcastic or spiteful remark; unpleasant insinuation.
I couldn't say anything back to my senior's sarcastic remark.
Used as 嫌味を言う / 嫌味な人.
語彙 Lesson 101|5: Selfish; doing as one pleases without asking.
You must not open other people's luggage without permission.
語彙 Lesson 101|6: I couldn't turn down his pushy invitation.
語彙 Lesson 101|7: Reckless driving is the cause of accidents.
語彙 Lesson 101|8: A careful person rereads a contract many times.
語彙 Lesson 102|1: The letters my grandmother left are a precious treasure to me.
Used as 貴重な経験, 貴重な時間, etc.
語彙 Lesson 102|2: This town has a distinctive atmosphere.
Both 独特の+noun and 独特な+noun are used.
語彙 Lesson 102|3: The townspeople are grieving over the unfortunate accident.
The opposite of 幸い/幸福.
語彙 Lesson 102|4: Messy; absurd; also 'extremely' in casual speech.
The room is in a terrible mess.
Also said めちゃめちゃ. Spoken style.
語彙 Lesson 102|5: Umbrellas with a unique design are sold at the shop front.
Has a more fun, interesting feel than 独特.
語彙 Lesson 102|6: I want to travel without taking unnecessary things.
Differs in form from the adverb 余計に (Unit 26).
語彙 Lesson 102|7: I was asked to do a troublesome job and I'm in a bind.
「やっかいになる」 means to be looked after by someone.
語彙 Lesson 102|8: A cute puppy was playing in the park.
Feels more delicate and small than かわいい.
語彙 Lesson 102|9: Extreme; tremendous (often in a bad sense).
In this region the temperature difference between day and night is extreme.
Used in formal writing, e.g. 誤解も甚だしい.
語彙 Lesson 102|10: Her Japanese is showing remarkable progress.
Only for good changes. Often 目覚ましい進歩/活躍/成長.
語彙 Lesson 102|11: It's rare for him to be late, isn't it?
語彙 Lesson 103|1: Hearing the happy news, everyone applauded.
Used for celebrations like weddings or passing exams.
語彙 Lesson 103|2: Wasteful; a waste of something valuable.
I think throwing away things that can still be used is wasteful.
もったいない is a distinctively Japanese concept.
語彙 Lesson 103|3: Uh-oh, I'm about to miss the train.
Casual talk among friends. Not used at work or interviews.
語彙 Lesson 103|4: Ridiculous; absurd; not worth bothering with.
I ended up fighting with my friend over something ridiculous.
語彙 Lesson 103|5: I think he is a suitable person to be the leader.
語彙 Lesson 103|6: Can't be helped; no way around it.
If it's a typhoon, it can't be helped even if the trip is cancelled.
Also said しょうがない.
語彙 Lesson 103|7: I'm grateful to be lent an umbrella on a rainy day.
The form ありがたいことに is also common.
語彙 Lesson 103|8: Making a lunch box every day is a hassle.
面倒を見る means to look after someone.
語彙 Lesson 103|9: A real hassle; too much bother.
In the morning even changing clothes feels like too much bother.
Expresses a stronger feeling of bother than 面倒.
語彙 Lesson 103|10: His explanation was long-winded and I got tired of listening.
語彙 Lesson 104|1: On rainy days the road is slippery, so please be careful.
Used as in 足が滑る (one's foot slips) and 手が滑る (it slips out of one's hand).
語彙 Lesson 104|2: Hearing my name called, I turned around.
〜に向いている also means 'is suited to'.
語彙 Lesson 104|3: Hearing my explanation, the customer nodded quietly.
語彙 Lesson 104|4: When I entered the interview room, I bowed politely.
おじぎ alone is a noun; use it as おじぎをする.
語彙 Lesson 104|5: My friend quietly whispered in my ear.
語彙 Lesson 104|6: The teacher glared at the student who was talking loudly.
語彙 Lesson 104|7: to gaze at, to stare at
The baby is gazing at its mother's face.
Unlike にらむ, it does not imply anger.
語彙 Lesson 104|8: Looking up at the tall building, I cried out without thinking.
語彙 Lesson 104|9: I looked down at the town from the top of the mountain.
見下す (mikudasu) means to look down on someone with contempt, a different word.
語彙 Lesson 104|10: She looked at me and smiled sweetly.
語彙 Lesson 105|1: You mustn't scratch the place where a mosquito bit you.
Often used with the body, as in 頭を掻く (scratch one's head) and 汗を掻く (sweat).
語彙 Lesson 105|2: to hold in one's arms; to have (a problem)
I climbed the stairs holding a big box in both arms.
Also used for negative things, as in 問題を抱える (have a problem) and 不安を抱える (harbor anxiety).
語彙 Lesson 105|3: I wrapped the present in pretty paper.
語彙 Lesson 105|4: In the movie, a man punched the other person in the face.
Stronger than たたく (to hit); it can cause injury.
語彙 Lesson 105|5: I tripped on a stone in the road and fell.
Also used figuratively, as in 計画につまずく (a plan stumbles).
語彙 Lesson 105|6: My lower back hurts and I can't bend my body.
The intransitive verb is 曲がる.
語彙 Lesson 105|7: My little sister tore out a page of her diary and threw it away.
Also common as 約束を破る (break a promise) and 記録を破る (break a record).
語彙 Lesson 105|8: Before going to the pool, I inflated the swim ring.
The intransitive verb is 膨らむ.
語彙 Lesson 105|9: I stuck the paper onto my notebook with glue.
Colloquial. The intransitive verb is くっつく.
語彙 Lesson 106|1: I twisted the towel and wrung out the water.
語彙 Lesson 106|2: I dug a hole in the garden and buried the seeds.
Also used for filling free time, as in 予定を埋める (fill one's schedule).
語彙 Lesson 106|3: I added too much sugar to the dish and it became too sweet.
語彙 Lesson 106|4: to scatter things about, to make a mess
The child is playing, scattering toys everywhere.
The intransitive verb is 散らかる.
語彙 Lesson 106|5: I loaded the luggage onto the moving truck.
Also used as in 経験を積む (gain experience little by little).
語彙 Lesson 106|6: I packed sweets tightly into a box and sent it.
Also used as in 席を詰める (move over to close the gap).
語彙 Lesson 106|7: It is rude to snap your fingers to call a store clerk.
The intransitive verb is 鳴る. Used as in ベルを鳴らす (ring a bell).
語彙 Lesson 106|8: Except for Sundays, the shop is open every day.
覗く (nozoku) means to peek through a gap; it is a different word.
語彙 Lesson 106|9: When I peeled off the sticker, glue marks were left.
The intransitive verb is はがれる.
語彙 Lesson 107|1: to put between; to get caught in
I tucked a memo between the pages of the book so I wouldn't forget.
Also used when a body part gets caught, as in ドアに指をはさむ.
語彙 Lesson 107|2: to turn over; to knock over
The child knocked over a glass on the table and the milk spilled.
The intransitive verb is ひっくり返る.
語彙 Lesson 107|3: to twist, to turn; to sprain
I turned the faucet and let the water run.
足首をひねる means to sprain one's ankle.
語彙 Lesson 107|4: Startled by the loud noise, I covered my ears without thinking.
Used as in 耳をふさぐ (cover one's ears) and 口をふさぐ (cover one's mouth).
語彙 Lesson 107|5: I bumped my head on the door and tears came out.
The intransitive verb is ぶつかる.
語彙 Lesson 107|6: I have a charm hanging from my bag.
語彙 Lesson 107|7: At the station, my friend waved and saw me off.
恋人を振る means to dump one's partner.
語彙 Lesson 107|8: Please mix the eggs and milk well.
The intransitive verb is 混ざる.
語彙 Lesson 107|9: My little brother imitates the way my older brother talks.
The noun is 真似; also said as まねをする.
語彙 Lesson 108|1: After explaining the grammar, the teacher gave three examples.
挙げる is read あげる; it is a different character from 上げる and 揚げる.
語彙 Lesson 108|2: My company deals in machine parts.
Also used as in 機械を扱う (operate a machine) and 問題を扱う (deal with an issue). 取り扱う is also used.
語彙 Lesson 108|3: I poured too much milk into the glass and it overflowed onto the desk.
Also used as in 喜びがあふれる (overflow with joy) and 人があふれる (be crowded with people).
語彙 Lesson 108|4: I filled out the application form incorrectly and had to rewrite it.
語彙 Lesson 108|5: Warned by the manager, I changed the way I speak to customers.
改めて can also mean 'once again'.
語彙 Lesson 108|6: The sea was rough because of the typhoon, so the ferry didn't sail.
Also used as in 肌が荒れる (skin gets rough) and 生活が荒れる (one's life falls into disorder).
語彙 Lesson 108|7: I'm working at a new company, making use of my experience from my last job.
生かす can also be written 活かす.
語彙 Lesson 108|8: I lost both my house and my property in the fire.
Used for bigger or more important things than なくす.
語彙 Lesson 108|9: to respond to; to accept (a request)
The city office takes consultations about daily life free of charge.
〜に応じて is also common, meaning 'according to ~'.
語彙 Lesson 108|10: I folded the large map small and put it in the case.
Also used as in 成功を収める (achieve success).
語彙 Lesson 108|11: This machine performs worse than the old model.
Used as 〜に劣る. The opposite is 優れる.
語彙 Lesson 109|1: The weather affects the price of vegetables.
語彙 Lesson 109|2: to be chipped; to be missing
I dropped the cup and its rim got chipped.
語彙 Lesson 109|3: Recently I feel strong fatigue after work.
Also used as in 痛みを感じる (feel pain) and 不安を感じる (feel anxious).
語彙 Lesson 109|4: This medicine works well for headaches.
Also used as in ブレーキが効く (the brakes work) and エアコンが効く (the A/C is effective).
語彙 Lesson 109|5: There is no bridge, so we cannot cross the river.
Also used for exceeding a standard, as in 限度を越える (exceed the limit).
語彙 Lesson 109|6: As children grow up, they start to defy their parents.
Also used as in 流れに逆らう (go against the current) and 風に逆らう (go against the wind).
語彙 Lesson 109|7: In the mountains, we walked avoiding dangerous places.
Also used for things one does not want to do, as in 会うのを避ける (avoid meeting).
語彙 Lesson 109|8: My grandmother's pension supports the family's livelihood.
Also used when supporting a person emotionally.
語彙 Lesson 109|9: The survey results show that young people are reading less.
語彙 Lesson 109|10: If the construction is delayed, problems will arise in terms of cost as well.
A formal expression. In speech, 起こる is more common.
語彙 Lesson 109|11: I shifted my chair a little so the person behind could get through.
The intransitive verb is ずれる.
語彙 Lesson 110|1: to be out of position; to slip off
The time on the clock is a little off.
Also used as in 予定がずれる (plans get shifted) and 話がずれる (the talk goes off topic).
語彙 Lesson 110|2: The athlete endured the pain in his leg and ran to the finish line.
Also means 'withstand', as in 地震に耐える建物 (a building that withstands earthquakes).
語彙 Lesson 110|3: I bought shoes suited for mountain climbing.
Used as 〜に適する / 〜に適した.
語彙 Lesson 110|4: When the teacher finished speaking, the students closed their notebooks.
For doors and windows, 閉める is used.
語彙 Lesson 110|5: I plan to stay in Japan and work even after graduating.
A formal expression. 残る or いる is more common in speech.
語彙 Lesson 110|6: to be lazy; to slack off
I slacked off on studying during the summer vacation and didn't finish my homework.
怠る (okotaru) is a different word, used as in 注意を怠る (fail to take care).
語彙 Lesson 110|7: This year we are aiming for our first win at the national tournament.
Used when one is clearly focused on the result.
語彙 Lesson 110|8: Spring came and grass began to grow in the field.
Also used as in 歯が生える (teeth come in) and ひげが生える (a beard grows).
語彙 Lesson 110|9: There was no time, so I left out part of the explanation.
Also used as in 手間を省く (save effort) and 時間を省く (save time).
語彙 Lesson 110|10: to go against, to be contrary to
Contrary to expectations, the result was a win for us.
Used as 〜に反して / 〜に反する. A formal expression.
語彙 Lesson 110|11: to refrain from; to cut down on
I'm cutting down on sweets for my health.
Also means holding back out of consideration, as in 外出を控える (refrain from going out).
語彙 Lesson 111|1: This juice contains 30 percent fruit juice.
The forms 含めて and 含まれる are also common.
語彙 Lesson 111|2: I got nervous and my voice trembled.
Also used for objects, as in 地震で窓が震える (the windows shake in an earthquake).
語彙 Lesson 111|3: She is blessed with a good family and good friends.
Also used as in 天気に恵まれる (be blessed with good weather) and 人に恵まれる (be blessed with good people).
語彙 Lesson 111|4: My younger brother is studying with the aim of becoming a doctor.
Also used when working toward a goal over a long time.
語彙 Lesson 111|5: The school set up a consultation room for international students.
Also used as in 規則を設ける (establish a rule) and 期限を設ける (set a deadline). A formal expression.
語彙 Lesson 111|6: These figures are based on last year's survey.
Often used as 〜に基づいて. A formal expression.
語彙 Lesson 111|7: The citizens asked the city for a new park.
Also used as in 助けを求める (ask for help) and 意見を求める (ask for opinions).
語彙 Lesson 111|8: Let's go out once the rain stops.
Used for natural phenomena, as in 雨が止む and 風が止む.
語彙 Lesson 111|9: I gave up my seat on the train to a pregnant woman.
Also used as in 道を譲る (yield the way) and 家を譲る (hand over a house).
語彙 Lesson 111|10: I ate too much, so I loosened the belt of my pants.
The opposite is しめる. The intransitive verb is ゆるむ.
語彙 Lesson 112|1: I hear a new smartphone will come out next month.
商品が出る means a product is put on sale.
語彙 Lesson 112|2: The results of practicing every day have finally started to show.
Also used as in 結果が出る (results appear), 差が出る (a difference shows) and 熱が出る (get a fever).
語彙 Lesson 112|3: A new world record was set at the swimming competition.
Also said as 新記録を出す (set a new record).
語彙 Lesson 112|4: I play in a soccer match every Sunday.
Also used as in 会議に出る (attend a meeting), 授業に出る (attend class) and テレビに出る (appear on TV).
語彙 Lesson 112|5: The teacher plans to publish a Japanese textbook next year.
Also used as in 手紙を出す (mail a letter), ごみを出す (put out the trash) and 元気を出す (cheer up).
語彙 Lesson 112|6: The store manager instructed the clerks to clean.
Also used as in 命令を出す (issue an order) and 合図を出す (give a signal).
語彙 Lesson 112|7: The honor of the town is at stake in the final.
Also used as in 命がかかる (a life is at stake) and 期待がかかる (expectations rest on).
語彙 Lesson 112|8: When a car passed, water splashed on me and my clothes got wet.
Also used as in ソースがかかる (sauce is poured on).
語彙 Lesson 112|9: An old car takes time until the engine starts.
Also used for people: やっとエンジンがかかってきた means one is finally getting into gear.
語彙 Lesson 112|10: to call out to, to speak to
I mustered the courage to speak to a person in trouble at the station.
Also means to invite, as in 友だちに声をかけて、食事に行く.
語彙 Lesson 112|11: On weekends I vacuum the rooms from the morning.
語彙 Lesson 113|1: Before the interview, I ironed my shirt.
語彙 Lesson 113|2: In summer, sales of cold drinks grow.
Used when a number or ability grows, as in 身長が伸びる (get taller) and 力が伸びる (ability improves).
語彙 Lesson 113|3: The match was postponed to next week because of the typhoon.
Use 延びる for dates or times pushed back, and 伸びる for length or numbers that grow.
語彙 Lesson 113|4: The meeting ran an hour longer than planned.
延びる is also used when time or a period becomes longer.
語彙 Lesson 113|5: This school values an education that develops children's talents.
Also used as in 力を伸ばす (improve one's ability) and 長所を伸ばす (develop one's strengths).
語彙 Lesson 113|6: I reached for the box on the shelf, but couldn't reach it.
Also means to expand into something, as in 新しい分野に手を伸ばす.
語彙 Lesson 113|7: I plan to grow my hair out until next spring.
Also used as in ひげを伸ばす (grow a beard) and 爪を伸ばす (grow one's nails).
語彙 Lesson 113|8: to be acquired, to become one's own
While using it every day, I came to master honorific language.
身につける means to acquire by oneself, or to wear (clothes etc.).
語彙 Lesson 113|9: Depending on whether you study every day, a gap appears in your grades.
差をつける means to create a gap oneself, as in 大差をつけて勝つ (win by a large margin).
語彙 Lesson 113|10: After arriving home, I realized I had forgotten my umbrella.
Same meaning as 気づく. よく気がつく人 means a person who is attentive to details.
語彙 Lesson 113|11: The teacher gave a score to each student's essay.
語彙 Lesson 114|1: The yogurt in the fridge had passed its best-before date.
Also used as in 期限が切れる (a deadline passes) and パスポートが切れる (a passport expires).
語彙 Lesson 114|2: The battery ran out and the clock stopped.
Also used as in 在庫が切れる (be out of stock).
語彙 Lesson 114|3: He said 'well then' and hung up right away.
The opposite is 電話をかける.
語彙 Lesson 114|4: Put the washed vegetables in a colander and drain the water.
There is also the noun 水切り (draining).
語彙 Lesson 114|5: Recently there are days when the temperature falls below 10 degrees.
Also used for small numbers, as in 100人を切る (drop below 100 people).
語彙 Lesson 114|6: After washing it, the color of the shirt faded.
語彙 Lesson 114|7: If you freeze it, the flavor of the fish gets worse.
Also used as in 質が落ちる (quality drops).
語彙 Lesson 114|8: I was busy with my part-time job and my grades dropped.
The opposite is 成績が上がる.
語彙 Lesson 114|9: I failed the driving test and took it again.
The opposite is 受かる or 合格する.
語彙 Lesson 114|10: Before a sharp curve, the bus slowed down.
語彙 Lesson 114|11: I removed the greasy dirt from the dishes with hot water.
語彙 Lesson 8|1: There are three banknotes in my wallet.
語彙 Lesson 8|2: I put coins into the vending machine.
語彙 Lesson 8|3: I had trouble with a friend over money matters.
Stiffer than 'okane'; used in phrases like 'kinsen kankaku'.
語彙 Lesson 8|4: Money you receive from work or sales; income.
語彙 Lesson 8|5: Food costs are half of my monthly expenses.
語彙 Lesson 8|6: An account at a bank for putting in and taking out money.
I opened a new bank account.
Often used as 'open an account' or 'transfer to an account'.
語彙 Lesson 8|7: Putting money in a bank; also the money itself.
I deposit part of my salary every month.
A 'yokin tsuuchou' is a passbook recording deposits.
語彙 Lesson 8|8: A paper proving that money was received; the payer gets it.
I got a receipt at the shop.
You get it after paying. A 'seikyuusho' comes before paying.
語彙 Lesson 8|9: A paper asking someone to pay money; a bill.
A bill arrived from the company.
It comes before paying. What you get after paying is a 'ryoushuusho'.
語彙 Lesson 8|10: Money paid to the country or city; tax.
Paying taxes is a duty of the people.
語彙 Lesson 9|1: Money paid for using a train, electricity, a service, etc.
The price for buying goods is 'daikin'.
語彙 Lesson 9|2: Money given or lent to help students pay for study.
I studied at university with a scholarship.
Some need not be repaid; some must be repaid.
語彙 Lesson 9|3: All items are sold and none are left.
This lunch box sells out by noon.
語彙 Lesson 9|4: The total money received from selling goods; sales.
This month's sales are higher than last month's.
Also written 'uriage'. It is the amount before costs are subtracted.
語彙 Lesson 9|5: The new product is selling well.
語彙 Lesson 9|6: Income is greater than spending; in the black.
The company went into the black this year.
語彙 Lesson 9|7: Spending is greater than income; in the red.
This shop has been in the red for three years.
語彙 Lesson 9|8: The yen gets stronger; foreign money becomes cheaper to buy.
Traveling abroad when the yen is strong is a good deal.
語彙 Lesson 9|9: The yen gets weaker; foreign money becomes more expensive.
Because of the weak yen, imported goods got expensive.
語彙 Lesson 9|10: A system for sending money to another place or changing it into another currency.
I check the exchange rate every day.
語彙 Lesson 10|1: Asking someone to pay money owed.
I billed the company for the repair cost.
You send a 'seikyuusho'. Paying yourself is 'shiharau'.
語彙 Lesson 10|2: I'm having trouble because vegetable prices went up.
'Neage' is when a shop raises prices; 'neagari' is when prices rise on their own.
語彙 Lesson 10|3: Business of buying and selling goods to make money.
My father runs a small shop.
Used as 'start a business' or 'business goes well'.
語彙 Lesson 10|4: Exchanging goods or money between companies; a deal.
We started doing business with that company.
The partner you deal with is a 'torihikisaki'.
語彙 Lesson 10|5: A company you do business with, exchanging goods or money.
I go to greet our business partners for the New Year.
It does not mean coworkers or the president.
語彙 Lesson 10|6: Please make the payment by the end of the month.
語彙 Lesson 10|7: To pay fixed money such as tax or tuition to a set place.
I pay the rent by the end of the month.
Not used for paying a shop bill.
語彙 Lesson 10|8: Paying the bill for goods or food at a shop.
I paid the bill after the meal.
Managing money at a company is also called 'kaikei'.
語彙 Lesson 10|9: Giving money to help people in need or a group.
I donated to the people hurt by the earthquake.
The money is not returned. Different from lending.
語彙 Lesson 10|10: Cutting waste to use less money or things; saving.
I rarely use the air conditioner to save electricity.
語彙 Lesson 11|1: Using up money, goods or energy; consumption.
語彙 Lesson 11|2: Everyone pays the same amount; splitting the bill.
Let's split the bill for today's meal.
語彙 Lesson 11|3: International students earn living costs with part-time jobs.
Noun: 'kasegi'. 'Moukeru' is gaining profit through business.
語彙 Lesson 11|5: This product has a small profit margin.
語彙 Lesson 11|6: To gain profit from business or investment; a person is the subject.
He made a lot of money on stocks.
'Okane o moukeru'. 'Moukaru' is when profit comes naturally.
語彙 Lesson 11|7: Profit comes out of business; the subject is a shop or company.
That shop has many customers and makes good profits.
Do not say 'rieki ga moukaru'; say 'rieki ga deru'.
語彙 Lesson 11|8: Money paid to a person who works at a company, etc.
Salary is paid on the 25th every month.
語彙 Lesson 11|9: Extra money a company pays besides base salary; allowance.
I want to join a company that pays a commuting allowance.
Often has a word before it, like 'kazoku teate'.
語彙 Lesson 11|10: Special money paid in summer or winter in addition to salary.
I bought a new computer with my winter bonus.
In Japan it is often paid twice a year.
語彙 Lesson 115|1: His prediction was right, and our team won.
語彙 Lesson 115|2: This room gets no sunlight, so it is dark even in the daytime.
Also common in the noun form 日当たり (sunniness).
語彙 Lesson 115|3: If I win the lottery, I want to travel the world.
Used for lucky results; close to 当選する.
語彙 Lesson 115|4: to be hit by a ball
A ball my friend threw hit my head, and it hurt.
Pattern ～に当たる. The thrower uses 当てる.
語彙 Lesson 115|5: I studied seriously, so my grades went up.
語彙 Lesson 115|6: By noon, the temperature in the room had risen.
For numbers or levels rising; 上昇する is more formal.
語彙 Lesson 115|7: to go up to the second floor
Please go up to the second floor and wait.
Also used for entering a house: どうぞ上がってください.
語彙 Lesson 115|8: Taking calls at the company is the job of new employees.
In business, 電話を取る is also used.
語彙 Lesson 115|9: I received instructions from the section chief and redid the materials.
Often used as ～から指示を受ける.
語彙 Lesson 115|10: I plan to take a Japanese exam next month.
試験をする is the giver's side; 受ける is the taker's side.
語彙 Lesson 115|11: My older brother attended university with a scholarship.
Used when something is given through a fixed system.
語彙 Lesson 116|1: I'm busy and don't have time to eat a meal slowly.
Slightly more formal than 食べる.
語彙 Lesson 116|2: It's important to keep a balance between work and life.
Here 取る means to adjust well.
語彙 Lesson 116|3: I went to school every day to earn the necessary credits.
単位を落とす means failing to get the credit.
語彙 Lesson 116|4: Please remove the price tag before giving it as a present.
Here 取る means to remove.
語彙 Lesson 116|5: It was warm after entering the room, so I took off my scarf.
Also used for small items such as hats and gloves.
語彙 Lesson 116|6: Many people go on to university after high school.
Same meaning as 進学する.
語彙 Lesson 116|7: In a quiet room, work progresses well.
Nearly the same as はかどる.
語彙 Lesson 116|8: You should go to the hospital early, before the illness gets worse.
Used for bad things; close to 悪化する.
語彙 Lesson 116|9: This clock is three minutes fast, so be careful.
Opposite: 時計が遅れている.
語彙 Lesson 116|10: I took out health insurance before studying abroad.
Used for joining a group or system; close to 加入する.
語彙 Lesson 117|1: Once May began, it suddenly got hot.
語彙 Lesson 117|2: When my pay comes in, I'll treat my friend to a meal.
Pattern お金が入る (money comes in).
語彙 Lesson 117|3: If you break a promise, you lose trust.
Opposite: 約束を守る. Also 規則を破る.
語彙 Lesson 117|4: He broke the record in the 100 meters.
Also expressed as 記録を更新する.
語彙 Lesson 117|5: They beat a strong opponent in the final and won the championship.
語彙 Lesson 117|6: I drew lines in red pen at the important parts.
Also used figuratively: to draw the line.
語彙 Lesson 117|7: He spoke loudly and drew everyone's attention.
Also 目を引く and 興味を引く.
語彙 Lesson 117|8: I asked the shopkeeper, "Could you take a little off the price?"
Same meaning as 値引きする.
語彙 Lesson 117|9: We decided to send staff from headquarters to the busy store.
送る is used for both people and things.
語彙 Lesson 117|10: International students lead busy lives every day.
Common patterns: 幸せな生活を送る, 楽しい毎日を送る.
語彙 Lesson 118|1: There were so many people that I lost sight of my friend.
Used when something goes out of sight. Also 道を見失う, 目標を見失う.
語彙 Lesson 118|2: I compared the two smartphones and chose the cheaper one.
語彙 Lesson 118|3: I checked my answers again before handing them in.
Also used to reconsider plans or ideas.
語彙 Lesson 118|4: A person I'm not familiar with is standing in front of the house.
Often used as 見慣れた～ / 見慣れない～.
語彙 Lesson 118|5: I was busy and missed my favorite drama.
見落とす means failing to notice; 見逃す can also mean letting an opportunity go.
語彙 Lesson 118|6: The police took back the bag stolen by the thief.
Used for concrete things such as points, money, objects.
語彙 Lesson 118|7: We are working on the problem of reducing garbage.
語彙 Lesson 118|8: My father installed a new light at the entrance.
Also 約束を取り付ける = to secure a promise.
語彙 Lesson 118|9: I recovered from my illness and finally regained a normal life.
Often used for intangible things such as energy, confidence, time.
語彙 Lesson 118|10: to pull up; to raise; to withdraw
I hear the shop will raise its prices from next month.
語彙 Lesson 118|11: to take on; to accept (a request)
Accepting my friend's request, I served as the host of the meeting.
Often used for tasks with responsibility.
語彙 Lesson 119|1: I noticed I'd forgotten something and turned back home halfway.
Used when going back the way you came.
語彙 Lesson 119|2: to pull out; to withdraw; to draw out
The teacher draws out the students' ideas well.
Patterns: お金を引き出す, 才能を引き出す.
語彙 Lesson 119|3: to hold back; to stop (someone leaving)
He tried to go home, so I held him back.
Used when keeping a person from leaving.
語彙 Lesson 119|4: I finished my homework and then went out to play.
語彙 Lesson 119|5: If it's something you like, you can keep doing it for years.
語彙 Lesson 119|6: Even if you fail, you can just try again as many times as you like.
語彙 Lesson 119|7: I looked back on the year and wrote down points to reflect on.
語彙 Lesson 119|8: Please transfer the tuition to the school's account by the end of the month.
語彙 Lesson 119|9: When I turned around after being called, the teacher was standing there.
Used like: turn around when one's name is called.
語彙 Lesson 119|10: to bring up; to start saying
My little brother suddenly said he wanted a dog, and I was at a loss.
～出す means an action suddenly starts.
語彙 Lesson 119|11: The baby suddenly started crying loudly.
語彙 Lesson 120|1: I was called out by the manager and went to the meeting room.
語彙 Lesson 120|2: He was convinced today was a day off and didn't come to school.
Often used for a mistaken belief.
語彙 Lesson 120|3: You must not bring food from other shops into the cinema.
You may see signs saying 持ち込み禁止.
語彙 Lesson 120|4: Sorry to cut in in the middle of the conversation.
Used as 列に割り込む, 話に割り込む.
語彙 Lesson 120|5: When in trouble, let's help each other.
語彙 Lesson 120|6: I was nervous and said my teacher's name wrong.
語彙 Lesson 120|7: My handwriting was messy, so I rewrote it.
語彙 Lesson 120|8: The taste was weak, so I made the soup again.
語彙 Lesson 120|9: The city is calling on citizens to save electricity.
語彙 Lesson 120|10: to pay on someone's behalf (in advance)
A colleague paid the taxi fare for me first.
The money is paid back later. 建て替える (with 建) means to rebuild a house and is a different word.
語彙 Lesson 120|11: to think of; to come up with
I thought of a good idea, so I wrote it down right away.
思い出す means to recall something known before.
語彙 Lesson 121|2: To avoid regretting not buying it, I decided to buy it today.
There is a proverb: 後悔先に立たず (regret never comes first).
語彙 Lesson 121|5: I misunderstood his joke and got angry.
The noun 誤解 is used in 誤解を招く (invite misunderstanding).
語彙 Lesson 121|6: Colds are going around, so I'm wearing a mask as a precaution.
Often used as 用心して～する.
語彙 Lesson 121|7: Thinking the weather was fine, I carelessly went out without an umbrella.
There is the phrase 油断は禁物 (never let your guard down).
語彙 Lesson 121|8: She is conscious of the exam day and is going to bed early.
意識 is also used as a noun.
語彙 Lesson 121|9: I'm satisfied with our new home.
語彙 Lesson 121|10: Experts predict that prices will rise next year.
Also used in 予想がはずれる.
語彙 Lesson 122|1: I decided on a job taking my age into consideration.
語彙 Lesson 122|2: If you book early, it gets cheaper and you save money.
語彙 Lesson 122|3: I've been seeing him since university.
語彙 Lesson 122|4: My older brother showed off his new watch to everyone.
Often carries a slightly negative feeling.
語彙 Lesson 122|5: Even when praised, she was modest and just smiled.
語彙 Lesson 122|6: to feel obliged; to be sorry
I'm sorry to trouble you when you are busy.
Used in polite situations, often as 恐縮です.
語彙 Lesson 122|7: My parents always take my side.
語彙 Lesson 122|8: The two of them are at odds, and the discussion isn't moving forward.
Suggests a clash between two sides.
語彙 Lesson 122|9: The two quarreled, but made up soon.
語彙 Lesson 122|10: The manager was out, so I left a message with the secretary.
語彙 Lesson 123|1: It's dangerous to cross while ignoring the signal.
語彙 Lesson 123|2: The captain ordered everyone to depart.
語彙 Lesson 123|3: The newspaper criticized how the government decided.
Less emotional than 非難する.
語彙 Lesson 123|4: The company that caused the accident was condemned by society.
語彙 Lesson 123|5: I printed 20 copies of the meeting materials.
語彙 Lesson 123|6: I was tired today, so I decided to eat out.
語彙 Lesson 123|7: A firefighter rescued a child from the fire.
語彙 Lesson 123|8: It took an hour to answer all the questions.
回答 (for surveys etc.) is a different word.
語彙 Lesson 123|9: I toured the new library and heard how to use it.
Used as 工場を見学する.
語彙 Lesson 123|10: Please bring your own lunch and drinks.
More polite than 持ってくる.
語彙 Lesson 124|1: to go on to a higher school
After high school, my older sister went on to university.
語彙 Lesson 124|2: He took entrance exams for three universities.
Often used for entrance and qualification exams.
語彙 Lesson 124|3: Please submit the application form by next Monday.
語彙 Lesson 124|4: Every month I send money to my family back home.
振り込む specifically means paying into a bank account.
語彙 Lesson 124|5: Flyers for a new shop are being handed out in front of the station.
Handing out from your side to others.
語彙 Lesson 124|6: I exchanged yen for euros at the airport.
Also used for changing a bill into small coins.
語彙 Lesson 124|7: Many people commute from this town to Tokyo.
For school, use 通学する.
語彙 Lesson 124|8: Because of snow, this road is closed to traffic.
You may see 通行止め signs.
語彙 Lesson 124|9: My older sister is going to take part in the national tournament.
語彙 Lesson 124|10: He retired because of an injury.
Often used for famous athletes and entertainers.
語彙 Lesson 125|1: The teacher raised a hand and signaled to the students.
Also used as a noun (合図を送る).
語彙 Lesson 125|2: This job has a stable salary, so I feel secure.
Also used before nouns, as in 安定した生活.
語彙 Lesson 125|3: The two agreed, so the plan was decided quickly.
語彙 Lesson 125|4: I was warned by the police for speeding.
語彙 Lesson 125|5: Influenced by my friend's story, I came to want to study abroad.
Also used as 影響を与える / 影響を受ける.
語彙 Lesson 125|6: I extended the loan period of the book at the library by one week.
延期 moves a date later; 延長 makes something longer.
語彙 Lesson 125|7: A long text is easier to read if you break lines here and there.
語彙 Lesson 125|8: We talked it over together and solved the problem in the class.
解決 means a problem is settled.
語彙 Lesson 125|9: My injury healed and my strength finally recovered.
Used when health, the economy or the weather improves after being bad.
語彙 Lesson 125|10: I enlarged the photo and looked at even the small details.
語彙 Lesson 125|11: At university I am active in a volunteer club.
活躍 is for visible results; 活動 is just being active.
語彙 Lesson 126|1: My older brother is doing great with a team overseas.
Used when someone shows outstanding results.
語彙 Lesson 126|2: This company does work related to car parts.
Almost the same as 関連, but 関係 can also be between people.
語彙 Lesson 126|3: The landlord manages this apartment himself.
経営 runs a business; 管理 keeps things in proper order.
語彙 Lesson 126|4: When the application procedure is complete, you will get an e-mail.
終了 is for time or an event ending; 完了 is for finishing a task.
語彙 Lesson 126|5: I looked for books related to this article at the library.
語彙 Lesson 126|6: to devise; to find a clever way
I worked out how to place the furniture so that even a small room looks wide.
Used as 「〜を工夫する」: to come up with a good idea.
語彙 Lesson 126|7: It is difficult to tell a real one from a fake.
Used as 「AとBを区別する」. Not the same as 差別 (discrimination).
語彙 Lesson 126|8: In the new country I had a hard time because I didn't know the language.
Also used as 苦労をかける / 苦労が多い.
語彙 Lesson 126|9: My grandfather runs a small restaurant.
語彙 Lesson 126|10: The important thing about a diary is to keep it up every day.
There is a saying: 継続は力なり (persistence is power).
語彙 Lesson 126|11: I had a blood test at the hospital.
Often used as 「検査を受ける」.
語彙 Lesson 127|1: She takes part in patrols to contribute to the safety of the area.
Used as 「〜に貢献する」, only in a good sense.
語彙 Lesson 127|2: This committee is made up of ten members.
Often used in the passive: 「Aで構成されている」.
語彙 Lesson 127|3: to take turns; to change over
The bus driver was changed along the way.
Can also be written 交替.
語彙 Lesson 127|4: He was afraid of speaking in public, but he overcame it by practicing.
Used as 困難を克服する / 苦手を克服する.
語彙 Lesson 127|5: I made a bag by reusing old cloth.
Recycling turns things back into material; 再利用 uses the thing itself again.
語彙 Lesson 127|6: I deleted the photos I didn't need from my phone.
Used for text, data, e-mails and so on.
語彙 Lesson 127|7: Next month we will carry out a survey of the citizens.
実行 can be personal; 実施 is mostly for events, surveys and systems.
語彙 Lesson 127|8: The date is specified on this ticket.
Also seen in 指定席 and 指定された場所.
語彙 Lesson 127|9: Autumn is the season to harvest rice.
Also means a result or gain, as in 大きな収穫があった.
語彙 Lesson 127|10: In interviews, we judge by content rather than speaking style.
The opposite is 軽視する.
語彙 Lesson 127|11: The game ended at five in the afternoon.
終了 is for time or an event ending; 完了 is for finishing a task.
語彙 Lesson 128|1: It takes about four hours to digest what you ate.
Also used for schedules and work, as in 予定を消化する.
語彙 Lesson 128|2: I practiced every day, so my piano improved a lot.
Used for a person's skill; more personal than 進歩.
語彙 Lesson 128|3: A motorbike crashed into a utility pole.
For opinions: 意見が衝突する.
語彙 Lesson 128|4: I showed something that proves my identity at the reception.
A 証明書 is a document that proves something.
語彙 Lesson 128|5: I am collecting documents in order to apply for a scholarship.
Used when you submit a request to an office or company.
語彙 Lesson 128|6: Science has advanced, and medicine has changed greatly too.
上達 is personal skill; 進歩 is broader, like science or society.
語彙 Lesson 128|7: This elevator is limited to eight people.
Used as 〜に制限される / 〜を制限する.
語彙 Lesson 128|8: A famous architect designed the new station.
Used for buildings, machines and systems; for clothes or pictures, use デザイン.
語彙 Lesson 128|9: My older brother majors in physics at university.
語彙 Lesson 128|10: You can choose next year's classes freely.
選択肢 means the available options.
語彙 Lesson 129|1: This new idea is attracting attention from all over the world.
Often used as 注目を集める / 注目される.
語彙 Lesson 129|2: Next year I plan to take on the JLPT N1.
Used as 「〜に挑戦する」 for difficult goals.
語彙 Lesson 129|3: Could you add a salad to this dish?
Also common in 追加注文 and 追加料金.
語彙 Lesson 129|4: Whether you passed will be notified next week.
Also used as 通知が届く / 通知される.
語彙 Lesson 129|5: The employees strongly resisted the sudden change.
「抵抗がある」 means you feel reluctant.
語彙 Lesson 129|6: The power went out at night, so I lit a candle.
The subject is a town or building, not a person.
語彙 Lesson 129|7: It is hard to unify the class's opinions into one.
統一感 means a sense of unity.
語彙 Lesson 129|8: Our business partner went bankrupt, and we can't get paid.
Used for companies and shops, not for people.
語彙 Lesson 129|9: The police identified the cause of the accident.
There is a phrase 不特定多数 (an unspecified large number of people).
語彙 Lesson 130|1: I discovered a rare flower in the mountains.
Use 発見 for finding what already exists; 発明 for creating something new.
語彙 Lesson 130|2: What the president said in front of reporters became a problem.
発言力 means the power to have your opinion accepted.
語彙 Lesson 130|3: This magazine is published once a month.
発売 starts selling; 発行 is producing and issuing.
語彙 Lesson 130|4: to put on sale; to release
A popular game will be released next month.
発売中 means it is on sale now.
語彙 Lesson 130|5: My grandfather invented a new machine for farming.
発見 is finding something that already existed.
語彙 Lesson 130|6: The new car will go on sale nationwide from April.
販売 is selling; 発売 is the start of selling.
語彙 Lesson 130|7: to take apart; to break down
I took the clock apart and examined its mechanism.
In chemistry, it also means a substance breaking into other substances.
語彙 Lesson 130|8: Please sort your garbage by type before putting it out.
語彙 Lesson 130|9: Students at this school study two hours a day on average.
The noun 平均 is common too (平均点).
語彙 Lesson 131|1: I choose my clothes to match the change of seasons.
Used when something changes by itself; when a person changes it, use 変更.
語彙 Lesson 131|2: I edited the travel footage into a short video.
Used for books, videos and programs.
語彙 Lesson 131|3: We carry out an inspection every month to prevent fires.
Common in words like 事故防止 and 再発防止.
語彙 Lesson 131|4: I took in a lost dog and looked for its owner.
Used when protecting people, animals or nature.
語彙 Lesson 131|5: This product comes with a five-year guarantee.
語彙 Lesson 131|6: I am interested in the work of translating Japanese novels into English.
翻訳 is written; spoken interpretation is 通訳.
語彙 Lesson 131|7: There are several contradictory points in that explanation.
語彙 Lesson 131|8: Used for clothes, music, diseases and more.
語彙 Lesson 131|9: Students get 20 percent off the admission fee.
半額 is half price; 割引 is a reduction of any amount.
語彙 Lesson 132|1: In the interview I clearly appealed my strong points.
Also common as 自己アピール (self-promotion).
語彙 Lesson 132|2: This song is a piano arrangement made by my friend.
Used for cooking, music, flowers and more.
語彙 Lesson 132|3: When I actually met him, he was different from the image I had.
Often means impression, as in イメージが悪い.
語彙 Lesson 132|4: My luggage exceeded the weight limit and I paid an extra charge.
オーバーな means exaggerated (オーバーな表現).
語彙 Lesson 132|5: In Kyoto, a guide who speaks Japanese showed us around.
Used for people and books; ガイドブック is a guidebook.
語彙 Lesson 132|6: I had my hair cut at the hair salon.
Also means to reduce, as in コストをカットする.
語彙 Lesson 132|7: I put a cover over the sofa so it wouldn't get dirty.
Also means to make up for something, as in ミスをカバーする.
語彙 Lesson 132|8: You can cancel the hotel reservation up to three days before.
キャンセル料 is the fee for cancelling.
語彙 Lesson 132|9: The video got a lot of comments.
ノーコメント means “no comment”.
語彙 Lesson 132|10: This hotel has very good service.
サービスする can mean giving a discount or a free extra.
語彙 Lesson 132|11: I want to lose three kilos by summer, so I started a diet.
In Japanese it means trying to lose weight.
語彙 Lesson 133|1: If you touch the screen, the menu appears.
タッチパネル is a touch screen.
語彙 Lesson 133|2: I train in the park every morning.
Also seen in ジムでトレーニングする and 筋トレ.
語彙 Lesson 133|3: That song was a big hit last year.
Often used as 大ヒット.
語彙 Lesson 133|4: A senior colleague covered for the new employee's mistake.
Also used to mean helping someone out.
語彙 Lesson 133|5: The teacher handed out the class handout.
At school, プリント often means the handout itself.
語彙 Lesson 133|6: Next week I will give a presentation on the new project.
Short for プレゼンテーション.
語彙 Lesson 133|7: It took three years, but I finally mastered Japanese honorifics.
The owner of a café or bar is also called マスター.
語彙 Lesson 133|8: Old newspaper is recycled and becomes toilet paper.
A リサイクルショップ is a second-hand shop.
語彙 Lesson 133|9: I took a bath and relaxed slowly.
「リラックスして」 can also be said to tell someone to loosen up.
語彙 Lesson 133|10: I go to a piano lesson once a week.
Lessons in school are 授業; レッスン is mostly for hobbies and skills.
語彙 Lesson 134|1: At this shop you can rent a DVD for 100 yen per night.
Also seen in レンタカー and レンタル料.
語彙 Lesson 134|2: In the second half, the new player scored a beautiful goal.
ゴール also means a goal or the finish line.
語彙 Lesson 134|3: I communicate with my foreign coworkers with a smile.
Used with とる; you can also just say する.
語彙 Lesson 134|4: This team has a good balance of attack and defense.
Also used as バランスをとる / バランスがくずれる.
語彙 Lesson 134|5: My family made a plan for the summer-holiday trip.
Used with 立てる; also プランを練る.
語彙 Lesson 134|6: This lunch is hearty and fills you up.
For loudness, say ボリュームが大きい.
語彙 Lesson 134|7: Losing the game damaged the team's confidence.
Often used as 大きなダメージ.
語彙 Lesson 134|8: I might get the chance to work overseas next month.
Also used as チャンスをつかむ / チャンスをのがす.
語彙 Lesson 134|9: Someone complained to the company that the construction noise was loud.
In Japanese クレーム means a complaint, unlike English claim.
語彙 Lesson 134|10: Riding a crowded train every day makes the stress build up.
Also used as ストレスをためる / ストレスを発散する.
語彙 Lesson 135|1: A train came just as I reached the station; the timing was good.
タイミングが悪い is the opposite.
語彙 Lesson 135|2: This cake is high in calories, so I try not to eat too much of it.
The opposite is カロリーが低い.
語彙 Lesson 135|3: My friend's wedding was a party with a casual atmosphere.
The opposite is フォーマル.
語彙 Lesson 135|4: I bought a compact camera for traveling.
コンパクトにまとめる means to summarize concisely.
語彙 Lesson 135|5: This room has little furniture and is simple.
Feels more like “plain and uncluttered” than 簡単.
語彙 Lesson 135|6: Whatever he does, his movements are smooth and stylish.
In Japanese it does not usually mean intelligent.
語彙 Lesson 135|7: I had prepared, so the procedure went smoothly.
Often used as スムーズに.
語彙 Lesson 135|8: Slim jeans make your legs look long.
Used for things as well as bodies (スリムな携帯).
語彙 Lesson 135|9: This job requires stamina and is quite tough.
Used as ハードスケジュール / ハードな仕事.
語彙 Lesson 135|10: I don't talk about my private life at work.
プライベートな質問 means a personal question.
語彙 Lesson 136|1: I sort my trash with the environment in mind.
It often attaches to other words, as in "eco bag" and "eco car."
語彙 Lesson 136|2: I talked with friends at a family restaurant until late at night.
Casual word. People go with friends as well as family.
語彙 Lesson 136|3: On rush-hour trains there are so many people that you can't sit.
Often used as "commuter rush" or "rush hour."
語彙 Lesson 136|4: I bought a coat cheaply at the department store sale.
語彙 Lesson 136|5: With this software, you can easily edit photos.
It can also mean "soft," as in a soft impression.
語彙 Lesson 136|6: I hear a fun event will be held in front of the station.
Often used as "hold an event" or "join an event."
語彙 Lesson 136|7: On busy days, I make do with instant food for dinner.
Includes cup noodles. Also used as in "instant ramen."
語彙 Lesson 136|8: Wearing a mask when you cough is good etiquette.
Close to "manners," but "etiquette" stresses consideration for others.
語彙 Lesson 136|9: If you skip breakfast, you run out of energy in the morning.
"Energetic" (エネルギッシュ) is the adjective meaning full of vigor.
語彙 Lesson 136|10: My older brother works as an engineer at a car company.
語彙 Lesson 137|1: "Original goods" means items sold only at that shop.
語彙 Lesson 137|2: I chose a new sofa while looking at the catalogue.
Used as "order a catalogue" or "order from a catalogue."
語彙 Lesson 137|3: They had no shoes in the color I liked, so I didn't buy any.
Often combined, as in "color photo" or "color copy."
語彙 Lesson 137|4: I want to study abroad and learn about the cultures of various countries.
Often used in "culture shock" and "culture center."
語彙 Lesson 137|5: On the day of the entrance ceremony, I made a friend on campus.
語彙 Lesson 137|6: After school, I practiced baseball on the ground.
語彙 Lesson 137|7: I had no cash, so I paid by credit card.
語彙 Lesson 137|8: The vacuum cleaner's cord is short, so it is hard to use.
"Code" can also mean cipher or dress code. Here it means the electric wire.
語彙 Lesson 137|9: This supermarket has a section for fresh vegetables.
Used widely, e.g. "toy corner" or a corner of a road.
語彙 Lesson 137|10: The song from that commercial won't leave my head.
Also called "CM." It means ads on TV or radio.
語彙 Lesson 138|1: My younger sister won the piano competition.
For art, music, writing and the like. Not used for sports.
語彙 Lesson 138|2: I wanted to charge my phone, so I sat at a seat with an outlet.
語彙 Lesson 138|3: I decided to enter a Japanese speech contest.
Used for many kinds of events, e.g. "speech contest."
語彙 Lesson 138|4: There's a club get-together next week, so I'm looking forward to it.
A casual word, used mainly by university students.
語彙 Lesson 138|5: These shoes didn't fit and were too small.
Often used as "the size fits" or "the size is big."
語彙 Lesson 138|6: You can check train times on this site.
語彙 Lesson 138|7: My father worked as a salaryman for a long time.
Japanese-made English. "Kaishain (company employee)" is also common now.
語彙 Lesson 138|8: To decide on a clothing color, I was shown fabric samples.
語彙 Lesson 138|9: It's ski season now, so there are many people in the mountains.
Refers to a period, as in "cherry blossom season."
語彙 Lesson 139|1: This restaurant has a system where you order on a tablet.
Also common in computer talk, as in "system error."
語彙 Lesson 139|2: My friend and I like the same genre, so we get along well in conversation.
Often used for kinds of movies, music and books.
語彙 Lesson 139|3: This novel is a series, and five volumes are already out.
Used for books, movies and products.
語彙 Lesson 139|4: I reserved a single room for one night.
Learn it by comparing with "twin" and "double."
語彙 Lesson 139|5: She has a good figure and looks good in whatever she wears.
"Good style" means a good figure. Also "lifestyle."
語彙 Lesson 139|6: I turned on the desk lamp and studied.
Used in "desk lamp" and "gas station." Can also mean spectator stands.
語彙 Lesson 139|7: When the singer came up on stage, applause broke out.
Same as "butai." Can also mean a stage of progress.
語彙 Lesson 139|8: He is a person who says what he thinks straight out.
"Say it straight" means to say it without beating around the bush.
語彙 Lesson 139|9: The room is small, and there's no space to put a desk.
It can also mean "outer space." The "room" meaning is key here.
語彙 Lesson 140|1: "Favorite type" means the kind of person one likes.
語彙 Lesson 140|2: I reserved a double room at the hotel.
"Twin" has two beds; "double" has one large bed.
語彙 Lesson 140|3: I often see that TV personality on variety shows.
In Japan it mostly means a person on TV, not "talent."
語彙 Lesson 140|4: I'm traveling with a friend, so I chose a twin room.
語彙 Lesson 140|5: Today's meeting theme is about the new product.
Used as "research theme" or "decide the theme."
語彙 Lesson 140|6: There was trouble with the plane before departure, and it was delayed.
Often used as "become a trouble" or "get caught up in trouble."
語彙 Lesson 140|7: I'm looking for a dance partner.
Used widely: business partner, life partner, etc.
語彙 Lesson 140|8: Every morning I leave the house in the same pattern.
Used as "behavior pattern" or "the same pattern."
語彙 Lesson 140|9: Vegetables contain a lot of vitamins.
Types have names, as in "vitamin C."
語彙 Lesson 140|10: It was a difficult problem, so I got a hint from the teacher.
Often used as "give a hint" or "become a hint."
語彙 Lesson 141|1: Right now, old clothes are a boom among young people.
Used as "~ boom" or "become a boom." Often short-lived.
語彙 Lesson 141|2: You must not talk about other people's privacy without permission.
Often used as "protect privacy" or "privacy issue."
語彙 Lesson 141|3: Plastic waste in the sea has become a problem.
Also used to show the material, as in "made of plastic."
語彙 Lesson 141|4: My older sister has a bag from a famous brand.
"Brand goods" means expensive items from famous makers.
語彙 Lesson 141|5: This shirt is one-size-fits-all, so anyone can wear it.
A word often seen in clothing shops.
語彙 Lesson 141|6: Inquiries are accepted via a toll-free number.
Often used for company help lines.
語彙 Lesson 141|7: I bought cheap books at the flea market in the park.
語彙 Lesson 141|8: That shop's manager is a veteran and knows everything.
Used in a good sense, for people, as in "veteran teacher."
語彙 Lesson 141|9: I summarized the key points of the explanation into three.
Also used for shop points, as in "collect points."
語彙 Lesson 142|1: Table manners differ from country to country.
Used as "have good manners" or "follow the manners."
語彙 Lesson 142|2: Before entering the movie theater, I put my phone on silent mode.
Often used as "set to silent mode."
語彙 Lesson 142|3: The two were enjoying their meal in a nice mood.
Used as "have a mood" or "ruin the mood."
語彙 Lesson 142|4: I sent a congratulatory message to my friend.
Used as "send a message" or "leave a message."
語彙 Lesson 142|5: Those two have been rivals since childhood.
Not only negative; it can mean someone who pushes you to improve.
語彙 Lesson 142|6: I became the team leader this year.
"Leadership" is the ability to lead people.
語彙 Lesson 142|7: Please follow the rules for garbage-collection days.
Often used as "follow the rules" or "rule violation."
語彙 Lesson 142|8: You need the receipt when returning something you bought.
A "ryoshusho" is a more formal document for companies.
語彙 Lesson 142|9: I choose books that suit my Japanese level.
語彙 Lesson 143|1: cannot hold one's head up before someone
I can't stand up to my wife.
Used for someone who has helped you or who has leverage over you.
語彙 Lesson 143|2: to have a headache over a problem
When I think about next month's payments, I get a headache.
It can also mean a real headache. Tell them apart by context.
語彙 Lesson 143|3: My grandfather is set in his ways and won't try new machines.
Used negatively. The opposite is "atama ga yawarakai."
語彙 Lesson 143|4: I admire my grandfather, who has tilled his field for ten years without a break.
Used for someone you respect. Not used for your own actions.
語彙 Lesson 143|5: I was forgotten about for our appointment and I really got angry.
Spoken style. Often written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 143|6: to bow one's head; to apologize or ask humbly
I made a mistake and bowed my head to the customer.
Similar in form to "atama ga sagaru," but the meaning is different.
語彙 Lesson 143|7: to use one's head; to think hard
This puzzle makes you use your head, so it's fun.
Also used as "a job that uses your head."
語彙 Lesson 143|8: to show up; to drop by
After the meeting, I dropped by my friend's shop.
You don't have to stay long. It means a short visit.
語彙 Lesson 143|9: My younger sister can't resist chocolate.
Used as "~ni me ga nai." Often about food.
語彙 Lesson 143|10: to catch one's eye; to be noticeable
When I walk through town, I often notice the same sign.
Something you see even without trying. Slightly different from "me o hiku."
語彙 Lesson 143|11: When I saw my score, I couldn't believe my eyes.
Used when the surprise is big.
語彙 Lesson 144|1: to look over; to skim through
I try to look over at least the newspaper headlines every morning.
Not a detailed read; just a once-over.
語彙 Lesson 144|2: to catch the eye; to attract attention
At the party, her red dress caught everyone's eye.
The subject is the thing that attracts attention.
語彙 Lesson 144|3: I underestimated the opposing team, so we lost the game.
Used as "underestimate an opponent" or "take an illness lightly."
語彙 Lesson 144|4: My grandmother is hard of hearing, so I speak loudly.
A softer way to say "mimi ga warui."
語彙 Lesson 144|5: When I heard I had passed, I couldn't believe my ears.
"Me o utagau" is for what you see; "mimi o utagau" is for what you hear.
語彙 Lesson 144|6: That clerk is such a smooth talker that I end up buying.
Often used with a slightly negative meaning.
語彙 Lesson 144|7: This country's food suits my taste.
Used only for food and drink.
語彙 Lesson 144|8: to eat or drink; to say aloud
I was sick and haven't had anything to eat or drink since yesterday.
"Nani mo kuchi ni shite inai" means having eaten nothing.
語彙 Lesson 144|9: It's not good for parents to butt in too much on their child's career path.
Used negatively, meaning saying unnecessary things.
語彙 Lesson 144|10: to be free; to have time
I'll be free from this afternoon, so we can have a meal together.
Often used between tasks, as in "when you're free."
語彙 Lesson 144|11: to take a lot of care or effort
Dogs are a lot of work to look after and take a lot of effort.
Also used for people, as in "a high-maintenance child."
語彙 Lesson 145|1: It's busy at year-end, and the shop is short-handed.
語彙 Lesson 145|2: cannot leave what one is doing
I'm in the middle of an important call, so I can't break away.
Often used to turn down a call or request.
語彙 Lesson 145|3: I finally got the popular game.
When something comes to you naturally, use "te ni hairu."
語彙 Lesson 145|4: I'm so worried that I can't concentrate on studying.
Used in the form "~ ga te ni tsukanai."
語彙 Lesson 145|5: When I moved, a friend lent me a hand.
"Te o kashite kudasai" is a way to ask for help.
語彙 Lesson 145|6: to start on; to touch (money, food)
I don't want to touch my savings.
Used for work, money, food and the like.
語彙 Lesson 145|7: He never cuts corners at work, so he is trusted.
Negative. "Te o nukanai" is a way of praising.
語彙 Lesson 145|8: Since I'd come as far as Kyoto, I went on to Nara as well.
Often used in talk about trips.
語彙 Lesson 145|9: to make the trip; to go out of one's way
I went to that exhibition many times.
Used when thanking visitors: "ashi o hakonde itadaki."
語彙 Lesson 145|10: The new clerk was attentive and brought water right away.
語彙 Lesson 145|11: I don't feel like attending a long meeting.
Used as "~ wa ki ga susumanai." The reason need not be stated.
語彙 Lesson 146|1: I thought the room shook just now, but it seems it was my imagination.
Often used as "ki no sei da."
語彙 Lesson 146|2: I get along well with my new coworker, so it's easy to talk to them.
Used as "~ to ki ga au."
語彙 Lesson 146|3: I have a feeling it will rain tomorrow.
Used as "~ ki ga suru." Also negative: "don't feel like studying."
語彙 Lesson 146|4: to be hasty; to jump ahead
Talking about graduation before entering school is jumping ahead.
語彙 Lesson 146|5: to bother; to be on one's mind
The noise from the next room bothers me, and I can't sleep.
語彙 Lesson 146|6: When it's noisy around, I get distracted and can't study.
語彙 Lesson 146|7: Everyone is eagerly waiting for the new game's release.
Used as "kubi o nagaku shite matsu," for something you look forward to.
語彙 Lesson 146|8: to be on a par with
His company has grown to stand on a par with big companies.
Used as "~ to kata o naraberu."
語彙 Lesson 146|9: That hairdresser is known to be skilled.
Used for people with technical skill: doctors, cooks, craftsmen.
語彙 Lesson 146|10: I'm working abroad to hone my cooking skills.
Put the name of a skill before "ude," like cooking or playing music.
語彙 Lesson 12|1: The child is counting on his fingers.
語彙 Lesson 12|2: I had no calculator, so I calculated in my head.
It does not mean "paying the bill". Do not confuse it with 勘定.
語彙 Lesson 12|3: bill, check (at a restaurant); to tally up
After the meal, I asked for the bill.
語彙 Lesson 12|4: to pile up, to accumulate (work, money, stress)
Work has piled up and I have no time to rest.
積もる is for snow or dust that lies on top of something.
語彙 Lesson 12|5: Overnight, 10 cm of snow piled up.
Often "yuki ga tsumoru". For work, use たまる.
語彙 Lesson 12|6: measurement; to measure with an instrument
In PE class we measured our physical fitness.
Used in tests and experiments, e.g. measuring eyesight.
語彙 Lesson 12|7: I measured the room before buying furniture.
"Hakaru" changes with the kanji. Length and size use 測る.
語彙 Lesson 12|8: Before cooking, I weighed the sugar.
語彙 Lesson 12|9: I timed the run with a stopwatch.
Time and numbers use 計る.
語彙 Lesson 12|10: to omit, to cut out, to save (effort)
I have no time, so I will skip the detailed explanation.
Used as "temae o habuku", "setsumei o habuku".
語彙 Lesson 13|1: If you take this class, you get 2 credits.
語彙 Lesson 13|2: You can borrow books up to 5 times a month.
It counts repetitions; different from 数字 or 量.
語彙 Lesson 13|3: This country is about twice the area of Japan.
語彙 Lesson 13|4: Today I reduced the amount I ate.
数 is for countable things; 量 is for what is hard to count.
語彙 Lesson 13|5: On the expressway, drive at the speed limit.
語彙 Lesson 13|6: This bakery has 50 kinds of bread.
語彙 Lesson 13|7: I wrote three letters to my friend.
Used for letters, e-mails and documents.
語彙 Lesson 13|8: counter for portions (one person's share) of food
We ordered two servings of steak and shared them.
語彙 Lesson 13|9: counter for copies of newspapers and documents
I made ten copies of the meeting material.
Newspapers are counted with 部, books with 冊.
語彙 Lesson 14|1: We looked at the sales figures and discussed them in the meeting.
数字 is the written figure; 数 is the count.
語彙 Lesson 14|3: 7 is an odd number and 8 is even.
語彙 Lesson 14|4: In Japanese, 1 oku is a 1 followed by eight zeros.
語彙 Lesson 14|5: Tax was added and the price went up.
The opposite is マイナス. "Purasu ni naru" can mean "advantageous".
語彙 Lesson 14|6: This morning the temperature was minus 3 degrees.
語彙 Lesson 14|7: under, less than (the number itself not included)
"Under 18" does not include 18. "18 or younger" does.
語彙 Lesson 14|8: This town is famous for its rich nature.
Used for good things, e.g. rich nature or a rich life.
語彙 Lesson 14|9: He is very experienced and reliable.
Used as "keiken ga hōfu", "chishiki ga hōfu".
語彙 Lesson 15|1: The universe may extend without limit.
語彙 Lesson 15|2: Often said to customers: "Shōshō omachi kudasai".
語彙 Lesson 15|3: Only some people know this story.
The opposite is 大半 or 全部.
語彙 Lesson 15|4: Used as "taihan no hito". Opposite of 一部.
語彙 Lesson 15|5: A large quantity of garbage washed up on the shore.
Used as "tairyō no ~" or "tairyō ni ~ suru".
語彙 Lesson 15|6: Used positively, e.g. "take plenty of time".
語彙 Lesson 15|7: I examined a huge amount of material by myself.
Often "bōdai na shiryō/dēta/hiyō". Stronger than 豊富.
語彙 Lesson 15|8: In the night sky I saw more stars than I could count.
語彙 Lesson 147|1: Feeling cheerful and light-hearted, in high spirits.
On payday evening, I go shopping feeling cheerful.
Used when you feel light-hearted because something good is happening. 'うきうきした気分' is a common form.
語彙 Lesson 147|2: Excited and eager while waiting for something fun.
My younger brother is waiting excitedly for the new game to arrive.
The feeling of waiting for something fun to happen. It has a stronger sense of 'anticipation' than うきうき.
語彙 Lesson 147|3: Completely worn out and limp from exhaustion.
After the marathon, the runners sat down limp with exhaustion.
Used as ぐったりする or ぐったりと座る. It can be used for people and animals.
語彙 Lesson 147|4: Brooding over something that is already over.
Don't brood over a small mistake; let's stay positive.
Used as くよくよする / くよくよ悩む, mostly in a negative sense. Also used to cheer someone up: 'くよくよするな'.
語彙 Lesson 147|5: Sparkling, glittering with repeated small flashes.
The morning light hits the snow and it sparkles.
Used as キラキラ光る or キラキラした目. Also written in hiragana as きらきら.
語彙 Lesson 147|6: This towel is fluffy because it was just washed.
Used as ふわふわのパン or ふわふわしている, for things that are soft and light.
語彙 Lesson 147|7: Steadily and vigorously, making rapid progress.
When I studied every day, my English improved rapidly.
Used as ぐんぐん伸びる / 上がる, for the speed of good changes such as growth, increase and improvement.
語彙 Lesson 147|8: A lot of people or things at once; a sudden rush.
When I opened the door, wind rushed in all at once.
Used as どっと〜する, when people, things or feelings like fatigue suddenly come or appear in large amounts.
語彙 Lesson 148|1: The mountain road at midnight is silent and a little scary.
Used as しーんとする / なる. Also written しいんと. Also used when a lively place suddenly becomes quiet.
語彙 Lesson 148|2: Lined up in a long, impressive row.
New magazines are lined up in a long row at the entrance of the bookstore.
Used as ずらっと並ぶ, for things or people lined up in a long, noticeable row.
語彙 Lesson 148|3: Just for a brief moment (to see or glimpse).
I caught a glimpse of Mt. Fuji from the train window.
Used as ちらっと見る / 見える. It is for a very short time, not for looking for a long time.
語彙 Lesson 148|4: Vague or hazy; spacing out, not paying attention.
In the morning my head is foggy and I can't think about anything.
Used as ぼんやりする / 見える. It means 'vague' or 'spaced out and not concentrating'.
語彙 Lesson 148|5: Wandering around aimlessly, going back and forth.
I lost my key and wandered around the house looking for it.
Used as うろうろする, when you do not know where to go or walk around for no reason.
語彙 Lesson 148|6: Lazing around lying down with nothing to do.
On days off, I want to laze around in bed like a cat.
Used as ごろごろする, for resting at home doing nothing. Also for the sound of thunder or heavy things rolling.
語彙 Lesson 148|7: Moving very slowly, making little progress.
The typhoon is slowly approaching Japan.
Used as のろのろ(と)進む / 歩く. Often a slightly negative way to say that a car or person is slow.
語彙 Lesson 148|8: Quietly, so that no one notices.
I write my diary secretly so my friends won't see it.
Used as こっそり〜する, when you do not want others to notice. Close in meaning to ひそかに.
語彙 Lesson 148|9: Ants are busily carrying food to their nest.
Used as せっせと働く / 貯金する, for continuing a good activity without resting.
語彙 Lesson 148|10: Unexpectedly (meeting someone); also suddenly falling or stopping.
I ran into a high school friend at the airport.
Used as ばったり会う, for meeting someone unexpectedly. It can also mean 'to fall down suddenly' (ばったり倒れる).
語彙 Lesson 149|1: Please apply by phone or by e-mail.
'A あるいは B'. Formal, written style. Same meaning as または.
語彙 Lesson 149|2: 'In this way / thus'; follows from what was said before.
I practiced a little every day. In this way, I became able to swim.
Used to move from a previous flow of events to a result. Often in the form こうして〜ようになった.
語彙 Lesson 149|3: 'Now then'; used to move on to the next topic.
The meal is over. Now then, let's start the meeting.
Used to change the topic or move on to the next thing.
語彙 Lesson 149|4: 'Moreover'; adds a further, often stronger point.
These shoes are light, and what's more, durable.
Adds something even better (or worse) to the previous content. Almost the same as そのうえ.
語彙 Lesson 149|5: 'Therefore'; the result follows from the previous statement (formal).
Sales have fallen. Therefore, we need to change the plan.
The previous part is the reason and the next part is the result. Formal. In speech, people use だから.
語彙 Lesson 149|6: 'That is'; restates the previous words differently.
My sister's husband, that is, my brother-in-law, is a teacher.
Restates the previous words in a formal way. Close to つまり.
語彙 Lesson 149|7: 'Come to think of it'; introduces something you just remembered.
Come to think of it, I haven't returned the book I borrowed last week.
Used when you suddenly remember something in the middle of a conversation.
語彙 Lesson 149|8: 'So'; states what was done as a result of the situation.
There was a long line in front of the shop. So I decided to go to another one.
Says what action was taken in response to the previous situation. The next part is usually what the speaker did.
語彙 Lesson 149|9: 'On top of that'; adds another item.
I caught a cold. On top of that, I lost my wallet.
Means 'not only A but also B'. Usually lines up things in the same direction (all good or all bad).
語彙 Lesson 149|10: I failed many times. Even so, I didn't give up.
Used when your feelings or actions do not change even though of what came before.
語彙 Lesson 150|1: Are you going by bus? Or are you going by train?
'A それとも B'. Used in a question to choose between two options.
語彙 Lesson 150|2: 'And yet'; an unexpected result given what came before.
I took medicine. And yet, the fever won't go down.
The result is different from what the previous fact would lead you to expect. It carries dissatisfaction or surprise.
語彙 Lesson 150|3: 'For that / considering that'; reality differs from what you would expect.
You run every day, right? Considering that, you don't have much stamina.
Used when reality differs from what you would expect from the previous information.
語彙 Lesson 150|4: 'Even so / all the same'; used with surprise or complaint.
It's cold today. Even so, snow in only October!
Accepts the previous point, then expresses surprise or disbelief.
語彙 Lesson 150|5: He is young. But he has plenty of experience.
A formal way of saying しかし. Used in writing.
語彙 Lesson 150|6: This cake looks delicious. But eating too much isn't good, right?
A bit more spoken than でも. Used in conversation with friends.
語彙 Lesson 150|7: 'Only'; or 'however, just one thing', adding a caveat.
This place is cheap and tasty. Only, there are few seats.
It means 'only', and in 'ただ、…' it adds a condition or a complaint.
語彙 Lesson 150|8: 'However / provided that'; adds a condition or exception.
Admission is free. However, a reservation is required.
Adds a condition or an exception to the previous sentence. Common in rules and notices.
語彙 Lesson 150|9: 'Only / just'; stresses that an amount is small.
There was only 100 yen in my wallet.
'たった + number'. Stresses smallness. Close to ほんの, but used with numbers and time.
語彙 Lesson 151|1: 'In that case'; responds to what the other person said.
Do you have a headache? In that case, go home early today.
Responds to the other person's words and gives a suggestion or opinion, meaning 'in that case'.
語彙 Lesson 151|2: 'But / because'; used to give an excuse or reason (casual).
'Why were you late?' 'Because the train stopped!'
Spoken word for giving a reason or an excuse. Not used much to people of higher status.
語彙 Lesson 151|3: 'However / but then'; something unexpected happens next.
I was fine in the morning. But from noon I suddenly ran a fever.
Used when something different from what you expected happens afterward.
語彙 Lesson 151|4: Let's end that topic. By the way, what shall we eat for lunch?
Used when you change the topic.
語彙 Lesson 151|5: The meeting starts at 9. Also, please help yourself to tea.
Used to add other information to what was said before. Common in notices.
語彙 Lesson 151|6: 'All kinds of / every'; placed before a noun.
This library has books in every field.
'あらゆる + noun'. Means 'every kind of'. Formal.
語彙 Lesson 151|7: 'A certain'; refers to something unspecified (e.g. ある日).
One morning, a foreigner asked me for directions at the station.
'ある + noun'. Used when you do not say exactly which one. (e.g. ある日)
語彙 Lesson 151|8: 'Impressive / significant'; with a negative, 'not a big deal'.
It's not a serious injury, so please don't worry.
'たいした + noun'. Means 'great'. 'たいしたことない' means 'not a big deal'.
語彙 Lesson 151|9: 'Just a (little)'; a very small amount or degree.
Please report even the tiniest mistake.
'ほんの + noun'. Used for very small amounts. When giving a gift, people say 'ほんの気持ちです'.
語彙 Lesson 152|1: My sister swims at the pool every other day.
一日おき means once every two days (with a one-day gap).
語彙 Lesson 152|2: For the first time in (a period of time).
I went back to my hometown for the first time in ten years.
Used when something happens again after a long gap.
語彙 Lesson 152|3: I write a diary every day.
Unlike おき, ごとに has no gap; it applies to every single unit.
語彙 Lesson 152|4: Each; one at a time; in equal amounts.
The teacher called the students' names one by one.
Follows numbers or amounts. 少しずつ means 'little by little'.
語彙 Lesson 152|5: Together with; whole, including the outer part.
You can eat this fruit skin and all.
Different from ごとに (every time). It attaches directly to a noun.
語彙 Lesson 152|6: Half-done; in the middle of doing.
There is a half-read book on the desk.
Attaches to the verb stem, e.g. 食べかけ, やりかけ.
語彙 Lesson 152|7: Freshly baked bread smells very good.
Attaches to the verb stem, e.g. 焼きたて, できたて.
語彙 Lesson 152|8: People who have already paid do not need to come to the counter.
Attaches to nouns, e.g. 使用済み, 支払い済み.
語彙 Lesson 152|9: Leaving something as it is (left on/open).
I went out leaving the window open.
Attaches to the verb stem. Often describes an undesirable state.
語彙 Lesson 152|10: In winter, people tend not to get enough exercise.
Used as in 忘れがち, 遅れがち. Not used for good things.
語彙 Lesson 152|11: The children played covered in mud.
Feels more like something sticking all over than だらけ.
語彙 Lesson 152|12: Full of; covered with (many unwanted things).
My brother's room is full of toys.
Used as in 間違いだらけ, 傷だらけ.
語彙 Lesson 153|1: She was looking out the window with a sad-looking face.
Attaches to the stem of adjectives, e.g. あやしげ, うれしげ.
語彙 Lesson 153|2: Somewhat; a bit more ... than usual.
I bought a slightly large bag.
Used as in 長め, 早め, 多め.
語彙 Lesson 153|3: No matter what; at all costs (with negative: just can't).
Even though I'm sick, I really want to take the exam.
With a negative, it means 'just cannot ...'.
語彙 Lesson 153|4: Also used in greetings like どうもありがとう.
語彙 Lesson 153|5: In a casual conversation, I learned about his dream.
The form 何気なく is also common. Close to さりげない.
語彙 Lesson 153|6: Considering that ...; you see (giving a reason as an excuse).
Since it's my first time, please forgive me even if I make mistakes.
A slightly formal way to give a reason politely.
語彙 Lesson 153|7: Somehow my head feels heavy today.
Close to なぜか and どういうわけか.
語彙 Lesson 153|8: One thing or another; in the end.
He says he's busy, but he ends up playing every day anyway.
語彙 Lesson 153|9: Used to express surprise or strong feeling.
語彙 Lesson 153|10: I didn't have enough money, but I managed to buy it.
語彙 Lesson 153|11: At any cost; by all means.
I must keep my promise at any cost.
Shows strong determination. Close to どうしても.
語彙 Lesson 154|1: For no particular reason I wanted to see the sea, so I took a train.
語彙 Lesson 154|2: That movie left me with an indescribable feeling.
Often used in なんとも言えない and なんともない.
語彙 Lesson 154|3: Let's discuss this kind of problem at the meeting.
語彙 Lesson 154|4: You operate the machine like this.
語彙 Lesson 154|5: I've never had such a hot day.
語彙 Lesson 154|7: He got deep in talk with his friend and lost track of time.
Used in 話し込む, 考え込む, 飛び込む, etc.
語彙 Lesson 154|8: Plural suffix for people (... and others).
The mayor and others went to see the new station.
Used for people. Slightly formal, common in writing.
語彙 Lesson 154|9: Intended for; aimed at (a target group).
This is a Japanese book for international students.
向け is the target decided by the maker; different from 向き.
語彙 Lesson 154|10: These shoes are light, so they are good for travel.
向き is about whether something's nature suits a purpose.
語彙 Lesson 154|11: I have never ridden an airplane until now.
語彙 Lesson 155|1: I intend to stick to my own opinion to the very end.
あくまでも ~ can also mean 'nothing more than ...'.
語彙 Lesson 155|2: To taste; to savor; to experience deeply.
On the trip, I savored the local food slowly.
語彙 Lesson 155|3: To quarrel; to argue with each other.
The older and younger brother are arguing about a game.
〜合う means doing something to each other.
語彙 Lesson 155|4: To act arrogant; to lord it over others.
Even if you are a senior, you must not lord it over juniors.
Used with に, as in 部下に威張る.
語彙 Lesson 155|5: As of now, no problems have occurred.
Used when things may change later.
語彙 Lesson 155|6: To move around; to run around.
The puppy is moving around the garden energetically.
語彙 Lesson 155|7: The president denied the rumor that the company would be sold.
Used as in うわさを打ち消す.
語彙 Lesson 155|8: To put on sale; to launch (a product).
The company will put a new bicycle on sale next month.
語彙 Lesson 155|9: To write down (so as not to forget).
I immediately wrote down the address I heard on the phone.
語彙 Lesson 155|10: I had the letter that arrived at my old address forwarded to my new house.
Attaches before nouns, e.g. 旧制度, 旧校舎.
語彙 Lesson 155|11: I met an old friend by chance at the station.
Also used as 偶然に and 偶然の出会い.
語彙 Lesson 155|12: I read the instructions and assembled the new desk.
語彙 Lesson 156|1: I searched all day, but in the end I couldn't find it.
語彙 Lesson 156|2: To sue; to appeal to; to complain of.
The noise from the neighbors was terrible, so I complained to the police.
Also used as in 痛みを訴える (to complain of pain).
語彙 Lesson 156|3: He kept tilting his head again and again.
語彙 Lesson 156|4: My grammar mistake was pointed out by the teacher.
語彙 Lesson 156|5: 製作 is more often used for making goods in a factory.
語彙 Lesson 156|6: The morning train is so packed that I can't move.
語彙 Lesson 156|8: This shop is closed on Mondays. In other words, it is open only six days a week.
Used to restate the previous sentence in other words.
語彙 Lesson 156|9: Homemade cakes take a lot of effort.
手間 by itself means the time and work required.
語彙 Lesson 156|10: The plane arrived at 3 p.m. as scheduled.
The opposite is 出発 or 発車.
語彙 Lesson 156|11: As for the homework, I finished it long ago.
語彙 Lesson 157|1: To jump into; to rush in.
In the rain, he dashed into the shop.
語彙 Lesson 157|2: To come off; to miss (a guess, a target).
A button on my jacket came off.
Used as in ボタンが外れる and 予想が外れる.
語彙 Lesson 157|3: The government decided to lower taxes.
The opposite is 引き上げる.
語彙 Lesson 157|4: A person who happened to pass by helped me.
語彙 Lesson 157|5: Dazzling; too bright to look at.
The morning sun is so bright I can't open my eyes.
語彙 Lesson 157|6: Just in case; if by any chance.
I prepare water just in case.
Used for unwanted events that could happen.
語彙 Lesson 157|7: I learned how to swim when I was a child.
語彙 Lesson 157|8: In short, you don't want to go, right?
語彙 Lesson 157|9: I have no room to spare in my budget this month.
語彙 Lesson 157|10: There is a service that discounts the fee for members.
語彙 Lesson 158|1: I returned the borrowed book to the library.
A formal way of saying 返す.
語彙 Lesson 158|2: I can't wait for summer vacation.
Used for happy or enjoyable things.
語彙 Lesson 158|3: Please explain by giving a concrete example.
語彙 Lesson 158|4: The talk was abstract, and I couldn't understand it well.
語彙 Lesson 158|5: Between A and B, the former is cheaper.
語彙 Lesson 158|6: If it's tea or coffee, I choose the latter.
語彙 Lesson 158|7: The clerk explained politely and carefully.
語彙 Lesson 158|8: The Japanese-origin verb is 育てる.
語彙 Lesson 158|9: Because of rain, the sports day was postponed until next week.
The Japanese-origin verb is 延ばす.
語彙 Lesson 158|10: I was relieved to be freed from the long work.
The Japanese-origin verb is 放す.
語彙 Lesson 158|11: The employees demanded that the company raise salaries.
The Japanese-origin verb is 求める.
語彙 Lesson 159|1: One's parents' home; the home where one was born and raised.
My parents' home is in Osaka, and I go back every New Year.
