実家 is used by someone who has married or moved out, to refer to their own parents' home.
語彙 Lesson 159|2: The youngest child among brothers and sisters.
He is the youngest of five brothers and was doted on by everyone.
Used for both boys and girls. The eldest child is 長男 (son) or 長女 (daughter).
語彙 Lesson 159|3: Being on good terms; a close friend.
The two have been close friends since elementary school and are always together.
Also used as 仲良しだ. Same meaning as 仲がいい.
語彙 Lesson 159|4: An acquaintance; someone you know by face or name but not a close friend.
I don't have a single acquaintance in this town, so I feel a little lonely.
A lighter relationship than a friend. 知人 is a slightly more formal word.
語彙 Lesson 159|5: A married couple; husband and wife.
We invited Mr. and Mrs. Yamada to dinner.
Usually attached after a surname. The polite form is ご夫妻.
語彙 Lesson 159|6: A bow (lowering the head to greet or show thanks).
The clerk bowed politely to the customer.
Used as お辞儀をする. Unlike 握手, you don't touch the other person.
語彙 Lesson 159|7: A handshake (clasping hands to greet or make up).
I shook hands firmly with the president I met for the first time.
Used as 握手をする or 握手する.
語彙 Lesson 159|8: Being good to one's parents and doing things that please them.
With my first paycheck I gave my parents a trip, to be a dutiful child.
Used as 親孝行をする. The opposite is 親不孝 (being undutiful to one's parents).
語彙 Lesson 159|9: To cancel; to withdraw something decided or said earlier.
Because of the heavy rain, I cancelled the trip reservation.
Used for reservations, orders, statements, etc. Similar to キャンセルする.
語彙 Lesson 159|10: Wording; the way one chooses and uses words when speaking.
In an interview, please try to use polite wording.
Used as 言葉遣いが丁寧だ／悪い. 〜遣い means "way of using".
語彙 Lesson 160|1: The new employee Tanaka asked questions proactively and learned the job quickly.
Opposite: 消極的. Often used as 積極的に + verb.
語彙 Lesson 160|2: Passive; reluctant to take the initiative.
She is passive by nature and rarely says her own opinion.
語彙 Lesson 160|3: Cheeky; acting arrogant and rude when younger or lower in status.
My five-year-old brother talked like an adult and was laughed at as cheeky.
Used when someone is rude toward a superior. It is not a compliment.
語彙 Lesson 160|4: Reliable; making you feel safe to rely on.
My older brother is a reliable presence who always helps me when I am in trouble.
Similar to 頼りになる. Can be used for people and for things.
語彙 Lesson 160|5: Calm and level-headed; not swayed by emotion.
Even when someone says terrible things to you, it's important to talk calmly.
Used as 冷静に〜する / 冷静な人. Opposite: 興奮する, 慌てる.
語彙 Lesson 160|6: Gentle and calm; quiet and mild in manner or atmosphere.
The sea was calm, and a small boat was moving slowly.
Can describe a person's character, or weather, the sea, feelings, etc.
語彙 Lesson 160|7: Selfish; wanting one's own way regardless of others.
He is selfish and only wants to go to shops he likes.
Also common as わがままを言う (to say selfish things).
語彙 Lesson 160|8: Shameless; brazen, not caring even when troubling others.
Asking someone you have just met to lend you money is shameless in the extreme.
Almost the same as 厚かましい. Used negatively.
語彙 Lesson 160|9: To betray; to go against the trust or promise of someone who believed in you.
He betrayed everyone's trust and ran away with the money.
Used as 信頼／期待を裏切る or 友達を裏切る.
語彙 Lesson 160|10: Plain; subdued in color or style, not eye-catching.
This job is not glamorous, but the company can't do without it.
Opposite: 派手. Can describe clothes, jobs, people, and lifestyles.
語彙 Lesson 161|1: To admire and long to be like (a person or thing).
As a child I admired a soccer player and practiced every day.
Used as 〜にあこがれる, for someone wonderful and different from oneself.
語彙 Lesson 161|2: To comfort someone who is sad.
Comforted by my friend's kind words, I felt a little better.
人を慰める means to comfort someone. 励ます is to cheer someone on.
語彙 Lesson 161|3: To run down; to speak ill of a person or thing.
He criticized his friend's picture harshly, and it led to a fight.
Opposite: ほめる (to praise). Usually written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 161|4: To dislike; to hate and not want to be near.
My younger brother hates vegetables and does not eat them at all.
嫌い is the opposite of 好き. 嫌う is used when strongly wanting to avoid a person or thing.
語彙 Lesson 161|5: Advice or a warning given for the other person's good.
I didn't listen to my senior's advice, so I failed.
Used as 忠告する or 忠告を聞く. Carries a stronger sense of warning than 助言.
語彙 Lesson 161|6: To hide; to keep something from being seen or known.
The child hid the test with a bad score in the drawer.
Used as 秘密を隠す (hide a secret) or 顔を隠す (hide one's face).
語彙 Lesson 161|7: To spread (news, knowledge); to make something widely known.
I want to spread Japanese culture around the world.
Used as うわさを広める / 知識を広める. 広まる means spreading by itself.
語彙 Lesson 161|8: To happen to see (someone or something) by chance.
I saw my teacher at the neighborhood supermarket.
Used when someone just catches your eye without your speaking to them or looking closely. Unlike 見る, it is not deliberate.
語彙 Lesson 161|9: To be popular with the opposite sex.
In my university days, the senior in the soccer club was very popular with the opposite sex.
Used as 異性にもてる. Usually written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 161|10: Heartbreak; a love ending without being returned.
The day after my heartbreak, I took a day off from work.
語彙 Lesson 162|1: To gnaw; to bite off a bit of something hard.
The dog is playing while gnawing a bone.
Used as りんごをかじる. There is also the idiom 親のすねをかじる (to live off one's parents).
語彙 Lesson 162|2: In autumn I get an appetite and end up eating a lot.
Used as 食欲がある／ない or 食欲が出る.
語彙 Lesson 162|3: A banquet; a party where many people gather to enjoy food and drink.
At the company banquet, I talked with the president for the first time.
Used as 宴会に出る / 宴会を開く.
語彙 Lesson 162|4: To pour liquid into a container.
I poured beer into my friend's glass.
注ぐ can also be read つぐ. Often used for pouring alcohol or tea.
語彙 Lesson 162|5: To get drunk; also used for motion sickness.
I got seasick and felt unwell.
Used as お酒に酔う / 船に酔う.
語彙 Lesson 162|6: At the morning market you can buy fresh vegetables cheaply.
Besides food, also used as 新鮮な空気 / 新鮮な気持ち.
語彙 Lesson 162|7: Luxury; spending more than necessary on nice things.
Once a month, staying at an expensive hotel is my little luxury.
Used as 贅沢をする / 贅沢な暮らし.
語彙 Lesson 162|8: Salty; having a strong taste of salt.
This miso soup is too salty to drink.
Same meaning as しょっぱい, which is more casual.
語彙 Lesson 162|9: Heavy or greasy in taste; also persistent in an annoying way.
Even when I refuse, he keeps calling persistently.
Used for food flavor and for people's behavior. くどい is similar.
語彙 Lesson 162|10: A line of people waiting; a queue.
To buy the new game, I lined up in the queue from morning.
Used as 行列に並ぶ / 行列ができる.
語彙 Lesson 163|1: To sew; to join cloth with needle and thread.
My mother sewed a skirt for me.
Used as 服を縫う / ミシンで縫う. Also used for stitching up a wound.
語彙 Lesson 163|2: To be scattered about; to be messy.
The children's room always has toys scattered about.
The transitive form is 散らかす. Often used as 部屋が散らかっている.
語彙 Lesson 163|3: To turn over; to turn inside out.
Before washing, I turned the pockets inside out and shook out the lint.
Used as 洗濯物を裏返す / 肉を裏返す.
語彙 Lesson 163|4: To shrink; to become smaller or shorter.
Cotton shirts may shrink when washed in hot water.
Used as 洗濯物が縮む. Opposite: 伸びる.
語彙 Lesson 163|5: A menu plan; the dishes planned for a meal.
Thinking about nutrition, I decided the menu for the week.
Used as 献立を考える / 献立を決める.
語彙 Lesson 163|6: I quickly boiled the spinach and cooled it in water.
Used as 卵をゆでる / 野菜をゆでる. Usually written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 163|7: To cook (rice) by heating it with water.
Every night I cook the rice for the next morning.
Used as ご飯を炊く. 煮る is for cooking side dishes or vegetables in liquid.
語彙 Lesson 163|8: I toasted the bread too long and burned it.
When something turns black by itself, it is 焦げる. Used as なべを焦がす.
語彙 Lesson 163|9: A warehouse; a place for storing goods.
The old chairs are kept in the company warehouse.
Used as 倉庫にしまう / 倉庫を借りる.
語彙 Lesson 163|10: In summer it is hot, so meat and fish go bad quickly.
Used as 牛乳が腐る. 腐った means rotten.
語彙 Lesson 164|1: Spreading of a disease from one person to another; infection.
A cold spreads easily from person to person.
伝染病 is a disease that passes from person to person. A bit more formal than うつる.
語彙 Lesson 164|2: I fell while skiing and broke my leg.
Used as 足を骨折する. You can also say 足を折る.
語彙 Lesson 164|3: A patient; a person being treated by a doctor.
The hospital waiting room was full of patients.
Often used in hospital settings, usually as 患者さん.
語彙 Lesson 164|4: Nursing a sick person; taking care of someone who is ill.
My mother didn't sleep and took care of me while I had a fever.
Used when family etc. take care of someone. The work of nurses is 看護.
語彙 Lesson 164|5: A pharmacy; a shop where medicine is sold or given.
I took the paper the doctor wrote for me to the pharmacy.
A shop where you take the prescription (処方せん) from the hospital.
語彙 Lesson 164|6: The day before the exam, I studied all night with a friend.
Used as 徹夜する or 徹夜で〜.
語彙 Lesson 164|7: To break down; to upset (one's health or balance).
I lost my balance and almost fell on the stairs.
体調を崩す means feeling unwell, not necessarily a full illness. Also used in バランスを崩す.
語彙 Lesson 164|8: To go numb; to have pins and needles.
I waited a long time in a cold place, so my fingers went numb.
Used as 足がしびれる / 手がしびれる.
語彙 Lesson 164|9: Just in case; for now (not perfectly, but at least).
I think I know the way, but I'll take a map just in case.
Used with the feeling of "just in case" or "not perfect, but at least".
語彙 Lesson 164|10: I have no spare money, so I can't buy new clothes.
Used as 余分な〜 or 余分に〜.
語彙 Lesson 165|1: Guidance; teaching and correcting someone so that they improve.
The new coach is teaching the players how to run.
A teacher or coach teaches students or players. Also 指導を受ける, 指導者.
語彙 Lesson 165|2: Improvement; becoming better at something through practice.
I practiced every day, so my guitar playing improved.
Same as 上手になる but a bit more formal. Also 上達が早い.
語彙 Lesson 165|3: Cheering for a team or person to give them support.
Every week I go to cheer for my favorite team.
Also used for supporting activities, e.g. 新しい店を応援する.
語彙 Lesson 165|4: Victory or defeat; the outcome of a game.
The outcome of the game was decided in the last minute.
Used as 勝敗が決まる / 勝敗を分ける. A formal version of 勝ち負け.
語彙 Lesson 165|5: A draw; a tie in a game.
Today's game ended in a draw because neither side could score.
Used as 引き分けになる / 引き分けに終わる. The verb is 引き分ける.
語彙 Lesson 165|6: To lose a game or battle (formal).
Our team lost to a strong opponent in the final.
A bit more formal than 負ける. Used as 〜に敗れる.
語彙 Lesson 165|7: The novel he wrote when he was young is still called a masterpiece.
Similar to 名作, but 傑作 stresses that it is especially excellent.
語彙 Lesson 165|8: An essay; free writing about one's feelings and thoughts.
I like reading essays about travel.
Unlike a novel, it freely records what you saw and what you think. Also called エッセイ.
語彙 Lesson 165|9: The teacher has to write a newspaper article by next month.
A formal word for 書く. 執筆者 is the writer.
語彙 Lesson 165|10: Full; no more room for people.
The morning train is packed, so I can't sit down.
Used as 満員電車. It can be used for both places and vehicles.
語彙 Lesson 166|1: A stay; staying in a place for a while for travel or work.
I stayed in Japan for three years and studied Japanese.
Used for a temporary stay, shorter than 住む. Used as 滞在期間 / 長期滞在.
語彙 Lesson 166|2: Customs; the place at an airport or port that checks goods and people from abroad.
At customs, I was told to show the inside of my bag.
Used as 税関を通る / 税関で検査を受ける.
語彙 Lesson 166|3: To go and meet someone who is arriving.
The president met the guests at the entrance.
The opposite of 見送る. Used when welcoming someone who arrives.
語彙 Lesson 166|4: To go around visiting various places one after another.
In Kyoto I took a trip visiting famous temples.
Used for visiting several places, as in 名所を巡る. More formal than 回る.
語彙 Lesson 166|5: A stop where buses or trams halt to pick up and drop off passengers.
There is a bus stop in front of my house, so it is convenient.
For trains we say 駅; for buses, 停留所. Also shortened to バス停.
語彙 Lesson 166|6: Ignoring someone's words or rules; treating them as if they did not exist.
It is dangerous to ignore a red light and cross the road.
Used as 信号を無視する / 意見を無視する. It has a strong negative feeling.
語彙 Lesson 166|7: A railroad crossing where a road crosses the tracks at the same level.
The crossing bell rang, so I stopped my bicycle.
When a train passes, the barrier comes down and you cannot cross.
語彙 Lesson 166|8: The maximum number of people allowed; capacity.
This elevator's capacity is eight people.
Used as 定員を超える / 定員になる.
語彙 Lesson 166|9: A passenger on a bus, train, airplane, etc.
All the passengers on the airplane were safe.
Refers specifically to people riding a vehicle.
語彙 Lesson 166|10: To meet at a decided time and place.
At three on Saturday, I met my friend in front of the station.
待ち合わせ is the noun. Used as 〜と待ち合わせる.
語彙 Lesson 167|1: A hill; gently rising land lower than a mountain.
There is a small church on top of the hill.
Lower than a 山. Read as おか.
語彙 Lesson 167|2: A basin; flat land surrounded by mountains.
Apple orchards spread across the basin in Nagano.
e.g. 京都盆地. Surrounded by mountains, so the temperature gap between summer and winter is large.
語彙 Lesson 167|3: As I walked along the mountain path, a big waterfall came into view.
Read as たき. 滝つぼ is the deep pool under a waterfall.
語彙 Lesson 167|4: The ground; the earth that supports buildings.
In the earthquake, the damage was greater in places with soft ground.
Used as 地盤がゆるい / 地盤がかたい.
語彙 Lesson 167|5: Offshore; far from the shore on the sea or a lake.
The fishermen went out to sea by boat early in the morning.
Used as 沖に出る / 沖へ流される. The side near land is 岸.
語彙 Lesson 167|6: Okinawa has a mild climate all year round.
Used for weather and climate (温暖な気候), not for people.
語彙 Lesson 167|7: Fog; tiny water droplets in the air that make distant things hard to see.
The fog was thick, so the plane could not take off.
Used as 霧が出る / 霧が晴れる. もや is thinner than 霧.
語彙 Lesson 167|8: To gaze at a view or something from a distance, calmly.
I ate breakfast while gazing at the sea from the window.
Used for looking slowly or for a long time. The noun is 眺め.
語彙 Lesson 167|9: A snowstorm; heavy snow with strong wind.
Because of the snowstorm, the trains stopped all day.
Used as 吹雪にあう / 吹雪になる.
語彙 Lesson 167|10: To be numb with cold; to be chilled stiff.
If you swim in the winter sea, your body will get numb with cold.
Used as 手が凍える / 凍えそうだ. Different from 凍る (water freezing).
語彙 Lesson 168|1: Going on to a higher level of school.
My sister finished high school and went on to university.
Used as 進学率 / 大学に進学する. Often contrasted with 就職.
語彙 Lesson 168|2: Because we moved, I had to transfer to a new school.
転校生 is a student who has transferred in.
語彙 Lesson 168|3: Being enrolled in a school as a student.
Many students study abroad while still enrolled.
Used as 在学中 / 在学証明書. The state before 卒業 (graduation).
語彙 Lesson 168|4: A class timetable showing which class is at which time.
I got my new timetable and checked the classrooms.
A table for school classes. Not used for work schedules.
語彙 Lesson 168|5: A school subject such as math or English.
In junior high school, I studied about ten subjects.
授業 is a class session; 科目 is a category of what is studied.
語彙 Lesson 168|6: Grading; marking a test and giving a score.
The teacher said she would finish grading the tests by the weekend.
Used as 採点する / 採点結果. The one giving scores is usually a teacher.
語彙 Lesson 168|7: Grades; results of tests or classes (also results in work or competition).
My grades were good, so I was able to get a scholarship.
Used as 成績が上がる/下がる, 成績表.
語彙 Lesson 168|8: Being in charge of a job, class, etc.
I am in charge of the Japanese class for international students.
Used as 担当者 / 担当する. Same meaning as 受け持つ, used for all kinds of work.
語彙 Lesson 168|9: Considering the quality, I think this price is reasonable.
Used for ideas and judgments: 妥当な意見 / 妥当な値段.
語彙 Lesson 168|10: Proof; showing evidence to make something clear as true.
To prove I was a student, I showed my student ID.
Used as 証明書 / 無実を証明する.
語彙 Lesson 169|1: To hold (a dream, feeling or idea) in one's heart.
He had held a dream of becoming a doctor since he was a child.
Used for inner feelings, as in 夢を抱く and 不安を抱く. Read as だく, it means to hold someone in one's arms.
語彙 Lesson 169|2: Training; learning the knowledge and skills needed for a job over a set period.
New employees receive a one-month training course in April.
Often used for study after joining a company: 研修を受ける, 研修に参加する.
語彙 Lesson 169|3: A policy; the basic direction a company or person decides to follow.
The company's policy is to increase new products from next year.
As in 経営方針 and 教育方針. Also common in the form 〜する方針だ.
語彙 Lesson 169|4: Improvement; fixing what is bad to make it better than before.
The employees asked the company to improve the working environment.
As in 労働条件を改善する. 改良 is for making things or methods better by renewing them.
語彙 Lesson 169|5: Taking up a new post, usually a high position.
Mr. Yamada became president in April.
As in 社長に就任する. For important posts; different from ordinary job-hunting (就職).
語彙 Lesson 169|6: A business trip; going to another place for work.
Next week I am going on a two-day business trip to Osaka.
As in 出張に行く and 出張中. Unlike travel, the purpose is work.
語彙 Lesson 169|7: Interests; what one stands to gain and lose.
The two companies' interests did not match, so the talks did not come together.
利害が対立する, 利害関係 (a relationship of shared interests). Whether something is a gain or a loss, in money or position.
語彙 Lesson 169|8: Bankruptcy; being unable to repay debts because the money has run out.
After taking on huge debts, the company went bankrupt.
破産する can be used for people as well as companies. つぶれる means a shop or company can no longer continue.
語彙 Lesson 169|9: (Of a shop or company) to go out of business; also to be crushed out of shape.
The restaurant near the station went out of business because it lost customers.
会社が潰れる. Also for objects (箱が潰れる). The transitive form is 潰す.
語彙 Lesson 169|10: In the unlikely event that; if by any chance.
If by any chance you get lost, please call this number.
Usually used as 万一〜たら, about a worry that something bad may happen.
語彙 Lesson 170|1: News reporting; telling the public about events through newspapers, TV or the internet.
The accident was widely reported on the TV news.
Used as 報道する and 報道される. There is also 報道機関 (news organizations such as newspapers and TV stations).
語彙 Lesson 170|2: To appear (in a newspaper, magazine, etc.); to be printed.
The essay my brother wrote was published in the local newspaper.
新聞に載る. It has the same reading as 乗る, so be careful. The transitive form is 載せる.
語彙 Lesson 170|3: Gathering material for an article or program by visiting the scene or interviewing people.
The reporter went to the town where the accident happened and interviewed the residents.
取材する / 取材を受ける. Done by reporters to collect information for an article.
語彙 Lesson 170|4: Obtaining; getting something or information that you want.
This old book is now hard to get hold of.
情報を入手する, 入手困難. A formal way of saying 手に入れる.
語彙 Lesson 170|5: A topic of conversation; something people are talking about or interested in.
That movie is the talk of the town because it is interesting.
話題になる (become a topic), 話題を変える (change the subject). Often used for things getting attention in the news.
語彙 Lesson 170|6: A headline or heading; a short title in large letters that sums up an article.
I read the newspaper headlines to learn that day's news.
見出しをつける, 大きな見出し. In a dictionary, the word you look up is called 見出し語 (headword).
語彙 Lesson 170|7: Rough; giving only the general idea without going into detail.
I made a rough calculation of the moving costs.
Used as 大まかな / 大まかに; the opposite of 細かい. 大ざっぱ can also sound careless.
語彙 Lesson 170|8: Nonsense; random; not true or correct but made up carelessly.
I wrote a random answer, but it turned out to be correct.
でたらめを言う, でたらめな〜. For lies or things done without proper thought.
語彙 Lesson 170|9: Shocking; giving a very strong shock or impact.
The last scene of that movie was shocking.
衝撃的な事件, 衝撃を受ける. Can be used in good or bad ways.
語彙 Lesson 170|10: Worthless; trivial; not worth one's time.
Stop talking about silly things and do your homework.
くだらない話 / くだらないことをする. It is rude to use it about what a superior says.
語彙 Lesson 171|1: Erasing; deleting data or text so that it is gone.
I deleted the photo data by mistake.
データを消去する. Similar to 削除, but 消去 feels like wiping something out completely.
語彙 Lesson 171|2: Sending (an email or data) to someone.
I finished writing the email, so I pressed the send button.
メールを送信する. The opposite is 受信. 送信ボタン and 送信済み are common on screens.
語彙 Lesson 171|3: In the mountains, I can't receive a mobile phone signal.
メールを受信する, 受信箱 (inbox). The opposite is 送信.
語彙 Lesson 171|4: Setting up; arranging a device or software to work in the way you want.
With this app you can set the volume yourself.
設定を変更する, 時間を設定する. 設定 also means deciding the scene or conditions of a story.
語彙 Lesson 171|5: Inserting; putting something between or inside other things.
I inserted three graphs into the report.
表を挿入する, 写真を挿入する. Common when making documents.
語彙 Lesson 171|6: Starting up; getting a machine or program running.
It takes about a minute to start up the software.
プログラムを起動する. 立ち上げる is often used with the same meaning. The opposite is 終了.
語彙 Lesson 171|7: To start up (a program); also to launch a new company or group.
My friend and I started a small IT company.
ソフトを立ち上げる, 会社を立ち上げる. The intransitive form is 立ち上がる.
語彙 Lesson 171|8: I had the phone whose screen cracked when I dropped it repaired at a shop.
修理に出す / 修理する. For machines and tools. More formal than 直す.
語彙 Lesson 171|9: A few; a little; some (not many).
Today seems slightly warmer than yesterday.
Used as 若干の〜 or 若干〜. Formal; nearly the same as 少し.
語彙 Lesson 171|10: Now; by now (stresses that things have changed from before).
Smartphones have now become an indispensable tool in daily life.
Often used as 今や〜だ / 今や〜になった. States change more clearly than 今は.
語彙 Lesson 172|1: Consent; agreeing to someone's request or proposal.
My boss agreed to my request for time off.
承諾する, 承諾を得る. A formal way of answering a request with yes.
語彙 Lesson 172|2: Persuasion; talking until the other person changes their mind.
My brother persuaded a friend who was about to give up studying abroad.
〜を説得する, 説得に応じる. Talking so that the other person decides for themselves.
語彙 Lesson 172|3: To build up; to create something solid over time.
He built a large company within his own generation.
家庭を築く, 信頼関係を築く, 城を築く. Also used for things you cannot see.
語彙 Lesson 172|4: The two got engaged, deciding to marry after graduating.
婚約する, 婚約者 (fiancé/fiancée), 婚約を解消する (break off an engagement).
語彙 Lesson 172|5: To swear; to promise firmly, to a god or another person, to keep one's word.
He lost the match and vowed in his heart to win next time.
愛を誓う, 心に誓う. 愛を誓う is often heard in wedding contexts.
語彙 Lesson 172|6: Grand; large-scale, lively and splendid (of an event).
We celebrated the school's 100th anniversary on a grand scale.
盛大な式, 盛大に祝う. Used for events such as parties and ceremonies.
語彙 Lesson 172|7: To leave something or someone in another person's or place's care for a while.
I left my dog with a friend while I was on a trip.
子どもを預ける, 荷物を預ける, お金を銀行に預ける. The opposite side is 預かる (to look after).
語彙 Lesson 172|8: Struggling hard; putting all one's strength into a difficult task.
My sister, who opened a new shop, works hard every day.
奮闘する, 育児に奮闘する. For working hard at something difficult.
語彙 Lesson 172|9: To grieve or lament; to express sadness or regret about something.
My mother grieved over my grandfather's death and cried every day.
死を嘆く, 不運を嘆く. For showing sadness strongly.
語彙 Lesson 172|10: To feel sorry to lose or part with something; also to be reluctant to spend or give.
On graduation day everyone was sad to part and took lots of photos.
別れを惜しむ, 努力を惜しまない. 嘆く is to grieve; 惜しむ is to be sorry to lose or spend.
語彙 Lesson 173|1: To rob; to take something from someone by force or threat.
The man snatched a passerby's bag and ran away.
お金を奪う, 命を奪う. Also for important things such as freedom or life.
語彙 Lesson 173|2: Fraud; deceiving people with lies to take their money or goods.
He was arrested for fraud after selling goods that did not exist.
詐欺にあう, 詐欺事件. Many frauds use the internet or the phone.
語彙 Lesson 173|3: Investigation; the police looking into a crime to find the culprit or cause.
The police are investigating where the missing jewels went.
捜査する, 捜査を始める. Used when the police investigate a crime; different from general 調査.
語彙 Lesson 173|4: Evidence; proof that clearly shows something is true.
A photo remained as proof that he had been at the scene.
証拠がある, 証拠を集める. Used for crimes and also in everyday talk.
語彙 Lesson 173|5: Strengthening; making power or a system stronger.
At the airport, security has been strengthened as a measure against terrorism.
警備を強化する, 規則を強化する. A formal way of saying 強くする.
語彙 Lesson 173|6: To crack down on; to check people or vehicles and warn or punish those who break laws or rules.
The police crack down on people who drive after drinking at night.
違反を取り締まる, 取り締まり. Done by police and others to enforce rules.
語彙 Lesson 173|7: To come up to; to approach a place or a point in time.
The bus came up to a sharp curve in the mountain road.
交差点に差しかかる. 通りかかる means to happen to pass by.
語彙 Lesson 173|8: Vigilance; being very careful so that nothing bad or dangerous happens.
There have been many thieves in this town recently, so everyone is on guard.
警戒する, 警戒を強める, 警戒心. Also used for disasters such as heavy rain.
語彙 Lesson 173|9: Restoration; something broken or stopped returning to its former state.
The water supply that stopped because of the earthquake was restored three days later.
電気が復旧する, 復旧作業. Often used for utilities after a disaster.
語彙 Lesson 173|10: Still; as before, with no change (often 依然として).
The rain has stopped, but part of the road is still impassable.
依然として〜ている / 依然〜だ. Formal; close to やはり and まだ.
語彙 Lesson 16|1: The Diet (parliament), where representatives make laws and decide the budget
The Diet is discussing a new law.
Japan's Diet consists of the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.
語彙 Lesson 16|2: A person elected to do political work in the Diet or a local assembly
A city assembly member asked a question about the town's roads.
Used as in 国会議員 (Diet member) and 市議会議員 (city assembly member).
語彙 Lesson 16|3: Something you must do by law or rule
Drivers are obliged to have insurance.
語彙 Lesson 16|4: Something you are allowed to do freely, as recognized by law
Adults have the right to marry whomever they like.
語彙 Lesson 16|5: The most important law, setting how the state is run and people's freedoms
The constitution has more power than any other law.
語彙 Lesson 16|6: The idea that citizens decide how politics is run
In a democracy, citizens choose their representatives by election.
語彙 Lesson 16|7: The head of Japan's cabinet; the prime minister
The prime minister answered reporters' questions and explained the new plan.
Same meaning as 総理大臣 (prime minister).
語彙 Lesson 16|8: A national leader elected by the people, as in the U.S.
The president of Brazil visited Japan.
Japan has no president; its leader is the 首相 (prime minister).
語彙 Lesson 16|9: The central body that runs the country (cabinet and ministries)
The government created a system to help families raising children.
City or prefectural offices are not called 政府.
語彙 Lesson 16|10: Before the election, the candidates spoke in front of the station.
Used as in 選挙で選ばれる (to be chosen by election).
語彙 Lesson 17|1: To cast a vote by writing your choice on paper
On Sunday I went to vote early in the morning, then went out.
Used as 投票する (to vote) and 投票に行く (go to vote).
語彙 Lesson 17|2: To resign from a post such as minister or president
The president resigned to take responsibility for the problem.
辞職 means quitting the job itself; 辞任 means leaving a post or role.
語彙 Lesson 17|3: The state of the economy and business; described as good or bad
When the economy is good, companies increase their staff.
Used as 景気がいい / 景気が悪い.
語彙 Lesson 17|4: Money left after subtracting costs from sales; profit
This shop makes its biggest profit in summer.
Used as 利益が出る / 利益を上げる.
語彙 Lesson 17|5: Money needed to make something or do a job; cost
As material prices rose, the cost of the goods also went up.
Used as コストがかかる / コストを下げる.
語彙 Lesson 17|6: Money used as a base to start or run a business; capital
He started a small shop with little capital.
語彙 Lesson 17|7: Having plenty of money or goods; also for a rich mind or nature
This town has rich nature, and fruit grows well.
Used as 豊かな生活 / 心が豊か.
語彙 Lesson 17|8: Plentiful in amount or number; not used for a person's lifestyle
This library has a rich variety of old books.
Used as ビタミンが豊富 / 経験が豊富.
語彙 Lesson 17|9: Lacking money or goods; living in hardship
We build schools for children in poor countries.
貧乏 is a slightly more casual word.
語彙 Lesson 17|10: Prices keep rising, so the same money buys less
Because of inflation, vegetables are more expensive than last year.
語彙 Lesson 18|1: Prices keep falling and the economy weakens
Deflation continued for a long time, and salaries did not go up either.
The opposite is インフレ.
語彙 Lesson 18|2: A country with an advanced economy and technology
Among developed countries, many have falling numbers of children.
The opposite is 発展途上国 (developing country).
語彙 Lesson 18|3: Involving many countries; worldwide in scope
This tournament is international, and athletes come from countries around the world.
Used as 国際的な会議 / 国際的に有名.
語彙 Lesson 18|4: Katakana word meaning "international"; common in school and company names
This town has two international schools.
Mostly used in names; in ordinary sentences 国際的 is used.
語彙 Lesson 18|5: Helping people or countries in need with money or goods
My parents helped pay my tuition, so I could enter university.
Used as 資金を援助する / 経済援助.
語彙 Lesson 18|6: Violence against people to spread fear for political aims
At airports, checks became stricter to prevent terrorism.
テロ is the short form of テロリズム (terrorism).
語彙 Lesson 18|7: Standing on one's own without depending on others; independence
My older brother quit his company, went independent, and opened a shop.
Used for countries as well as for companies and individuals.
語彙 Lesson 18|8: Growth and progress into something bigger or better
Thanks to the development of science, life has become very convenient.
Used as 経済が発展する / 発展途上国.
語彙 Lesson 18|9: Areas outside big cities; or a broad region within a country
After graduating, I want to work in a small town in the countryside.
Also used for broad regions such as 関東地方.
語彙 Lesson 19|1: Things for everyone in society, run by the state or city
You must not throw trash in public places.
Used before nouns as 公共の, e.g. 公共料金 (utility fees), 公共の施設 (public facilities).
語彙 Lesson 19|2: An area within a town with a particular purpose or character
In this district, the height of new buildings is limited to protect the old houses.
Often used with a word before it, as in 開発地区 or 商業地区.
語彙 Lesson 19|3: A rule set by the Diet that citizens must obey
Using a mobile phone while driving is prohibited by law.
Used as 法律を守る / 法律を作る.
語彙 Lesson 19|4: Doing something bad that the law forbids; crime
This town is bright at night, and there is little crime.
犯罪 is the act; 犯人 is the person.
語彙 Lesson 19|5: An unusual incident, such as one the police investigate
There seems to have been an incident near the station, and police cars were gathered.
Used as 事件が起きる / 殺人事件.
語彙 Lesson 19|6: A person who committed a crime
The police found the criminal from the surveillance camera footage.
Used as 犯人を捕まえる (to catch the criminal).
語彙 Lesson 19|7: The share of elderly people in the population increases
As aging advances, there are areas where half the residents are over 65.
Used as 高齢化社会 (aging society).
語彙 Lesson 19|8: The number of children born decreases
Because of the falling birthrate, more elementary schools are closing.
Often said together as 少子高齢化.
語彙 Lesson 19|9: Loss or harm suffered from accidents, disasters or crime
Many houses suffered damage in this earthquake.
Often used as 被害を受ける (to suffer damage).
語彙 Lesson 20|1: Suffix for a kind of business, as in 製造業 or サービス業
Farming is thriving in this town, and some people work in fishing.
業 is attached after another word, such as 農業 or 漁業.
語彙 Lesson 20|2: Treating illness and injury; the work of hospitals
Villages in the mountains have little medical equipment.
Used as 医療費 (medical costs) / 医療ミス (medical error).
語彙 Lesson 20|3: Business of lending and keeping money, such as banks
My older brother works at a financial company, handling money consultations.
金融機関 means financial institutions such as banks.
語彙 Lesson 20|4: Newspapers, TV, radio, etc., that deliver information to many people
That incident was widely covered by the media.
Short for マスコミュニケーション (mass communication).
語彙 Lesson 20|5: A company that makes and sells products; a maker
This camera was made by a famous manufacturer.
Used with a word before it, as in 自動車メーカー.
語彙 Lesson 20|6: The place or overall activity where goods are bought and sold; market
The new product is selling well in overseas markets too.
市場 can also be read いちば for a place that sells fish or vegetables.
語彙 Lesson 20|7: To start selling a new product in stores
The sequel to the popular game will be released next week.
Used as 発売日 (release date) / 新発売 (newly released).
語彙 Lesson 20|8: To devise, for the first time, something new that never existed
My grandfather invented a handy kitchen tool and obtained a patent.
Different from 発見 (finding something that already existed).
語彙 Lesson 20|9: Exchanging information by phone, the Internet, etc.
On the mountain top, communication sometimes becomes impossible.
Used as 通信販売 (mail order) / 通信速度 (communication speed).
語彙 Lesson 20|10: Making goods in a factory using machines
This factory manufactures medicine and ships it nationwide.
Used as 製造業 (manufacturing) / 製造日 (manufacture date).
語彙 Lesson 20|11: (Of a new product) to come out on the market
This company's new smartphone comes out tomorrow.
出る has many meanings such as "go out"; here it means "be released".
語彙 Lesson 21|1: To examine and confirm that nothing is wrong; inspection
Every product is inspected before shipment.
Used as 血液検査 (blood test) / 検査を受ける (to be tested).
語彙 Lesson 21|2: High in level; advanced and difficult
At this hospital, you can receive advanced surgery.
Used as 高度な技術 / 高度成長 (rapid growth).
語彙 Lesson 21|3: Cutting waste to make work or methods more efficient
The company introduced machines and pushed ahead with rationalizing the work.
Used as 合理化する. It can also mean reducing staff.
語彙 Lesson 21|4: Handed down from the past and kept in its original form
At the festival, people dance in traditional clothes.
Used as 伝統的な行事 (traditional event).
語彙 Lesson 21|5: Saving energy such as electricity and gas
This fridge is energy-saving, so the electricity bill is low.
Short for 省エネルギー (energy saving).
語彙 Lesson 21|6: Working by itself without a person doing anything
When night comes, the street lights come on automatically.
Often used as 自動的に.
語彙 Lesson 21|7: Adjusting or fitting things so that they work out well
I adjusted the air conditioner's temperature a little lower.
Used as 日程を調整する / 音量を調整する.
語彙 Lesson 21|8: Delivering needed goods to people or places that need them; supply
The power plant supplies electricity to the town.
語彙 Lesson 21|9: Producing goods such as rice, vegetables or factory products
Fruit production is thriving in this region.
製造 is making goods in factories; 生産 also includes farm products.
語彙 Lesson 21|10: The basic material used to make a product
The raw material of paper is pulp made from trees.
語彙 Lesson 21|11: To deal with and finish tasks or problems
There is so much work that I can't keep up with handling my email.
Used as ごみ処理 (waste disposal) / データ処理 (data processing).
語彙 Lesson 22|1: The function a thing has; what it can do
This app has a function for changing the colors of photos.
性能 is how well it works; 機能 is the function itself.
語彙 Lesson 22|2: Natural things such as oil, water and forests that can be used in life and industry
Japan has few resources, so it imports oil.
資源ごみ means recyclable waste.
語彙 Lesson 22|3: The overall mechanism formed by combined parts; structure
This building has a structure that is strong against earthquakes.
Also used as 文の構造 / 社会の構造.
語彙 Lesson 22|4: How well a machine works; its level of ability
This computer has high performance and runs very fast.
Used as 性能がいい / 高性能.
語彙 Lesson 22|5: Goods made in a factory, intended for sale; product
The new product is lighter and easier to use than the old one.
商品 is what a shop sells; 製品 is what was manufactured.
語彙 Lesson 22|6: 他社 is another company; 自社 is one's own company
Compared with other companies' products, our own company's products are cheaper.
他社 and 自社 are used separately; 弊社 is the humble form for one's own company.
語彙 Lesson 22|7: Machines and equipment installed in a factory or building
This hotel is old, but its hot spring facilities are in good order.
Easy to confuse with 準備 (preparation).
語彙 Lesson 22|8: Each individual part that makes up a machine
Old cars sometimes can't be repaired because the parts are no longer available.
部品 is a part of a machine; 部分 is a general part of a whole.
語彙 Lesson 22|9: A type or model within the same kind of thing
The new-model washing machine is quiet.
Used as 〜型, read かた or がた, as in 小型 and 新型.
語彙 Lesson 22|10: Operating a machine in the right way
This machine is easy to operate, so even children can use it.
Used as パソコンを操作する / 操作ミス (operation error).
語彙 Lesson 22|11: How much work gets done in a given time; efficiency
If you study in a quiet room, your efficiency goes up.
Used as 能率がいい / 能率が上がる.
語彙 Lesson 23|1: A very large body of land surrounded by sea; continent
He crossed to the continent by ship and began a new life.
Used as アジア大陸 / 大陸性の気候.
語彙 Lesson 23|2: A wide land of sand and stone with very little rain
People traveling through the desert carry a lot of water.
Often follows a name, as in サハラ砂漠 (Sahara Desert).
語彙 Lesson 23|3: A wide area where many trees grow; forest
Walking in the forest, the air is clean and it feels good.
Refers to a larger area than 森. Used in 森林浴 and 森林破壊.
語彙 Lesson 23|4: A large structure that holds back river water and stores it
The water in this dam is used for the town's water supply and for power generation.
Used as ダムの水が減る (the dam's water level drops).
語彙 Lesson 23|5: The highest point of a mountain; summit
The rice ball I ate at the summit tasted better than usual.
Also said 山頂. 頂上 can be used figuratively, too.
語彙 Lesson 23|6: The scenery seen from a high place or a window; view
This hotel is famous for its wonderful sea view.
Used as 眺めがいい. The verb is 眺める.
語彙 Lesson 23|7: The movement of water; also the course of events
The river's flow is slow, which is just right for fishing.
Also means a procedure, as in 仕事の流れ (the flow of work).
語彙 Lesson 23|8: Cherry trees continue all along the road.
Used as 〜沿い, e.g. 川沿い, 海沿い.
語彙 Lesson 23|9: This mountain is gently sloped, so even beginners can climb it easily.
Used as なだらかな坂. Opposite: 険しい.
語彙 Lesson 23|10: Steep and dangerous to walk on
A small temple stands on top of a steep cliff.
Also used for a stern expression, as in 険しい顔.
語彙 Lesson 24|1: A small grain from which a plant grows; seed
In spring I sowed flower seeds and watered them every day.
Read differently from 種 in 種類.
語彙 Lesson 24|2: A flower that has not opened yet; bud
Many buds have formed on the cherry tree, so spring is near.
Used as つぼみがつく / つぼみが開く.
語彙 Lesson 24|3: Leaves that have fallen from trees in autumn or winter
Children are playing in the park, gathering fallen leaves.
Used as 落ち葉を拾う (to pick up fallen leaves).
語彙 Lesson 24|4: Things to eat, especially a general term for kinds of food
When food becomes scarce, animals move to another place.
A slightly more formal word than 食べ物. Used in 食物連鎖 and 食物アレルギー.
語彙 Lesson 24|5: Plants such as rice and vegetables grown in fields
This year there is little rain, so the crops are not growing well.
語彙 Lesson 24|6: (Of plants) to grow and bear fruit or grain
Autumn came and the rice in the paddies has ripened to yellow.
Also used figuratively, as in 努力が実る (efforts bear fruit).
語彙 Lesson 24|7: (Of grass or leaves) to grow thick and spread
When the rainy season ends, the leaves of the garden trees grow thick and it gets dark.
Used as 草が茂る / 木が茂る.
語彙 Lesson 24|8: When a stranger comes, our dog barks right away.
Used for dogs, lions, etc.; not for birds or insects.
語彙 Lesson 24|9: The long thin part at the back of an animal's body; tail
When a dog is happy, it wags its tail.
A casual way of saying 尾.
語彙 Lesson 24|10: Light feathers covering a bird; also the wings for flying
I picked up one bird feather on the road.
語彙 Lesson 25|1: The sky is clear with almost no clouds
On the day of the excursion it was perfectly clear from morning, and everyone was happy.
In weather forecasts, 快晴 is used for days with very few clouds.
語彙 Lesson 25|2: Rough weather with strong wind and heavy rain; storm
Because of the storm, all the ships stopped.
Used in expressions such as 嵐の前の静けさ (the calm before the storm).
語彙 Lesson 25|3: Rain that starts suddenly and soon stops; shower
When I went out I got caught in a shower and took shelter in front of a shop.
Used as にわか雨にあう (to be caught in a shower).
語彙 Lesson 25|4: A sudden strong rain on a summer afternoon or evening
After an evening shower, it gets a little cooler.
A summer word; often stronger and shorter than にわか雨.
語彙 Lesson 25|5: I had no umbrella and was soaked by the time I got home.
Used as ずぶぬれになる; common in conversation.
語彙 Lesson 25|6: A huge sea wave caused by an earthquake, etc.
After the earthquake, there was a risk of a tsunami, so we fled to high ground.
Used as 津波警報 (tsunami warning).
語彙 Lesson 25|7: A room that gets plenty of sunlight is warm even in winter.
Used as 日光浴 / 直射日光. 日光 is also a place name in Tochigi.
語彙 Lesson 25|8: The sun rising above the horizon in the morning; sunrise
To see the sunrise from the mountain top, we set out in the middle of the night.
The opposite is 日の入り.
語彙 Lesson 25|9: The sun setting below the horizon in the evening; sunset
In winter the sun sets early, and it is already dark around five o'clock.
The opposite is 日の出. Also called 日没.
語彙 Lesson 25|10: (Of the sun, etc.) to shine brightly
Since morning the summer sun has been shining fiercely.
語彙 Lesson 26|1: (Of water, etc.) to turn into ice from the cold
On cold mornings, the water on the road freezes and becomes slippery.
凍る means water solidifies; 冷える means temperature drops.
語彙 Lesson 26|2: The early-summer season of continuous rainy days, around June
When the rainy season begins, the laundry hardly ever dries.
Also read ばいう. Used as 梅雨入り / 梅雨明け.
語彙 Lesson 26|3: Tree leaves turning red or yellow in autumn
In Kyoto, the number of tourists grows very large in the autumn foliage season.
Also read もみじ. Used as 紅葉狩り (autumn leaf viewing).
語彙 Lesson 26|4: The force of air pressing on the ground and objects; related to weather
When a typhoon approaches, the pressure drops and some people get headaches.
Used as 高気圧 (high pressure) / 低気圧 (low pressure).
語彙 Lesson 26|5: The typical weather and temperature of a region through the year; climate
This region has a mild climate and is suited to growing fruit.
天気 is daily conditions; 気候 is the long-term pattern.
語彙 Lesson 26|6: Being in a natural state, untouched by people
This restaurant uses only wild fish.
Used as 天然記念物 / 天然水. Opposite: 人工.
語彙 Lesson 26|7: Damage to the natural environment caused by human activity
Cutting down too many forest trees leads to environmental destruction.
Used as 環境破壊が進む.
語彙 Lesson 26|8: Air, water, soil, etc., becoming dirty and harmful; pollution
Water from factories is spreading pollution in the river.
Used as 大気汚染 (air pollution) / 水質汚染 (water pollution).
語彙 Lesson 26|9: The gradual rise in temperature of the whole Earth; warming
Because of the effects of warming, summers have become longer and hotter.
Used as 地球温暖化 (global warming).
語彙 Lesson 174|1: A recession; a time when the economy is doing badly.
Because of the recession, the shops in town closed one after another.
The opposite is 好景気 (good economic times).
語彙 Lesson 174|2: Cutting back; reducing costs, amounts, etc.
The company decided to cut expenses by ten percent.
Used as コストを削減する / 予算を削減する.
語彙 Lesson 174|3: Investment; putting money into stocks or a business to make a profit.
My older brother invests part of his savings in stocks.
Used as 〜に投資する. If it does not go well, you can lose money.
語彙 Lesson 174|4: Savings; setting money aside for the future.
I save a little every month for the future.
Almost the same as 貯金, but a little more formal.
語彙 Lesson 174|5: I repay my debt 50,000 yen every month.
Used as 借金を返済する / ローンを返済する. Only for money.
語彙 Lesson 174|6: People who work have a duty to pay taxes.
Often used in the form 納税の義務 (the duty to pay taxes).
語彙 Lesson 174|7: Burden; taking on a cost, work, or responsibility.
The company pays half of the travel costs for us.
Used as 費用を負担する and 負担が重い (the burden is heavy).
語彙 Lesson 174|8: Transport; carrying goods or people a long way by truck, ship, etc.
Fresh fish is transported to the town by refrigerated truck.
Used for carrying a lot of goods. More formal than 運ぶ.
語彙 Lesson 174|9: Improvement; rising to a better or higher level.
I practiced every day, and my Japanese ability improved.
Used as 技術が向上する. The opposite is 低下する.
語彙 Lesson 174|10: Assets; money, land, houses, etc. that a person or company owns.
My grandfather owns many assets, such as land and houses.
Used as 資産を増やす (increase one's assets).
語彙 Lesson 175|1: Leaders; the top officials of a country or organization.
Next week, the leaders of two countries will meet in Tokyo.
Used as 首脳会談 (summit meeting) and 両国の首脳.
語彙 Lesson 175|2: Negotiation; talking with the other side to settle a problem or terms.
I negotiated with the shop staff and got the price lowered.
語彙 Lesson 175|3: A treaty; a formal agreement made between countries.
The two countries signed a treaty to keep the peace.
Used as 条約を結ぶ (conclude a treaty).
語彙 Lesson 175|4: An opposition party; a political party that is not in the government.
The opposition parties oppose the government's new plan.
The opposite is 与党 (the ruling party).
語彙 Lesson 175|5: Discussion or debate; exchanging opinions with others.
A heated debate took place in the Diet about the new law.
Used as 議論を重ねる (discuss again and again) and 議論になる (turn into a debate).
語彙 Lesson 175|6: Testimony; telling in court what one saw or knows.
A person who saw the accident gave testimony at the trial.
Used as 証言する and 目撃者の証言 (an eyewitness's testimony).
語彙 Lesson 175|7: Agreement; both sides coming to the same decision after talking.
After long talks, the two companies reached an agreement.
Used as 合意に達する (reach an agreement) and 〜に合意する.
語彙 Lesson 175|8: A revolution; a sudden, big change in an old political or social system.
At the end of the 18th century, a revolution took place in France.
Also used for big changes in technology or industry, as in 産業革命 (Industrial Revolution).
語彙 Lesson 175|9: Rule or control; governing people or a country by one's own power.
Long ago, this island was ruled by a foreign country.
Used as 国を支配する and 〜に支配される (be ruled by ...).
語彙 Lesson 175|10: Power; the force to make people or a country obey.
I think it is not good for a president to have too much power.
Used as 権力を握る (seize power) and 権力者 (a person in power).
語彙 Lesson 176|1: Discharge; letting waste, gas, or dirty water out.
Factories must not discharge dirty water into rivers.
Used as ガスを排出する and 排出量 (amount emitted).
語彙 Lesson 176|2: Harmful; having a bad effect on the body or nature.
It contains harmful substances, so please do not let children use it.
The opposite is 無害 (harmless). Used as 有害な物質 (a harmful substance).
語彙 Lesson 176|3: Collection; gathering used or unneeded items to take them back.
Every Monday, people in town collect old newspapers.
Used as ごみを回収する and 回収車 (collection truck).
語彙 Lesson 176|4: Serious; so grave that it must be dealt with right away.
The river water has become dirty, and it has turned into a serious problem.
Used as 深刻な問題. 深刻化 means getting worse and worse.
語彙 Lesson 176|5: Improvement or maintenance; getting facilities ready and in good order.
To prepare for heavy rain, the town improved its sewer system.
Often used for roads, rivers, facilities, etc., as in 道路を整備する.
語彙 Lesson 176|6: Breeding; animals or plants increasing in number.
When it gets warm, the frogs in the pond breed.
The opposite case, disappearing completely, is called 絶滅 (extinction).
語彙 Lesson 176|7: Extinction; a kind of living thing disappearing completely.
As the forests shrink, many animals are in danger of extinction.
Used as 絶滅の危機 (danger of extinction) and 絶滅した動物 (an extinct animal).
語彙 Lesson 176|8: To attack; to strike suddenly and cause harm.
Yesterday, a big typhoon struck the town.
Used as 台風が襲う (a typhoon strikes) and クマが人を襲う (a bear attacks people).
語彙 Lesson 176|9: Raising animals; feeding and taking care of them.
At school, the students take turns raising rabbits.
Used for animals. For plants, we use 栽培.
語彙 Lesson 176|10: Cultivation; growing vegetables, flowers, or other plants.
My grandmother grows vegetables in her garden without using pesticides.
Used as 野菜を栽培する. For animals, we use 飼育.
語彙 Lesson 177|1: Development; creating new products or technology, or making land usable.
The company is developing a new car that runs on electricity.
Used as 新製品を開発する. 発明 means making something that did not exist before for the first time.
語彙 Lesson 177|2: Achievements; good results from work or research; a company's business results.
He left great achievements in medical research.
Used as 業績を残す (leave achievements) and 会社の業績がいい (the company's results are good).
語彙 Lesson 177|3: Introduction; adopting a new machine, method, or system.
This shop introduced a new machine where customers pay by themselves.
Used as 新しいシステムを導入する (introduce a new system).
語彙 Lesson 177|4: Inspection; checking one by one whether anything is wrong.
Before a plane flies, a staff member inspects the machines.
Used as 機械を点検する and 定期点検 (regular inspection).
語彙 Lesson 177|5: Efficiency; how much work gets done for the time, money, or effort used.
If you use a computer, work efficiency goes up.
Used as 効率がいい (efficient), 効率が悪い (inefficient), and 効率的.
語彙 Lesson 177|6: Sturdy; strong and hard to break or to get sick.
This bag is sturdy and does not break even after ten years of use.
Used for both people and things: 体が丈夫だ (healthy and strong), 丈夫なかばん (a sturdy bag).
語彙 Lesson 177|7: Exchange; replacing something with something else.
The clothes I bought were too small, so I had them exchanged for a larger size.
Used as 電池を交換する (change the battery) and 名刺を交換する (exchange business cards).
語彙 Lesson 177|8: Heredity; traits of parents being passed on to children.
My eye color was inherited from my mother.
遺伝子 (gene) is the thing that carries heredity.
語彙 Lesson 177|9: Improvement; fixing the weak points of something to make it better.
Farmers have improved the rice varieties over many years.
Used as 品種改良 (improving crop varieties) when changing something to make it better.
語彙 Lesson 177|10: He spent ten long years completing this dictionary.
Used as 時間・お金・力を費やす.
語彙 Lesson 178|1: Scarce; lacking; having very little of what is needed.
This region gets little rain, so water is scarce.
Used as 経験が乏しい (lacking experience) and 資源が乏しい (poor in resources).
語彙 Lesson 178|2: Only a little; a very small amount.
There are only three days left until the exam.
Used as わずかな時間 (a very short time) and わずかしかない (there is only a little).
語彙 Lesson 178|3: Large-scale; very big in size or range.
Next month, a large-scale construction project will start in front of the station.
The opposite is 小規模 (small-scale). Used as 大規模な工事 and 大規模な調査.
語彙 Lesson 178|4: In this town, it is rare for snow to fall.
Used as まれにしか〜ない (only rarely) and まれな病気 (a rare disease).
語彙 Lesson 178|5: Increase; growing larger in amount or size.
The company's workload suddenly grew, so I am busy every day.
Used as 負担が増大する (the burden grows), for a big increase.
語彙 Lesson 178|6: Reducing a burden, pain, etc.; making it lighter.
The country decided to lighten taxes for families with children.
Used as 負担を軽減する (lighten the burden). 削減 means cutting down an amount.
語彙 Lesson 178|7: Volume; how much space a solid object takes up.
When ice turns into water, its volume gets smaller.
面積 is the area of a flat surface; 体積 is the size of a solid.
語彙 Lesson 178|8: Large in degree; a big change in number or amount.
There was little rain this year, so the price of rice rose sharply.
Used as 大幅に増える (increase greatly) and 大幅な値上げ (a big price hike).
語彙 Lesson 178|9: It takes about ten minutes to walk from here to the station.
Used before numbers, as in およそ十人 (about ten people). It means the same as 約.
語彙 Lesson 178|10: Interval; the gap between things or between points in time.
The trees are planted at two-meter intervals.
Used as 間隔をあける (leave a gap) and 五分間隔 (every five minutes).
語彙 Lesson 179|1: Since a certain time, up to now.
I have not heard from him since last spring.
Used as Vて＋以来 or Noun＋以来. What follows is something that still continues now.
語彙 Lesson 179|2: Up to now; the way things have been done or thought until now.
This store stopped the old method and started a new system.
Often used as 従来の〜 or 従来通り. A formal word.
語彙 Lesson 179|3: Around (a time or number); a little before and after.
Let's meet at the station around nine o'clock.
Attached after a time or number, as in 十日前後. Close in meaning to ごろ.
語彙 Lesson 179|4: I take care of my health every day and eat a lot of vegetables.
Often used as 日ごろから or 日ごろの努力. Different from ごろ used with clock times.
語彙 Lesson 179|5: The passing of time; the progress of a situation.
A week has passed since the operation, and my condition is getting better.
Used as 時間が経過する. 経過を見る means to watch how things go afterward.
語彙 Lesson 179|6: A cycle; the time from one occurrence of a repeated event to the next.
The moon becomes full in a cycle of about 29 days.
Often used in the form 〜の周期で.
語彙 Lesson 179|7: Space; an open area; the expanse around something.
Even in a small room, you can make a wide space if you reduce the furniture.
Used as 空間を作る or 広い空間. It feels more like an expanse than スペース.
語彙 Lesson 179|8: After the rain, puddles had formed here and there on the road.
Used as 所々に or 所々で. It means "partly", not "everywhere".
語彙 Lesson 179|9: This medicine is extremely dangerous for children, so please do not use it.
Used for both good and bad things, as in 極めて重要 or 極めて危険. More formal than とても.
語彙 Lesson 179|10: Far away (in distance or time); much more, by comparison.
This year's summer is far hotter than last year's.
Used as はるか遠く or 〜よりはるかに….
語彙 Lesson 180|1: To tilt or lean; to move toward a certain direction (the sun, feelings, a business).
Evening came, and the sun began to sink toward the west.
Used for houses, ships, the sun and feelings. 会社が傾く means the business is going downhill.
語彙 Lesson 180|2: To chop finely; to carve or engrave; to keep firmly in mind.
Before cooking, I chop the green onions finely.
Used as 野菜を刻む, 名前を刻む and 心に刻む. It has three main meanings.
語彙 Lesson 180|4: To go wrong or out of order; to be thrown off (plans, rhythm).
Because of heavy snow the trains were late, and my plans for the day were thrown off.
Used as 時計が狂う and 予定が狂う. 気が狂う is a very strong expression.
語彙 Lesson 180|5: To shave or scrape off with a blade; to cut down (a budget, time).
The tip of the pencil had become round, so I sharpened it with a knife.
Used as えんぴつを削る, 予算を削る and 睡眠時間を削る.
語彙 Lesson 180|6: To tie up with a string or rope; to restrict someone's freedom.
I tie old newspapers up with string and put them out on garbage day.
「縛られる」 as in 規則に縛られる means that one has no freedom.
語彙 Lesson 180|7: To squeeze or wring out; to narrow down (a topic, candidates).
I wrung out the washed towel well and then hung it on the balcony.
Used as レモンを絞る, テーマを絞る and 知恵を絞る.
語彙 Lesson 180|8: To soak or seep in (water, smell, taste); to sting; to be deeply felt.
Rainwater has soaked through to my socks, and my feet are cold.
Used as 味が染みる, 傷口に薬が染みる and 心に染みる. It has a wide range of meanings.
語彙 Lesson 180|9: To draw near (a deadline, danger); to press someone to do something.
The deadline is drawing near, so this week I work late every night.
Used as 締め切りが迫る, 危険が迫る and 結論を迫る.
語彙 Lesson 181|1: To untie; to solve a problem; to clear up a misunderstanding.
I untied the string on the package and took out the book inside.
Used as ひもを解く, 問題を解く and 誤解を解く. It is read the same as 溶く.
語彙 Lesson 181|2: To catch or capture; to grasp the meaning or features of something.
A cat has caught a small insect in the garden and is playing with it.
Often written in hiragana as とらえる. Also used as 状況をとらえる and 心をとらえる.
語彙 Lesson 181|3: To grip firmly with the hand; to hold (power, a secret) in one's hands.
The child gripped his mother's hand tightly when crossing the road.
Used as 手を握る, 権力を握る and 秘密を握る. Also used for shaping rice, as in おにぎりを握る.
語彙 Lesson 181|4: To jump or leap up; to splash or spatter (water, mud).
A fish in the pond jumped up above the water.
Used as 魚が跳ねる, 水が跳ねる and どろが跳ねる.
語彙 Lesson 181|5: To fit snugly into; to get stuck in a hole or trap; to become hooked on something.
Recently my younger sister has been hooked on Korean dramas.
Used as ボタンがはまる, 穴にはまる and ゲームにはまる. Often written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 181|6: To swell or expand; (hopes, dreams) to grow bigger.
When I put air in the balloon, it swelled up large.
Used as 風船が膨らむ, 夢が膨らむ and 予算が膨らむ.
語彙 Lesson 181|7: To bump or crash into; to run into a problem; (opinions) to clash; (schedules) to overlap.
I was walking while talking with a friend and bumped into a utility pole.
Used as 車がぶつかる, 問題にぶつかる, 意見がぶつかる and 予定がぶつかる. It has a wide range of meanings.
語彙 Lesson 181|8: To touch lightly; to mention a topic; to come into contact with (culture, art).
Please do not touch the pictures on display.
Used as 手を触れる, 話題に触れる, 文化に触れる and 法律に触れる. Wider in meaning and more polite than 触る.
語彙 Lesson 181|9: To move something close or to the side; to send in or give (opinions, expectations).
The teacher places great expectations on the students.
Used as 車を寄せる, 意見を寄せる, 期待を寄せる and 関心を寄せる.
語彙 Lesson 181|10: To be blocked or closed up; to be occupied (hands, seats, schedule).
A big tree fell down and the road got blocked.
Used as 道がふさがる, 手がふさがる and 席がふさがる. 手がふさがる means your hands are full. It is the intransitive form of ふさぐ.
語彙 Lesson 182|1: He had come running, and his breathing was rough.
Used as 息が荒い, 波が荒い and 言葉づかいが荒い. It is a different word from 粗い.
語彙 Lesson 182|2: The sugar grains are coarse, so they hardly dissolve even in tea.
Used as 目が粗い, つぶが粗い and 作りが粗い. The opposite is 細かい.
語彙 Lesson 182|3: When I was little, the house shook in an earthquake, and I had a very frightening experience.
Used as 恐ろしい事件 and 恐ろしい病気. More formal than こわい, and it can also describe extreme degree.
語彙 Lesson 182|5: Pure, with nothing mixed in; innocent and sincere.
This juice is made only from pure fruit juice.
Used as 純粋な水, 純粋な気持ち and 純粋な人.
語彙 Lesson 182|6: Poor in quality or humble; (as 粗末にする) to treat carelessly.
It is an old and humble house, but the whole family lives together happily.
Used as 粗末な家 and 食べ物を粗末にする. 粗末にする means to not treat something with care.
語彙 Lesson 182|7: Dull (a blade, pain); slow in reaction or feeling.
This knife has become old and no longer cuts well.
Used as 切れ味が鈍い, 反応が鈍い and 鈍い痛み. The opposite is 鋭い.
語彙 Lesson 182|8: Shade; the place out of the light; the back or hidden side of something.
It was hot, so I rested a little in the shade of a big tree.
影 is the dark shape made by light; 陰 is a place the light does not reach.
語彙 Lesson 182|9: Shape or form; the outward appearance of something.
I baked star-shaped cookies and gave them to my friends.
Used as 〜の形をしている and 形が変わる. Also used for a style or way of doing things.
語彙 Lesson 182|10: A wave on water; ups and downs in a situation; a trend.
The number of customers at this shop goes up and down; some days are busy and some are slow.
Used as 波が高い, 時代の波 and 成績に波がある. 波がある means the level is not stable.
語彙 Lesson 183|1: After I took the medicine, my headache eased somewhat.
A more formal word than 少し. It is often used when talking about change, such as getting better.
語彙 Lesson 183|2: In this town, accidents occurred one after another after the strong typhoon.
Often used when bad or big events keep happening. It also appears as the verb 相次ぐ.
語彙 Lesson 183|3: You should not lend money to friends too easily.
簡単に can be positive, but 安易に carries a negative sense of not thinking enough.
語彙 Lesson 183|4: I overslept in the morning, so, as expected, I missed my train.
Often used for bad results. Close in meaning to やはり.
語彙 Lesson 183|5: The manager warned Yamada, who is often late, over and over, but it did not improve.
Often used with actions toward people, such as warning, asking, or contacting. A formal word.
語彙 Lesson 183|6: Construction vehicles pass on this road so often that it is noisy.
Close to たびたび and しょっちゅう. It is formal and used when there is little time between occurrences.
語彙 Lesson 183|7: The procedure was troublesome and could not be finished in one day.
Close to 面倒な, but also used for problems and people, as in 厄介な問題 or 厄介な人.
語彙 Lesson 183|8: I ran into an unexpected person at the station and was surprised.
Close to 意外な. It can be used for good or bad surprises.
語彙 Lesson 183|9: She suddenly started crying and surprised the people around her.
Close to 急に and 突然. にわかには信じられない means 'I cannot believe it right away.'
語彙 Lesson 183|10: Talking loudly on the train is unseemly.
Used when something looks embarrassing or bad to others. Usually written in hiragana.
語彙 Lesson 184|1: The police continue investigating to reveal the truth of the case.
事実 means what actually happened. 真実 strongly suggests the hidden, real truth.
語彙 Lesson 184|3: Use; purpose (what something is used for).
These boxes come in many sizes and colors, so you can choose according to the use.
Same meaning as 使い道. Used as in 用途に合わせて or 用途が広い, about how things are used.
語彙 Lesson 184|4: Studying abroad was the opportunity that got me interested in Japanese culture.
Often used as 〜を契機に. A more formal word than きっかけ.
語彙 Lesson 184|5: The store manager sincerely apologized for making the customer wait.
More formal than 謝る. Often used as お詫びする or お詫び申し上げます in polite situations.
語彙 Lesson 184|6: He insisted to the end that he knew nothing.
To state your own idea strongly. Close to 言い張る.
語彙 Lesson 184|7: To carry on one's back; to take on (a burden or responsibility).
I walked along the mountain path with my child on my back.
担ぐ is carrying on the shoulder; 背負う is on the back. It is also used as in 責任を背負う.
語彙 Lesson 184|8: To get tired out; to be worn out.
I walked around all day and got completely worn out.
Close to 疲れる but a little more casual. Also means 'worn out' for things (くたびれたくつ).
語彙 Lesson 184|9: To relax; to make oneself at home.
On days off I relax at home, drinking tea.
Same meaning as リラックスする. どうぞおくつろぎください is a polite thing to say to guests.
語彙 Lesson 184|10: To recover; to pick up again.
The economy, which once got worse, has gradually picked up again.
Used for illness, the economy, weather, etc. getting better after getting worse. Close to 回復する.
語彙 Lesson 185|1: If there is something you do not understand, please feel free to ask.
Often used as 気軽に. It means the relationship or action is not heavy and there is no need to hold back.
語彙 Lesson 185|2: I am not responsible, so I am watching with a carefree mind.
気軽 is about being easy to act; 気楽 is about having no worries in your mind.
語彙 Lesson 185|3: I met my friend after a fight, and the mood became awkward.
Used as in 気まずい雰囲気 or 気まずい思いをする.
語彙 Lesson 185|4: The day before moving was hectic from the morning.
忙しい means having a lot to do. あわただしい means being restless because there is no time.
語彙 Lesson 185|5: My grandfather has a sturdy body even though he is old.
Used for both body and mind: たくましく生きる.
語彙 Lesson 185|7: The mayor promised to reform the way the city hall works.
Used for changing big things such as systems, organizations, and society: 教育改革, 働き方改革.
語彙 Lesson 185|9: As the teacher told me, I revised the content of my report.
Used when slightly changing something already made, such as a text, plan, or photo.
語彙 Lesson 185|10: Correction (of a mistake in letters or words).
I noticed a mistake in the email and corrected it right away.
Used when correcting mistakes in letters, numbers, or statements: 訂正記事.
語彙 Lesson 186|2: Very much; considerably (used when guessing a strong degree).
He slept all day. He must have been very tired.
Often used as よほど〜のだろう when guessing a reason. In speech it is also said よっぽど.
語彙 Lesson 186|3: When I actually went, it was far more beautiful than in the photo.
Used when comparing two things: AはBよりはるかに〜. Also used for distance: はるかに遠い.
語彙 Lesson 186|4: All the more; even more so.
I hate the heat, and since the air conditioner is broken, it is all the more painful.
Used as 〜なら、なおさら or 〜だから、なおさら when an existing feeling or reason becomes even stronger.
語彙 Lesson 186|5: When a fire breaks out, please escape outside immediately.
A formal version of すぐに. Used in formal situations such as warnings, orders, and news.
語彙 Lesson 186|6: I have reserved the place for next week's party in advance.
Used when doing something beforehand for later, such as preparation or contact. Same as 前もって.
語彙 Lesson 186|7: No longer; by now (it is too late).
The shop has become old, and customers hardly come anymore.
Used as もはや〜ない or もはや〜だ when the situation has changed and cannot go back. A formal word.
語彙 Lesson 186|9: For the time being; for a while.
I hurt my leg, so I cannot exercise for a while.
Used as 当分の間 or 当分は〜ない. The length of the period is not clearly decided.
語彙 Lesson 186|10: From outside the window, bird calls can occasionally be heard.
A formal version of ときどき. Often used in writing.
語彙 Lesson 187|1: Not at all; not even a little.
Even when he heard my story, he was not surprised at all.
Used as 少しも〜ない. Same meaning as ちっとも〜ない, which is more spoken.
語彙 Lesson 187|2: This test was not particularly difficult.
Used as 別に〜ない, meaning 'not especially'. In conversation it is also used to avoid answering clearly.
語彙 Lesson 187|3: I never imagined that famous singer would come to this shop.
Used as まさか〜とは思わなかった or まさか〜ないだろう.
語彙 Lesson 187|4: Used as めったに〜ない. Close to ほとんど〜ない.
語彙 Lesson 187|5: No matter how much (...); however much.
No matter how much I searched, I could not find the key I had lost.
Used as いくら〜ても. Said when the result does not change even if the effort or degree is large.
語彙 Lesson 187|6: With this rain, the game will probably be canceled.
Used as 恐らく〜だろう/と思う/にちがいない. Said when you are fairly sure for some reason.
語彙 Lesson 187|7: He spoke arrogantly, as if he were the president.
Used as あたかも〜ようだ/かのようだ. A formal word, close to まるで.
語彙 Lesson 187|8: Even if I fail, I intend to try again without giving up.
Used as たとえ〜ても. Used when imagining something that has not happened yet.
語彙 Lesson 187|9: Who on earth is calling at this time of night?
Used as いったい+question word+〜か/のだろう to strongly express surprise or puzzlement.
語彙 Lesson 187|10: I wonder whether the new president can really rebuild this company.
Used as 果たして〜だろうか, expressing doubt about whether something will be so.
語彙 Lesson 188|1: at last; in the end (after a long time or much effort)
I finally quit the company where I had worked for five years.
Can be used for bad or good results. ようやく is for good things.
語彙 Lesson 188|2: finally; at long last (a good result after time or effort)
After practicing many times, I finally became able to swim.
Used when something good finally happens. Same meaning as やっと.
語彙 Lesson 188|3: I forgot my promise with a friend before I knew it.
Often used as つい〜てしまう. Used when you do something without meaning to.
語彙 Lesson 188|4: suddenly; by chance; on a whim
I suddenly woke up in the middle of the night.
Used when a thought or action comes suddenly, as in ふと思い出す.
語彙 Lesson 188|5: It started to rain, so I went into a nearby shop for now.
Also common when ordering, as in とりあえずビール.
語彙 Lesson 188|6: Because of the heavy snow, we had no choice but to cancel the trip.
Also used as やむをえない. A formal expression.
語彙 Lesson 188|7: Even a teacher can't solve this problem. A student certainly can't.
Usually follows a first sentence and is followed by a strong statement such as 〜はずがない.
語彙 Lesson 188|8: The preparations for the meeting are almost done.
A formal word similar to ほとんど. Can be used with numbers and amounts.
語彙 Lesson 188|9: When I contacted him, he had already returned to his country.
More formal than もう. Often used as 既に〜た.
語彙 Lesson 188|10: The reason he didn't come is simply that he forgot.
Often used as 単に〜だけだ or 単に〜にすぎない.
語彙 Lesson 189|1: The morning mountain air is cool and pleasant.
Used as ひんやり(と)する, often when coolness feels pleasant.
語彙 Lesson 189|2: On the snowy morning, the town was hushed.
Used when there are few people or sounds. Also means "quietly, unnoticed", as in ひっそりと暮らす.
語彙 Lesson 189|3: The pumpkin my grandmother gave me was solid and heavy.
Used as ずっしり(と)重い. Also for a heaviness that comes from being full.
語彙 Lesson 189|4: When I got back from the trip, heaps of letters had arrived in the mailbox.
Used when there are lots of things.
語彙 Lesson 189|5: She went ahead with the meeting preparations briskly and efficiently.
Used for doing work or chores quickly and well. A positive word.
語彙 Lesson 189|6: He studied Japanese steadily every night and passed N2.
Used as こつこつ(と)＋続ける・努力する. A positive word.
語彙 Lesson 189|7: My proposal passed smoothly at the meeting.
Often used as すんなり(と)＋決まる・通る・受け入れる.
語彙 Lesson 189|8: She flatly turned down the offer of a dangerous job.
Often used as きっぱり(と)＋断る・言う・やめる.
語彙 Lesson 189|9: While waiting for my family at the airport, I was fidgeting with excitement.
Used as そわそわ(と)する. For both worry and excited anticipation.
語彙 Lesson 189|10: The old dictionary's pages tore and it became tattered.
Used as ぼろぼろになる/だ. Also for a person who is exhausted in body or mind.
語彙 Lesson 190|1: to know many people; to be well-connected
I asked a well-connected senior and got a reservation at a good restaurant.
It means knowing many people. It is a little different from "having many friends".
語彙 Lesson 190|2: to calm down; to cool one's head
My brother, who had left the room angry, was cooling his head outside.
Often said to an angry person as 頭を冷やせ.
語彙 Lesson 190|3: to picture vividly; to come to mind
I can still clearly picture the sea of my hometown.
Often used as 〜の様子が目に浮かぶ.
語彙 Lesson 190|4: to keep secrets; to be tight-lipped
He keeps secrets, so I can talk to him with peace of mind.
The opposite is 口が軽い.
語彙 Lesson 190|5: I got drunk, let it slip, and told a company secret.
Also said as 口を滑らせる. Used when it was not on purpose.
語彙 Lesson 190|6: to be painful to hear (because it is true about oneself)
My mother's words telling me to study every day are hard to hear.
Used when what you hear is true and hard to accept. It is not about an ear illness.
語彙 Lesson 190|7: to hear (by chance); to come across a rumor
I heard that a big building will be built near the station.
Often used as 話・うわさ・ニュースを耳にする.
語彙 Lesson 190|8: My younger brother got into a famous university, and I, his older brother, am proud too.
Often used about family members or people close to you.
語彙 Lesson 190|9: to join hands; to team up
I teamed up with a strong rival and took on a big job.
Often used when companies or countries cooperate.
語彙 Lesson 190|10: to be disappointed; to slump one's shoulders
The trip she had been looking forward to was canceled, and my younger sister was crestfallen.
Often used as がっくり肩を落とす.
語彙 Lesson 191|1: I got angry when I was told something rude.
Similar to 頭に来る. Used about someone's words or actions.
語彙 Lesson 191|2: to make up one's mind; to be resolved
I made up my mind to see it through to the end, even if it is hard.
Used for a big decision. Close to 覚悟を決める.
語彙 Lesson 191|3: to hold one's head high; to be confident
The winning player went home with his chest out proudly.
Used when you have done nothing wrong or are confident.
語彙 Lesson 191|4: to hold someone back; to drag someone down
He is always getting in the way of his coworkers.
Used both when it is on purpose and when it is not.
語彙 Lesson 191|5: to feel satisfied; to feel at ease
I'm the kind of person who can't feel at ease unless I check it myself.
The form 気が済まない is very common.
語彙 Lesson 191|6: to like; to be pleased with
I like the bag I newly bought, so I use it every day.
Used as 〜が気に入る. The opposite is 気に食わない.
語彙 Lesson 191|7: When I ran to the station, I was out of breath and couldn't talk.
Often used after running or climbing stairs.
語彙 Lesson 191|8: While traveling, I wrote a picture postcard to my family with all my heart.
Used like 心を込めて作る・書く・歌う.
語彙 Lesson 191|9: to put effort into; to focus on
The restaurant is putting effort into developing new menu items.
Used as 〜に力を入れる when you put special effort into something.
語彙 Lesson 191|10: to be hard work; to be demanding
Carrying all the moving boxes by myself is hard work.
It does not mean a real broken bone. Used when work or a task is hard.
語彙 Lesson 192|1: To talk something over with each other; to discuss.
I talked it over with my family about moving.
〜合う means to do something to each other.
語彙 Lesson 192|2: To reconsider; to think over again.
My friend disagreed, so I reconsidered my plan to study abroad.
〜直す means to do something again from the start.
語彙 Lesson 192|3: To finish writing; to write something up to the end.
My brother stayed up all night and finished writing his paper.
〜上げる means to bring something to completion. The intransitive form is 書き上がる.
語彙 Lesson 192|4: To run away; to flee suddenly.
The dog ran away from the yard, and it was a big problem.
〜出す can mean to start doing something, or to do something outward.
語彙 Lesson 192|5: To search all over the place.
I lost my wallet and searched all around the station.
〜回る means to do something here and there.
語彙 Lesson 192|7: To climb over; to overcome (a hardship).
She overcame a big failure and became president.
Often used with objects such as hardship, barriers, or anxiety.
語彙 Lesson 192|8: To accept; to take in (people, opinions).
The manager accepted the customers' opinion and changed the menu.
Can be used for both people and opinions.
語彙 Lesson 192|9: My younger sister practiced every day and finally caught up with her older sister.
Used as 〜に追いつく. 追い越す means to pass and get ahead.
語彙 Lesson 192|10: To pull; to drag; to lead people along.
The child pulled at his mother's clothes and said, "Let's go quickly."
Used when pulling with more force than 引く.
語彙 Lesson 193|1: I started the trip with no plan, and I could not get a place to stay.
語彙 Lesson 193|2: The incident of twenty years ago is still unsolved.
語彙 Lesson 193|4: The minister met with company presidents unofficially.
語彙 Lesson 193|5: Japan's total population is slowly decreasing.
語彙 Lesson 193|6: The city office handed out a garbage-collection calendar to each household.
語彙 Lesson 193|7: Midnight; the middle of the night.
There was a loud noise from the next room in the middle of the night.
真〜 means "right in the middle of ..." or "exactly ...".
語彙 Lesson 193|8: If you warn too much, it can have the opposite effect.
語彙 Lesson 193|9: This medicine has the side effect of making you sleepy.
語彙 Lesson 193|10: Putting children's safety first, they repaired the road.
語彙 Lesson 194|1: My grandfather was a famous scientist.
〜者 means a person who does that research or work. 〜家 means an expert or a creator of works.
語彙 Lesson 194|2: A diplomat negotiates with foreign governments.
〜官 means a person who does work for the state or a government office.
語彙 Lesson 194|3: International students earn their living expenses by working part-time.
〜費 means money that is needed for something.
語彙 Lesson 194|4: After the earthquake, donations came in from all over the world.
〜金 means a lump sum of money.
語彙 Lesson 194|5: The road was crowded, so we were late reaching our destination.
〜地 means a place or area of land.
語彙 Lesson 194|6: Many people gathered at the stadium to watch the match.
〜場 means a wide place where something is done.
語彙 Lesson 194|7: I took my child's temperature with a thermometer.
〜計 means a measuring instrument. 〜機 means a machine that works.
語彙 Lesson 194|8: I bought a small printer for home use.
語彙 Lesson 194|9: Before a match, there is always a feeling of tension.
語彙 Lesson 194|10: My sister is studying at school to become a hairdresser.
〜師 means a person with special skills.
語彙 Lesson 195|1: When my grandmother died, the whole family grieved.
A verb made from the adjective 悲しい. The noun is 悲しみ.
語彙 Lesson 195|3: I ran too much, and my legs ached.
Also used for feelings, as in 心が痛む.
語彙 Lesson 195|4: The typhoon came closer, and the rain got stronger.
The transitive verb is 強める.
語彙 Lesson 195|5: As the election comes closer, people's interest is rising.
Often used with words like 関心 (interest), 期待 (expectation), and 意識 (awareness).
語彙 Lesson 195|6: The two talked it over, and their friendship deepened.
Often used with words like 理解 (understanding), 関係 (relationship), and 秋 (autumn).
語彙 Lesson 195|7: Something to look forward to; enjoyment.
A walk on my days off is my pleasure.
A noun made from the adjective 楽しい.
語彙 Lesson 195|8: Thinking about the weight of life, he became a doctor.
A noun made from the adjective 重い. Often used as 〜みがある.
語彙 Lesson 195|9: Before the negotiation, I look into the other side's weak points.
The opposite of 強み (strong point).
語彙 Lesson 195|10: While studying abroad, there were nights when I felt lonely.
Adding さ to an adjective makes a noun.
語彙 Lesson 27|1: After running, my whole body was wet with sweat.
Used as in 全身がだるい (the whole body feels sluggish).
語彙 Lesson 27|2: I run every morning to build muscle.
Often used as 筋肉がつく / 筋肉をつける (build muscle).
語彙 Lesson 27|3: A baby's skin is very soft.
A bit more formal than 肌 (hada); common in medical contexts.
語彙 Lesson 27|4: I fell and broke a bone in my leg.
骨が折れる also means that something is very hard work.
語彙 Lesson 27|5: This is the body organ, not the feeling-related 心 (kokoro).
語彙 Lesson 27|6: Every morning I take my temperature before leaving home.
Typical forms: 体温を測る, 体温が高い.
語彙 Lesson 27|7: When I smile, wrinkles form around my eyes.
Also used for creases in clothes or paper.
語彙 Lesson 27|8: My father shaves his beard every morning before going out.
Used as ひげをそる (shave) / ひげを生やす (grow a beard).
語彙 Lesson 27|9: After turning thirty, my white hairs increased a little.
Read しらが, not はくはつ.
語彙 Lesson 27|10: During class, a big yawn came out before I knew it.
Used as あくびをする / あくびが出る.
