語彙 Lesson 28|1: Seeing my test results, I let out a sigh.
Used as ため息をつく or ため息が出る.
語彙 Lesson 28|2: After running up the stairs, I was out of breath.
Used in phrases like 息をする, 息が切れる, 息をのむ.
語彙 Lesson 28|3: If you breathe slowly, you feel calmer.
息 is everyday speech; 呼吸 is slightly more formal.
語彙 Lesson 28|4: I got out of the pool and took a big breath.
息を吸う is the opposite of 息を吐く. Also used for smoking.
語彙 Lesson 28|5: I breathed out deeply and then started reading the questions.
息を吐く = exhale. Also means to vomit.
語彙 Lesson 28|6: My friend is pregnant and is due to give birth next spring.
Used as 妊娠する / 妊娠している.
語彙 Lesson 28|7: My brother has grown, and is ten centimeters taller than last year.
Also used for the growth of companies and economies.
語彙 Lesson 28|8: That delicate chair looks like it would break if a heavy person sat on it.
Unlike 細い, it carries a feeling of looking fragile.
語彙 Lesson 28|9: These shoes are a little tight, so I had them exchanged for a bigger size.
Also means harsh or demanding, as in きつい仕事 / きつい言い方.
語彙 Lesson 28|10: People with a peanut allergy should not eat this snack.
Common forms: 〜アレルギー, アレルギーがある.
語彙 Lesson 29|1: My hay fever is bad in spring, and I can't do without a mask.
Used as 花粉症になる / 花粉症の薬.
語彙 Lesson 29|2: On cold mornings, I sneeze when I go outside.
Used as くしゃみをする / くしゃみが出る.
語彙 Lesson 29|3: to spread; to be in fashion
A new style of hat is popular among young people in front of the station.
The noun is 流行 (りゅうこう/はやり); the verb is read はやる.
語彙 Lesson 29|4: This table has a lot of small scratches.
Used for objects as well as the body.
語彙 Lesson 29|5: The scar from the operation has not faded even after six months.
Used as 傷あとが残る / 傷あとが消える.
語彙 Lesson 29|6: I washed the wound with water and then applied medicine.
傷口 is the open wound; 傷あと is what remains after healing.
語彙 Lesson 29|7: to get hurt; to be hurt emotionally
I was lied to, and I was hurt deeply.
傷つく: oneself gets hurt. 傷つける: you hurt someone or something.
語彙 Lesson 29|8: Please be careful not to injure your finger with the knife.
傷つく is for oneself; 傷つける is done to someone or something.
語彙 Lesson 29|9: to be bitten by a mosquito
I was bitten by mosquitoes last night, and my legs itch.
The base form is 蚊にさす, but it is normally used as 蚊にさされる.
語彙 Lesson 30|1: I fell, and my knee swelled up a lot.
Used as 顔が腫れる / 目が腫れる.
語彙 Lesson 30|2: My tooth hurts, so I made an appointment at the dental department.
Examples: 内科 (internal medicine), 外科 (surgery), 歯科 (dentistry).
語彙 Lesson 30|3: When traveling, I worry about the hygiene of the water.
Also common as 衛生的な and 衛生管理.
語彙 Lesson 30|4: I got a fever while traveling and saw a local doctor.
かかる here means to be seen by a doctor; the subject is the patient.
語彙 Lesson 30|5: In winter, the whole family caught the flu.
病気にかかる means to come down with an illness.
語彙 Lesson 30|6: Before the examination, the nurse took my temperature.
After 診察, the illness is decided in the 診断.
語彙 Lesson 30|7: The doctor's diagnosis showed it was mild gastritis.
Used as 診断を受ける / 診断書.
語彙 Lesson 30|8: Fever and a cough are typical symptoms of a cold.
Used as 症状が出る / 症状が軽い・重い.
語彙 Lesson 30|9: I went to the dentist three times for cavity treatment.
Used as 治療を受ける / 治療する.
語彙 Lesson 31|1: Please buy a ticket before boarding.
Opposite of 下車. Used in 乗車券, 乗車口.
語彙 Lesson 31|2: If you transfer to an express at this station, you arrive ten minutes sooner.
Used as AからBに乗り換える. The noun is 乗り換え.
語彙 Lesson 31|3: I slept soundly and rode all the way to the last stop.
Nearly the same as 乗り過ごす. Different from 乗り越える (overcome).
語彙 Lesson 31|4: I was tired and fell asleep, so I missed my station.
Often used when you fall asleep and cannot get off.
語彙 Lesson 31|5: to change and connect (to a destination)
I took a bus and a train in connection and arrived in three hours.
Often used for long trips and flights; stresses connecting legs of a journey.
語彙 Lesson 31|6: The rain made me leave home late, and I missed the bus.
Also used figuratively, e.g. missing a trend.
語彙 Lesson 31|7: I got off at Kyoto Station and took a taxi.
Opposite of 乗車. Common in announcements and writing.
語彙 Lesson 31|8: I overtook the truck that was running ahead.
追い付く only reaches; 追い越す goes ahead.
語彙 Lesson 31|9: I left late, but caught up with my friend in front of the station.
Used as Aに追い付く; also for study or skills.
語彙 Lesson 32|1: I passed my teacher at the station and greeted him.
Also used when two people miss each other despite plans.
語彙 Lesson 32|2: If you turn right at the next intersection, you reach the station.
語彙 Lesson 32|3: The car ahead turned left, so I turned after it.
語彙 Lesson 32|4: Express trains pass through small stations.
Also used for passing an exam or screening.
語彙 Lesson 32|5: Department stores and banks line the main street.
語彙 Lesson 32|6: Please do not put your bag in the aisle.
Also used for the aisle between seats on planes and trains.
語彙 Lesson 32|7: It's dangerous to step onto the roadway, so let's walk on the sidewalk.
語彙 Lesson 32|8: Cars must stop at a pedestrian crossing.
語彙 Lesson 32|9: I took a shortcut and ended up getting lost.
Opposite of 回り道 / 遠回り.
語彙 Lesson 33|1: The road was under construction, so I went home by a detour.
Almost the same meaning as 遠回り.
語彙 Lesson 33|2: The rain was heavy and I couldn't cross the bridge, so I went a long way round.
Used as 遠回りする / 遠回りになる. Opposite of 近道.
語彙 Lesson 33|3: To my office, the private railway is cheaper than JR.
語彙 Lesson 33|4: Because of snow, the trains going north are stopped.
A bit more formal than 電車; also used for long-distance trains.
語彙 Lesson 33|5: Even in the morning rush, the last car is a little emptier.
語彙 Lesson 33|6: It is very dangerous to go onto the tracks.
語彙 Lesson 33|7: There was an accident in which a train derailed because of the typhoon.
Also used when a conversation goes off topic.
語彙 Lesson 33|8: It is convenient to go to the airport by monorail.
語彙 Lesson 33|9: How much is a round trip to Tokyo by Shinkansen?
Used in 往復切符. Opposite of 片道.
語彙 Lesson 34|1: It takes twenty minutes one way to the station.
Used in 片道切符. Opposite of 往復.
語彙 Lesson 34|2: On this section, trains are delayed because of construction.
Used in 乗車区間 and 運転区間.
語彙 Lesson 34|3: It was canceled, so we will refund the price.
The noun is 払い戻し.
語彙 Lesson 34|4: The game was canceled because of rain, and the admission fee was refunded.
The verb is 払い戻す.
語彙 Lesson 34|5: The last train leaves at midnight.
Used in 最終電車, 最終回, 最終日. A bit more formal than 最後.
語彙 Lesson 34|6: Parking is prohibited in front of this shop.
Used in 駐車場 and 駐車禁止.
語彙 Lesson 34|7: During consecutive holidays, the expressways get very congested.
Used as 混雑する / 混雑した電車.
語彙 Lesson 34|8: I went to the station to see my friend off.
The verb is 見送る. Opposite of 出迎え.
語彙 Lesson 34|9: I waited in front of the company to meet the president.
The verb is 出迎える. Opposite of 見送り.
語彙 Lesson 35|1: Please walk on the right side of the road.
Attached after other words: 右側, 内側, 窓側.
語彙 Lesson 35|2: A big tree stands in the center of the square.
Also used in names such as 中央図書館 and 中央線.
語彙 Lesson 35|3: In the center of the town, there is an old temple.
Also means the core, as in 〜を中心に. 中央 is the middle of a place.
語彙 Lesson 35|4: Seen from the front, this building is symmetrical.
語彙 Lesson 35|5: A new bookstore opened across from the post office.
斜め向かい is slightly off from directly opposite.
語彙 Lesson 35|7: Don't put the glass on the edge of the table.
隅 is an inner corner; 端 is the outer edge.
語彙 Lesson 35|8: The corner of the box is a little crushed.
隅から隅まで means every part.
語彙 Lesson 35|9: There is a supermarket halfway between the school and the station.
Also means midway in time, as in 中間テスト.
語彙 Lesson 35|10: He is sitting in the seat directly behind me.
Used in 真上, 真下, 真ん中, 真っ赤. The reading changes to ま, まっ, まん.
語彙 Lesson 36|1: Please write the address on the front of the envelope.
Opposite of 裏. 表 can also be read ひょう (table).
語彙 Lesson 36|2: There are questions on the back of the paper, too.
Opposite of 表. Used in 裏口 and 裏道.
語彙 Lesson 36|3: This village is surrounded by high mountains.
The base form is 囲む. Used as Aに囲まれている.
語彙 Lesson 36|4: to be in contact with, adjoin
My house shares a wall with the neighbor's.
The base form is 接する. Used as AがBに接している.
語彙 Lesson 36|5: The living room faces south and is very bright.
The base form is 面する. Used as AがBに面している.
語彙 Lesson 36|6: I walk along the narrow road that runs beside the railway every day.
The base form is 沿う. Often seen as 川に沿って歩く.
語彙 Lesson 36|7: The hot spring is located at the foot of the mountain.
The base form is 位置する. Common as 〜に位置している.
語彙 Lesson 36|8: I went down a road I didn't know, and it was a dead end.
語彙 Lesson 36|9: There is an emergency exit at the end of the corridor.
Common in giving directions, e.g. 突き当たりを右に曲がる.
漢字 Unit 10-1|1: left and right; (as a verb) to influence or decide something

Look left and right before crossing the road.
The weather decides the result of the match.
漢字 Unit 10-1|2: A distinctive feature of this university is that it has many international students.
"色" is read "shoku" here, not "shiki". Similar in meaning to "tokuchou".
漢字 Unit 10-1|3: He complains about his work every day.
Often used as "monku o iu" (to complain). It is not read "bunku".
漢字 Unit 10-1|4: nausea; feeling sick to the stomach
I got carsick and felt nauseous.
Often used as "hakike ga suru". The last sound is "ke", not "ge".
漢字 Unit 10-1|5: We will make the design of the company uniforms uniform.
漢字 Unit 10-1|6: The young men of the town helped with the festival.
"青" is read "ao" or "sei". Do not confuse it with 清, 晴, 静.
漢字 Unit 10-1|7: I eat breakfast at seven every morning.
"朝" is also read "chou". Learn it with "chuushoku" (lunch) and "yuushoku" (dinner).
漢字 Unit 10-1|8: I ate fresh seafood near the sea.
Often used as "gyokairui" or "gyokai ryouri". "魚" is read "gyo".
漢字 Unit 10-2|1: I work every day to pay back my debt.
"借" is usually "shaku", but here it becomes "shak-" with a small "tsu".
漢字 Unit 10-2|2: "次第" is read "shidai". Do not confuse it with "jidai" (era).
漢字 Unit 10-2|3: I worked out ways to make the food taste better.
"工" is usually "kou", but is read "ku" in this word. A special reading.
漢字 Unit 10-2|4: His ideas had an influence on many people.
"shikou" means the act of thinking. "shisou" means a person's core ideas. Mind the reading.
漢字 Unit 10-2|5: I work at a shop that buys and sells used cars.
Both "売" and "買" are read "bai". Say the same sound twice.
漢字 Unit 10-2|6: I get up at six every morning.
"起" is read "ki". The opposite word is "shuushin" (going to bed).
漢字 Unit 10-2|7: There was a party to welcome the new students.
"迎" is read "gei" here (kun-yomi: "mukaeru"). "Kangeikai" (welcome party) is common.
漢字 Unit 10-3|1: The temperature dropped as night came.
漢字 Unit 10-3|2: We aim for a society where men and women can work equally.
"平" is read "byou", not "hei". A special reading.
漢字 Unit 10-3|3:
He is an honest person.
To be honest, I am against it.
Often used as "shoujiki ni iu to" (to be honest). "正" is read "shou".
漢字 Unit 10-3|4: I will go back to Nepal via Tokyo.
Used as "~ o keiyu shite". Read "yu" short, not "yuu".
漢字 Unit 10-3|5: Used as "koukishin ga tsuyoi" or "koukishin o motsu". "好" is read "kou".
漢字 Unit 10-3|6: You cannot eat or drink inside the library.
"飲" is read "in". Often seen as "inshokuten" (restaurant) and "inshoku kinshi" (no food or drink).
漢字 Unit 10-3|7: Reading the classics lets you learn about life in the past.
"古" is read "ko". Also used in "koten bungaku" (classical literature) and "koten ongaku".
漢字 Unit 10-3|8: Before the match, I reviewed my weak points.
The opposite is "chousho" (strong point). "弱" is read "jaku".
漢字 Unit 10-4|1: I reflect my face in the mirror.
Do not confuse it with 写す (copy, photograph). "Utsuru" is the intransitive form.
漢字 Unit 10-4|2: My grandmother likes to talk about the old days.
A little more formal than "hanasu". "語" is also read "go" (nihongo).
漢字 Unit 10-4|3: I work every day to support my family.
Used for objects and also for a person's life or feelings. The noun is "sasae".
漢字 Unit 10-4|4: to be filled; to become full
On nights when the moon is full, it is bright outside.
Used as "~ ni michiru". The transitive form is "mitasu". "満" is also read "man".
漢字 Unit 10-4|5: to be taught; to learn from someone
It is fun to learn Japanese from my teacher.
Used as "~ ni (kara) osowaru". The okurigana is different from "oshieru".
漢字 Unit 10-4|6: In this experiment, we use a new method.
Common in writing and explanations. "用" is also read "you" (riyou).
漢字 Unit 10-4|7: I plan to study economics at university.
Similar to "narau" and "osowaru". "学" is also read "gaku".
漢字 Unit 10-4|8: I dilute strong tea with water.
Learn it with "usui" and "usumaru". The opposite idea is "koku suru".
漢字 Unit 10-5|1: A letter came from my mother in my hometown.
"便" is also read "ben" or "bin" (benri, yuubin). This word uses the kun-yomi "tayori".
漢字 Unit 10-5|3: The children are playing in the field.
"原" is read "hara", without the voiced sound "bara".
漢字 Unit 10-5|4: The world is becoming more and more convenient.
"世" is read "yo", not "se". Close in meaning to "shakai" and "seken".
漢字 Unit 10-5|5: There is an exam in the middle of next month.
Used as "tsuki no nakaba" or "nakaba akirameru". It can describe a time or a state.
漢字 Unit 10-5|6: He is a former soccer player.
Used as "moto + noun", like "moto shachou". "元" is also read "gen" or "gan".
漢字 Unit 10-5|7: Often placed at the start of a sentence as "saiwai, ~". Same kanji as "shiawase".
漢字 Unit 10-5|8: I set out on a trip alone.
The "旅" of "ryokou". Alone it is read "tabi". Often used as "tabi ni deru".
漢字 Unit 1-1|1: The humidity in the room is high, and it is muggy.
“湿” is read “shitsu” and “度” is read “do”. It is also used in “湿気 (shikke)”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|2: It is cool on the mountain even in summer.
漢字 Unit 1-1|3: In winter I sleep under two layers of bedding.
“布” is “fu” and “団” is read “ton” here (not “dan”).
漢字 Unit 1-1|4: Kyoto is famous for its autumn leaves.
“紅葉” can also be read “momiji”. Here “紅” is “kou” and “葉” is “you”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|5: The child touched the insect with curiosity.
“触る” is “sawaru” and “触れる” is “fureru”. The okurigana changes the reading.
漢字 Unit 1-1|6: to become rough; to get chapped
In winter my hands get chapped and hurt.
“荒” is read “ara-i” and “a-reru”. “荒れる” is not “areru” with “ara”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|7: I am saving on food costs because of my move.
“節” is read “setsu”. It is also used in “季節” and “調節”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|8: We moved to the meeting room by elevator.
“移” is read “i”. The kun-readings are “utsu-ru” and “utsu-su”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|9: Before the presentation I lacked confidence and was worried.
“自” is read “ji”. There is also the kun-reading “mizuka-ra”.
漢字 Unit 1-1|10: I put on sunscreen to protect my skin.
“肌” is read “hada”. It is also used in “肌色 (hadairo)”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|1: Every morning, the first thing I do after getting up is the laundry.
“洗濯” is read “sentaku”. It sounds the same as “選択”, so tell them apart by meaning.
漢字 Unit 1-2|2: I dry vegetables to keep them for a long time.
“乾” is “kan” and “燥” is “sou”. Learn this on-reading separately from “kawaku”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|3: My feet hurt after I put on my new shoes.
“靴” is read “kutsu”. After another character, as in “長靴”, it becomes “gutsu”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|4: I polished the window glass until it was clean.
“磨” is read “miga-ku”, the same as “miga” in “歯磨き”. The on-reading is “ma”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|5: I changed into a yukata at the inn and took a bath in the hot spring.
“浴衣” has a special reading. “浴” is “yoku” and “衣” is “i”, but the word is read “yukata”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|6: I wrapped the baby in a soft blanket.
“毛” is read “mou” and “布” is read “fu”. “毛” can also be read “ke”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|7: In summer I wear a hat when I play outside.
“帽” is read “bou”. It is mostly used in “帽子”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|8: to dry (in the sun or wind); to hang out
I salt the fish, dry it, and then eat it.
“干” is read “ho-su” and “kan”. Be careful: it looks like “千”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|9: A needle pricked my finger and it bled.
“針” is read “hari”. The on-reading is “shin”, as in “方針”.
漢字 Unit 1-2|10: “綿” is read “men” and “wata”. “木綿” is read “momen”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|1: If you move from the city to the suburbs, commuting takes more time.
“郊外” is read “kougai”. It sounds the same as “公害”, so tell them apart by meaning.
漢字 Unit 1-3|2: I dozed off in class and was warned by the teacher.
“居” is read “i” (as in “居る”). It is not read “kyo” here.
漢字 Unit 1-3|3: My father, who works in construction, gets up early.
“築” is read “chiku” and is also used in “新築” and “改築”. “建設” sounds similar but is a different word.
漢字 Unit 1-3|4: I replaced the tatami in the room with new ones.
“畳” is read “tatami”. It is “jou” when counting room size (六畳), and the verb is “畳む”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|5: Big wooden pillars support the roof.
“柱” is read “hashira”. The on-reading is “chuu”, as in “電柱”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|6: Even a small room can be used well with some ideas.
“狭” is read “sema-i”. The opposite is “広い”. The on-reading is “kyou”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|7: I can hear sounds from the next room through the wall.
“壁” is read “kabe”. The on-reading is “heki”, as in “壁画”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|8: I sat on the floor and played a game with my friend.
“床” is read “yuka”. It can also be read “toko” (床屋), and the on-reading is “shou”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|9: A dog is running around in the large garden.
“庭” is read “niwa”. The on-reading is “tei”, as in “家庭” and “校庭”.
漢字 Unit 1-3|10: I bought wooden materials to make furniture.
“材” is read “zai”. It is also used in “木材” and “人材”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|1: Everyone fell silent at her sarcastic remark.
“皮” is read “hi” and “肉” is read “niku”. The kun-reading of “皮” is “kawa”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|2: White steam is rising from the hot soup.
“湯” is read “yu” and “気” is read “ge” (voiced). It is not “yugi”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|3: In summer, fruits such as watermelon and peaches are delicious.
“果物” is read “kudamono”. “果” is usually read “ka” in other words.
漢字 Unit 1-4|4: If you keep food in the refrigerator, it lasts longer.
“蔵” is read “zou” and “庫” is read “ko”. “庫” is the same as in “車庫”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|5: On cold nights, the window glass sometimes freezes.
“凍” is read “koo-ru” and “kogo-eru”. The on-reading is “tou”, as in “冷凍”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|6: The company uniform is a blue shirt and trousers.
“制” is read “sei”. “制服” sounds the same as “征服”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|7: I handed out sweets to the children.
“菓” is read “ka”. Be careful: it looks like “果”. It is often used as “お菓子”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|8: On a winter morning, ice had formed on the puddle.
“氷” is read “koori”. The on-reading is “hyou”, as in “氷山”. It is easy to mistake for “水”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|9: If you exercise every day, the effects will show.
“効” is read “kou”. The kun-reading is “ki-ku”. “果” in “効果” is read “ka”.
漢字 Unit 1-4|10: This company makes products for the kitchen.
“製” is read “sei”. Many characters are read “sei”, such as “制” and “整”, so be careful.
漢字 Unit 1-5|1: Vegetables contain a lot of nutrition.
"栄" is read "ei" and "養" is read "you". The "you" is a long vowel.
漢字 Unit 1-5|2: Using spices changes the taste of a dish.
"香" is "kou" and "辛" is "shin" (on-yomi), not the kun-yomi "kaori" or "karai".
漢字 Unit 1-5|3: The doctor told me to cut down on salt.
"塩" is read "en" here (kun-yomi is "shio"). "分" is read "bun".
漢字 Unit 1-5|4: I bought canned food for emergencies.
漢字 Unit 1-5|5: I bought flour to bake bread.
"粉" is read "ko" here; it can also be "kona" or "fun". "小麦" is "komugi".
漢字 Unit 1-5|6: After work, I went out to eat with a coworker.
"同" is "dou" and "僚" is "ryou". Do not shorten it to "douryo".
漢字 Unit 1-5|7: I take a water bottle filled with tea on the school trip.
"筒" is read "tou" here; it can also be read "tsutsu". "水" is "sui".
漢字 Unit 1-5|8: Egg yolk contains a lot of vitamins.
"卵" can be "ran" or "tamago". "卵黄" is read "ranou".
漢字 Unit 1-5|9: I bought a boxed lunch at the station and ate it on the Shinkansen.
"弁" is read "ben", and "当" in "弁当" is read "tou".
漢字 Unit 1-5|10: My grandfather grows vegetables in his field.
"菜" in "野菜" is read "sai". It can also be read "na" (e.g. 菜の花).
漢字 Unit 2-1|1: I saw an exhibition of contemporary art at the art museum.
"芸" is "gei" and "術" is "jutsu". Do not drop the "tsu".
漢字 Unit 2-1|2: My grandfather is raising rare plants.
"珍" is read "mezura(shii)". It can also be "chin" (e.g. 珍品).
漢字 Unit 2-1|3: My older sister can play three instruments.
"楽" is normally "gaku", but in "楽器" it becomes "gakki" with a small "tsu".
漢字 Unit 2-1|4: A young man was playing the guitar in front of the station.
"演" is "en" and "奏" is "sou". "演" is also used in 演技 and 演劇.
漢字 Unit 2-1|5: A new theater opened near the station.
"劇" is "geki" and "場" is "jou" here, not "ba".
漢字 Unit 2-1|6: My grandmother is good at making traditional dishes.
漢字 Unit 2-1|7: The children showed their dance on the stage.
"舞" is read "bu" here. It can also be "mai" or "mau".
漢字 Unit 2-1|8: I read a book and looked into the history of Kyoto.
"歴" is "reki" and "史" is "shi". "史" is used in 歴史 and 日本史.
漢字 Unit 2-1|9: The trip was postponed to next month because of the typhoon.
"延" is read "en". It can also be "nobiru" or "nobasu". 延期 means moving a date later.
漢字 Unit 2-1|10: On the night of the festival, everyone enjoyed the Bon dance.
"踊" is read "odo(ru)". 踊り is the noun form of the verb 踊る. The on-yomi is "you".
漢字 Unit 2-2|1: Old paintings are on display at the art museum.
"展" is "ten" and "示" is "ji". "示" can also be "shimesu", but in 展示 it is "ji".
漢字 Unit 2-2|2: There are many inexpensive shops around the station.
"周" is read "shuu" here. It can also be "mawari". 周辺 is "shuuhen".
漢字 Unit 2-2|3: During consecutive holidays, every road gets congested.
"混" is "kon" and "雑" is "zatsu". "混" is the same character as in 混ざる (mazaru).
漢字 Unit 2-2|4: The employees demanded that the company raise their pay.
"要" is "you" and "求" is "kyuu". "求" can also be "motomeru".
漢字 Unit 2-2|5: In a hospital, you always keep your hands clean.
"清" is "sei" and "潔" is "ketsu". "清" can also be "kiyoi".
漢字 Unit 2-2|6: After the surgery, my grandfather is recovering well.
"順" is "jun" and "調" is "chou". "調" can also be "shiraberu".
漢字 Unit 2-2|7: After the earthquake, the town fell into confusion.
"乱" is read "ran". It can also be "midareru" or "midasu".
漢字 Unit 2-2|8: He was quietly reading a book in the corner of the room.
"隅" is read "sumi". It can be repeated as in 隅々 (sumizumi).
漢字 Unit 2-2|9: She works at an international company.
"際" is read "sai". It can also be "kiwa". 国際 is "kokusai".
漢字 Unit 2-2|10: I gave flowers as a present for my mother's birthday.
"贈" is read "oku(ru)" and also "zou" (e.g. 贈答). It is different from 送る.
漢字 Unit 2-3|1: Customs differ from country to country.
"異" is read "koto(naru)", and also "i" (e.g. 異常). 異なる means the same as ちがう.
漢字 Unit 2-3|2: The package is scheduled to arrive tomorrow afternoon.
"到" is "tou" and "着" is "chaku". The opposite word is 出発.
漢字 Unit 2-3|3: I will take my passport and plane ticket without forgetting them.
"航" is "kou", "空" is "kuu" and "券" is "ken". "空" is not "sora" here.
漢字 Unit 2-3|4: Buses in the countryside sometimes do not come according to the timetable.
"刻" is "koku" and "表" is "hyou". "表" can also be "omote" or "arawasu".
漢字 Unit 2-3|5: I took a photo of the view from the window.
"景色" is read "keshiki". Note that "色" is read "shiki" here, not "iro".
漢字 Unit 2-3|6: Just in case, I will check inside my bag once more for anything I forgot.
漢字 Unit 2-3|7: I picked up a pretty stone in the park.
"拾" is read "hiro(u)". It is also "juu" (a formal way to write ten).
漢字 Unit 2-3|8: to bathe in; to take (a shower)
Every morning I bathe in the morning sun in the garden.
"浴" is read "a(biru)". It is also "yoku" (e.g. 入浴).
漢字 Unit 2-3|9: I stayed overnight at my friend's house.
"泊" is read "to(maru)" and also "haku" (e.g. 宿泊). It is a different character from 止まる.
漢字 Unit 2-3|10: I played on the beach collecting shells.
"貝" is read "kai". The shape of the character looks like a shell.
漢字 Unit 2-4|1: Today's match ended in a draw.
"合" is read "ai" here, not "gou". "試" is read "shi".
漢字 Unit 2-4|2: I tried a new method, but it failed.
When 失 and 敗 join, a small "tsu" comes in and it is read "shippai" with "pa".
漢字 Unit 2-4|3: trouble; hassle; taking care of someone
Preparing for the move is a hassle.
"面" is "men" and "倒" is "dou". "面倒をみる" also means to take care of someone.
漢字 Unit 2-4|4: Ideas that go against the trend of the times are hard to accept.
"逆" is read "saka". Also learn the on-reading "gyaku" (逆転) and 逆さ (sakasa).
漢字 Unit 2-4|5: I slept soundly on the soft futon.
"柔" is read "yawa". In 柔道 it is read "juu". 軟らかい is another way to write it.
漢字 Unit 2-4|6: A player was substituted during the match.
"交" is "kou" and "代" is "tai" (not voiced "dai"). Used when people take each other's place.
漢字 Unit 2-4|7: The older and younger brothers want to compete at everything.
"競" is read "kyou". The kun-reading "kisou" (競う) also exists. "争" is read "sou".
漢字 Unit 2-4|8: I bought a magazine at the station kiosk.
"雑" takes a small "tsu" and is read "zas". "誌" is read "shi" and relates to publications and records.
漢字 Unit 2-4|9: We compare life in the Edo period with life today.
"代" is read "dai". It is used in words for periods of time such as 時代 and 古代.
漢字 Unit 2-4|10: At the award ceremony, she had the bronze medal hung around her neck.
"銅" is read "dou". The 1st, 2nd and 3rd places get gold, silver and bronze medals.
漢字 Unit 2-5|1: I made a mistake operating the machine and was warned by the teacher.
"操" is read "sou"; the kun-reading is "ayatsuru". "作" is read "sa" here, not "saku".
漢字 Unit 2-5|2: The medicine worked and the fever went down.
"効" is read "ki". The on-reading is "kou" (効果). The okurigana is "ku". It can also be written 利く.
漢字 Unit 2-5|3: I just cannot accept his opinion.
"納" takes a small "tsu" and is read "nat". It is not "nou" as in 納入.
漢字 Unit 2-5|4: Remove the skin of the vegetables and boil them.
"除" is read "nozo". The on-reading is "jo" (削除, 除外). The form "〜を除いて" is very common.
漢字 Unit 2-5|5: I keep up the habit of reading a book every night.
"習" is "shuu" and "慣" is "kan". It is not voiced as "shuugan".
漢字 Unit 2-5|6: Playing in the road is dangerous.
"険" is read "ken". "危" is read "ki", and also "abu" in あぶない.
漢字 Unit 2-5|7: The school's facilities were renewed, and it became easier to study.
"設" is read "setsu". The kun-reading is "mouker-u" (設ける).
漢字 Unit 2-5|8: I set a goal and practice a little every day.
"標" is read "hyou" and "目" is read "moku" here (not "me").
漢字 Unit 2-5|9: I would like to change my reservation date.
"更" is read "kou". The kun-reading is "sara" (更に). 変更 means changing plans or rules.
漢字 Unit 2-5|10: I invited my friends to the wedding.
"招" is "shou" and "待" is "tai". 待 is the same character as in 待つ (matsu) but is read "tai" here. The kun-reading of 招 is "mane" (招く).
漢字 Unit 3-1|1: My grandmother is healthy and walks every day.
"祖" is "so" and "母" is read "bo" here (on-reading), unlike 母 (haha) or 母親 (hahaoya).
漢字 Unit 3-1|2: The sisters attend the same school.
"妹" is read "mai" (on-reading). 姉妹 is read "shimai", not "ane-imouto". "姉" is read "shi".
漢字 Unit 3-1|3: I became close with him and we often play together.
"親" is read "shita" here. It differs from 親 (oya) and 親 (shin).
漢字 Unit 3-1|4: "娘" is read "musume". Be careful: it looks similar to 息子 (musuko).
漢字 Unit 3-1|5: He has been that teacher's disciple for three years.
"弟" is read "de" here (not "otouto", "tei" or "dai"). 弟子 does not mean "younger brother".
漢字 Unit 3-1|6: to suit; to look good on
"似" is "ni" and "合" is "a". It combines 似る (niru) and 合う (au). Used in the form "〜に似合う".
漢字 Unit 3-1|7: The amount of medicine differs depending on age.
"齢" is read "rei". 年齢 is "nenrei". It is also used in 高齢 (kourei).
漢字 Unit 3-1|8: Every summer we visit our ancestors' grave.
"祖" is read "so". It is also used in 祖母 (sobo), 祖父 (sofu) and 先祖 (senzo).
漢字 Unit 3-1|9: Let's protect nature for our descendants.
"孫" is read both "mago" and "son". In 子孫 it is read "son".
漢字 Unit 3-1|10: Recently, more men are taking part in child-rearing.
"児" is read "ji". It is also used in 児童 (jidou) and 幼児 (youji). "育" is read "iku".
漢字 Unit 3-2|1: to hold in one's arms; to have (a problem)
He is troubled, carrying a big problem.
"抱" is read "kaka". It can also be read "daku" (抱く). "問題を抱える" (to have a problem) is a common usage.
漢字 Unit 3-2|2: A wise person learns from failure.
"賢" is read "kashiko". The on-reading is "ken" (賢明). Do not forget the "ko" in "kashikoi".
漢字 Unit 3-2|3: When I was little, I often went fishing with my grandfather.
"幼" is read "osana". Do not forget the "na" in "osanai". The on-reading is "you" (幼稚園).
漢字 Unit 3-2|4: I stayed up late and overslept.
"坊" is read "bou". It is the same character as in 赤ん坊 (akanbou).
漢字 Unit 3-2|5: Companions who share the same goal are reassuring.
"仲" is read "naka". The on-reading is "chuu" (仲介). "間" is read "ma" here (not "kan").
漢字 Unit 3-2|6: Was it a bother that I called when you were busy?
"迷" is "mei" and "惑" is "waku". Only in 迷子 (maigo) is 迷 read "mai". The form "迷惑をかける" is common.
漢字 Unit 3-2|7: After turning twenty, I became independent from my parents.
"独" is read "doku". The kun-reading is "hitori" (独り). It is also used in 独身 and 独特.
漢字 Unit 3-2|8: An elderly person is taking a walk with a dog in the park.
"老" is read "rou". The kun-reading is "oi" (老いる). It means almost the same as お年寄り.
漢字 Unit 3-2|9: She gave birth at the hospital, and her family was delighted.
"産" is "san" and "出" is "shut" with a small "tsu". It is the same character as in 産む (umu).
漢字 Unit 3-2|10: He is a typical Japanese office worker.
"型" is read "kei" (and also "kata"). In 新型 and 大型 it is read "gata".
漢字 Unit 3-6|1: A large mountain is painted in the background of the stage.
“背” is read “hai” here (not “se” as in 背中). It is not “seikei”.
漢字 Unit 3-6|2: to aim at; to aim for
He is studying to become a doctor.
The “za” is voiced: it is “mezasu”, not “mesasu”. Often used as “目指して”.
漢字 Unit 3-6|3: “拍” is “haku” and “手” is “shu” here. It is not “hakuju”.
漢字 Unit 3-6|4: After running, sweat beaded on my forehead.
“額” is read “hitai” (forehead). It is “gaku” in 金額 (amount of money).
漢字 Unit 3-6|5: I had a terrible headache yesterday, so I took a day off work.
漢字 Unit 3-6|6: I carried a heavy load and hurt my lower back.
“腰” is read “koshi”. The on-reading “yō” appears in words like 腰痛.
漢字 Unit 3-6|7: Taking medicine on an empty stomach can make your stomach hurt.
“腹” is “fuku” (on-reading) and “hara” (kun-reading). Also used in お腹 (onaka).
漢字 Unit 3-6|8: In winter the air is dry and the skin gets rough easily.
“膚” is read “fu”. It is a hard character, so watch the 月 (flesh) part.
漢字 Unit 3-6|9: After running, my chest feels tight.
“胸” is read “mune”. The on-reading is “kyō” (as in 胸囲). Also means one's feelings.
漢字 Unit 3-6|10: He has long hair, tied back in one bunch.
“髪” is “hatsu” (on-reading) and “kami” (kun-reading). 白髪 is read “shiraga”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|1: The president said he wanted to hire someone with experience.
“雇う” is read “yatou”. The noun 雇用 is read “koyō”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|2: This product has a reputation for being of excellent quality.
“優” is read “sugu(reru)”, “yasa(shii)” or “yū”. Often used as “優れた”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|3: “刺” is “shi” (on-reading) and “激” is “geki”. 刺す is read “sasu”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|4: He passed the interview and was hired as a regular employee.
“採” is read “sai” (on-reading of 採る “toru”). Watch the part that looks like 才.
漢字 Unit 4-1|5: The café in front of the station is recruiting staff.
漢字 Unit 4-1|6: The teacher gave the students a chance to present.
“与” is read “ata(eru)” or “yo”. Often used as “影響を与える”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|7: When my grandfather was young, he lost a lot of money on stocks.
“株” is read “kabu”. 株式会社 is read “kabushiki gaisha”.
漢字 Unit 4-1|8: This company has a rich track record of overseas sales.
“績” is read “seki”. Be careful: it looks like 積 (“seki”, “tsu(mu)”).
漢字 Unit 4-1|9: I shared the moving work with my older brother.
“担” is read “tan”. Also used in 担当 and 負担.
漢字 Unit 4-1|10: My monthly rent is one third of my salary.
“家” is read “ya” and “賃” “chin”. It is not “iechin”. 賃金 is also used.
漢字 Unit 4-2|1: Since we got married, my wife's income has also become important.
“収” is read “shū”. The opposite of 収入 is 支出 (expenses).
漢字 Unit 4-2|2: to entrust; to leave to someone
I decided to leave the management of the shop to my eldest son.
“任” is read “maka(seru)” or “nin”. Often seen in “お任せください”.
漢字 Unit 4-2|3: The section chief did not blame his subordinate who made the mistake.
“責” is read “se(meru)” or “seki”. It differs in meaning from 攻める (to attack).
漢字 Unit 4-2|4: At this company, transportation costs are paid in full.
“支” is read “shi”. 支給 is used when a company or office provides something.
漢字 Unit 4-2|5: This week is busy, and I am working overtime every day.
“残” is voiced: “zan”. Easily confused with 産業 (sangyō).
漢字 Unit 4-2|6: After graduating from university, I plan to work for a local bank.
“就” is read “shū”, and also “tsu(ku)” as in 仕事に就く.
漢字 Unit 4-2|7: Having experience is a condition for this job.
“条” is read “jō”. Used in 条件, 条約, 条文, etc.
漢字 Unit 4-2|8: My first choice is the local university.
“志” is read “shi” and also “kokoroza(su)”. 志望 is often used for school or job applications.
漢字 Unit 4-2|9: My older brother will graduate from university next year.
“卒” is read “sotsu”. Also used in 大卒 (university graduate).
漢字 Unit 4-2|10: The length of working hours is set by law.
“労” is read “rō”. Also used in 労働者 and 苦労.
漢字 Unit 4-3|1: The doctor has studied sea creatures for many years.
博士 has the special reading “hakase” (also “hakushi”). “博” is “haku” and “士” is “shi”.
漢字 Unit 4-3|2: I have to finish writing my thesis before graduation.
“文” is voiced here: “bun”. It is “ronbun”, not “ronmon”.
漢字 Unit 4-3|3: He lost his family in an accident.
“失” is read “ushina(u)” or “shitsu”. Do not forget the “na” in 失う.
漢字 Unit 4-3|4: My mother does not allow me to go out late at night.
“許” is read “yuru(su)” or “kyo”. Also used in 許可 (kyoka).
漢字 Unit 4-3|5: This movie is based on a real incident.
“基” is read “moto” or “ki”. It is written with “づ” (not “ず”).
漢字 Unit 4-3|6: He is a great person who built up the company by himself.
“偉” is read “era(i)” or “i”. Also read “idai” in 偉大.
漢字 Unit 4-3|7: The bank in front of the station is not open on Sundays.
“営” is read “ei” or “itona(mu)”. Be careful: it looks like 栄 and 労.
漢字 Unit 4-3|8: Some people change their family name when they marry.
“姓” is read “sei”. Also in 姓名 and 旧姓. It looks like 性.
漢字 Unit 4-3|9: Have you finished preparing for tomorrow's meeting?
“準” is read “jun”. Also in 基準 and 水準. Easily confused with 順 and 純.
漢字 Unit 4-3|10: There is a high possibility of rain tomorrow.
“能” is read “nō”. Also in 能力 (nōryoku). 可能性 is read “kanōsei”.
漢字 Unit 3-3|1: She always greets people with a smile.
漢字 Unit 3-3|2: a message left with someone to pass on
I asked someone to pass a message to Mr. Tanaka.
"言" is read "gon". Used when you ask a person to pass the message on.
漢字 Unit 3-3|3: My father is in a very good mood today.
Often used as "機嫌がいい/悪い".
漢字 Unit 3-3|4: Past form is "叫んだ". Stronger than "呼ぶ" (to call).
漢字 Unit 3-3|5: Stronger than "嫌う". The adjective is "憎い".
漢字 Unit 3-3|6: This car is old, but its condition is very good.
Used as "状態がいい/悪い" or "〜の状態".
漢字 Unit 3-3|7: My mother raised me with love.
"情" is read "jou". Often "愛情を注ぐ".
漢字 Unit 3-3|8: I had a bad feeling, so I made a phone call.
漢字 Unit 3-3|9: Three languages are used in this country.
"言" is "gen" here, different from "gon" in "伝言".
漢字 Unit 3-3|10: "〜状" means a letter or document (e.g. 年賀状).
漢字 Unit 3-3|11: I am worrying about my future path by myself.
Write "悩" (with the heart radical). Suggests long, painful thinking.
漢字 Unit 3-3|12: First, we need to know the current state of the company.
Write "現". Often "現状を変える" or "現状維持".
漢字 Unit 3-3|13: The teacher got angry at the student who was late.
Write "怒". "叱る" means to scold for the person's good; "怒る" is an emotion.
漢字 Unit 3-3|14: I hear he has a girlfriend abroad.
漢字 Unit 3-3|15: He is talking to himself as he walks.
漢字 Unit 3-4|1: I have plans to meet a friend today.
Special reading. Do not read each kanji separately.
漢字 Unit 3-4|2: I will explain using a familiar example.
Written "みぢか". Often used as "身近な〜".
漢字 Unit 3-4|3: Different from "尋ねる" (to ask). "訪ねる" means to go and see.
漢字 Unit 3-4|4: I am praying for everyone's safety.
漢字 Unit 3-4|5: The house with the red roof is the landmark.
漢字 Unit 3-4|6: There are people of many religions in this country.
漢字 Unit 3-4|7: I hope this beautiful scenery remains forever.
Used as "永久に". Almost the same as "永遠".
漢字 Unit 3-4|8: to calm down; to settle down
I will contact you when work calms down.
漢字 Unit 3-4|10: Would you like to go together this coming Sunday?
Here "今" is read "kon", unlike in "今日".
漢字 Unit 3-4|11: I saw a large Buddha statue at the temple.
漢字 Unit 3-4|12: I made a mistake in front of everyone and felt embarrassed.
漢字 Unit 3-4|13: This old-model computer can no longer be used.
漢字 Unit 3-4|14: My first impression of him was that he was a kind person.
Write "印". Often "印象に残る", "第一印象".
漢字 Unit 3-4|15: Next week I will visit the customer's company.
漢字 Unit 3-5|1: It is important to respect older people.
"敬" is read "uyama(u)" here, but "kei" in "敬語".
漢字 Unit 3-5|2: Let's respect the other person's opinion.
Used as "尊重する", with objects such as opinions or culture.
漢字 Unit 3-5|3: to pray (with hands together); to worship
I put my hands together and prayed at the shrine.
漢字 Unit 3-5|4: Keigo for your own action toward a customer; often "承りました".
漢字 Unit 3-5|5: He is an important presence in the class.
"存" is read "son". Also used as "存在する".
漢字 Unit 3-5|6: I will come to you right away.
Use for your own going/coming, not for the other person's.
漢字 Unit 3-5|7: This text consists of three parts.
Often used as "〜から構成される".
漢字 Unit 3-5|8: I forgot to save the file.
Used for data ("データを保存") and food ("保存食").
漢字 Unit 3-5|10: A well-mannered student is praised by teachers.
Often "礼儀正しい" or "礼儀を守る".
漢字 Unit 3-5|11: This book will be useful as a reference for the report.
Write "参". Used as "参考にする", "参考書".
漢字 Unit 3-5|12: I don't mind if you're a little late.
漢字 Unit 3-5|13: Write "尊". "尊敬語" is respectful keigo.
漢字 Unit 3-5|14: I have looked at the materials.
Write "拝". Use for your own seeing.
漢字 Unit 3-5|15: Yes, understood. I will send it by tomorrow.
Write "承". "承知しました" is more polite than "分かりました".
漢字 Unit 7-1|1: He was elected in the mayoral election.
漢字 Unit 7-1|2: to make up for; to supplement
I made up for the shortage with my savings.
漢字 Unit 7-1|3: The prime minister will go abroad next month.
漢字 Unit 7-1|4: I work for a private company.
漢字 Unit 7-1|5: Since there was no time, I left out the explanation.
Form: "省いて". Same kanji as "省略".
漢字 Unit 7-1|7: The prime minister held a press conference.
漢字 Unit 7-2|1: Demand for air conditioners rises in summer.
Remember as a pair: "需要と供給".
漢字 Unit 7-2|3: This year's sales exceeded last year's.
Past form: "上回った". Opposite: "下回る".
漢字 Unit 7-2|5: to change for the better; to revise
It was decided that the rules would be revised.
漢字 Unit 7-2|6: This product will go on sale next month.
漢字 Unit 7-2|8: We suffered great damage from the typhoon.
漢字 Unit 7-3|1: We crossed the border by train.
漢字 Unit 7-3|2: The two countries talked about territory.
漢字 Unit 7-3|3: Two teams competed for the championship.
漢字 Unit 7-3|5: Everyone has the right to express an opinion.

漢字 Unit 7-4|2: I looked for my friend in the crowd.
漢字 Unit 7-4|3: Formal; used in speeches and writing.
漢字 Unit 7-4|4: I edit books at a publishing company.

漢字 Unit 7-4|6: I found the first edition of this book at an old bookstore.
漢字 Unit 7-4|7: This text is easy to read.
漢字 Unit 7-4|8: The author of this book is a famous doctor.
漢字 Unit 7-5|1: There is an exam the week after next.
"再" is read "sa". Same in "再来月", "再来年".
漢字 Unit 7-5|2: When my cold gets better, I will go to school.
Illness is "治る"; broken things are "直る".
漢字 Unit 7-5|3: I have a bandage wrapped around my foot.
漢字 Unit 7-5|4: Symptoms such as fever and cough appeared.
漢字 Unit 7-5|5: The tests showed no problems with my internal organs.
漢字 Unit 7-5|6: The doctor diagnosed me with a cold.
漢字 Unit 7-5|7: In the countryside, some towns lack medical care.
漢字 Unit 4-4|1: There is a shop that serves free meals for poor people.
“貧” is read “mazu(shii)” here. The “hin” in “hinkon” is the on reading.
漢字 Unit 4-4|2: Doctors work every day to save as many lives as possible.
“救” is read “kyuu” in the on reading, as in “kyuujo” (rescue).
漢字 Unit 4-4|3: He is a person who readily admits his own mistakes.
“認” is read “nin” in the on reading, as in “shounin” (approval).
漢字 Unit 4-4|4: A customer complained about how the shop handled things.
漢字 Unit 4-4|5: People from all over the world take part in this organization.
“組” is read “so” here. “Kumi” is the kun reading. “組織” is “soshiki”.
漢字 Unit 4-4|6: In heavy rain, it is important to evacuate early.
“避” is “hi” and “難” is “nan”. The “難” is read the same as in “konnan”.
漢字 Unit 4-4|7: He donates books to the school every year.
漢字 Unit 4-4|8: Cooperation is needed worldwide to solve the problem of poverty.
“貧” is “hin” and “困” is “kon”. “貧” is also the kanji in “mazushii”.
漢字 Unit 4-4|9: My friends cooperated, so we finished early.
“協” is “kyou” and “力” is “ryoku” here, not “chikara”.
漢字 Unit 4-4|10: In the future, I want to become an interpreter in Japan.
漢字 Unit 4-5|1: to rely on; to depend on
I want to stop a life of always relying on my parents.
“頼” is read “tayo(ru)” or “tano(mu)” as a kun reading. The “rai” in “irai” is the on reading.
漢字 Unit 4-5|2: If you do not follow the rules, it can lead to a serious accident.
“規” is “ki” and “則” is “soku”. Do not read “soku” as “zoku”.
漢字 Unit 4-5|3: I saved money by working part-time at a convenience store late at night.
“深” is “shin” and “夜” is “ya”. We do not say “fukayoru”.
漢字 Unit 4-5|4: The couple respects each other's work.
漢字 Unit 4-5|5: I decided to invite close friends to the wedding.
“招” is “mane(ku)” as a kun reading and “shou” as an on reading, as in “shoutai” (invitation).
漢字 Unit 4-5|6: I looked for shellfish in the shallow part of the sea.
漢字 Unit 4-5|7: I asked a senior colleague to make the documents.
“依” is “i” and “頼” is “rai”. The reading differs from “tayoru”.
漢字 Unit 4-5|8: I introduced a tasty ramen shop to my friend.
“紹” is “shou” and “介” is “kai”. The “介” is the same as in “kaigo” (nursing care).
漢字 Unit 4-5|9: Parents have a duty to raise their children.
“義” is “gi” and “務” is “mu”. “義務” means something you must do.
漢字 Unit 4-5|10: My commute takes an hour, so I spend it reading.
“勤” is read “kin”. It is the same kanji as in “tsutomeru” (to work for).
漢字 Unit 5-1|1: This bay has calm waves and is a good place for ships to rest.
“湾” is read “wan”. It appears in place names such as “Toukyou-wan” (Tokyo Bay).
漢字 Unit 5-1|2: I sat on the riverbank and fished leisurely.
“岸” is “kishi” as a kun reading and “gan” as an on reading, as in “kaigan” (coast).
漢字 Unit 5-1|3: Her feelings are complicated, and I can't tell whether she is happy or sad.
“複” is “fuku” and “雑” is “zatsu”. The “za” is voiced.
漢字 Unit 5-1|4: In autumn, the whole valley is colored red and yellow.
“谷” is read “tani” as a kun reading. In “Shibuya” it is read “ya”.
漢字 Unit 5-1|5: This weekend I plan to go on a hot-spring trip with friends.
“泉” is read “sen” in the on reading. “Izumi” is the kun reading. “温泉” is “onsen”.
漢字 Unit 5-1|6: The continent closest to Japan is the Asian continent.
“陸” is read “riku”, as in “chakuriku” (landing). It is not “roku”.
漢字 Unit 5-1|7: The number of tourists grew, and the shops in town became lively.
“観” is read “kan”. It is the same as in “kansatsu” (observation).
漢字 Unit 5-1|8: In this area, there is a festival every summer.
“域” is read “iki”. It is also used in “ryuuiki” (river basin) and “kuiki” (zone).
漢字 Unit 5-1|9: In Europe and America, people often greet each other with a handshake.
漢字 Unit 5-1|10: Kyushu (the large island in southwestern Japan and its region)
In southern Kyushu, it hardly snows even in winter.
“九” is read “kyuu” here, not “ku”. “州” is “shuu”.
漢字 Unit 5-2|1: To plant a tree in the garden, we need to dig a deep hole.
“掘” is read “ho(ru)” as a kun reading. The on reading is “kutsu”.
漢字 Unit 5-2|2: We value the time when the whole family gathers around the table.
“囲” is read “kako(mu)” as a kun reading. The on reading is “i”, as in “shuui” (surroundings).
漢字 Unit 5-2|3: The workers are filling the hole in the road with soil.
“埋” is read “u(meru)” or “u(maru)”. “Umeru” is also used for filling a hole.
漢字 Unit 5-2|4: This stone is hard, so it can't be broken by hand.
“硬” is read “kata(i)” as a kun reading and “kou” as an on reading, as in “kouka” (coin).
漢字 Unit 5-2|5: My savings have grown, so I decided to buy a new computer.
“貯” is “cho” and “金” is “kin”. Do not lengthen it to “choukin”.
漢字 Unit 5-2|6: Influenced by my friend, I also started morning jogging.
“影” is “ei” and “響” is “kyou”. Read “eikyou” with long vowels.
漢字 Unit 5-2|7: Countries with few natural resources depend on imports.
“資” is “shi” and “源” is “gen”. “資” is also used in “shiryou” (materials) and “shikaku” (qualification).
漢字 Unit 5-2|8: Japan is one of the countries with a thriving fishing industry.
“漁” is read “gyo” or “ryou”. It is also used in “ryoushi” (fisherman).
漢字 Unit 5-2|9: The volcano erupted and ash fell on the town.
“爆” is read “baku”. It has many strokes, so be careful with the shape.
漢字 Unit 5-2|10: Foreign culture easily enters port towns where trade flourishes.
“貿” is read “bou”. “貿易 (boueki)” means buying and selling with other countries.
漢字 Unit 5-3|1: The company created an environment that is easy to work in.
"環" is read "kan" and "境" is read "kyou". It is not "kangyou" (no voicing).
漢字 Unit 5-3|2: to protect; to keep a promise
I took part in an activity to protect precious nature.
"守" is read "mamo-ru" (kun reading). Do not confuse it with the on readings "shu" and "su".
漢字 Unit 5-3|3: I tell my family the important news.
"伝える" means to let someone know. "伝わる" means the message reaches the person. "伝" is also read "den".
漢字 Unit 5-3|4: The sea is polluted and the fish are decreasing.
"汚" is read "o". Its kun readings are "yogo-reru" and "kitana-i".
漢字 Unit 5-3|5: a group; a herd; a flock
A flock of sheep is walking across the grassland.
"群" is read "mu-re" (kun reading). Its on reading is "gun".
漢字 Unit 5-3|6: His manner when apologizing is very polite.
"態" is read "tai" and "度" is read "do". It is not "taito".
漢字 Unit 5-3|7: A car consumes gasoline when it runs.
"費" is read "hi"; its kun reading is "tsui-yasu". It is easy to confuse with "貸" and "貿".
漢字 Unit 5-3|8: Please write an appropriate answer to the question.
"適" is read "teki". It is easy to confuse with "敵", "滴" and "摘", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 5-3|9: The teacher manages the class computers.
"管" is read "kan". It is easy to confuse with "官", "館" and "缶", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 5-3|10: "永" is read "ei". It is easy to confuse with "泳" and "栄" (same reading) and "氷" (similar shape).
漢字 Unit 5-4|1: My grandfather has been farming for a long time.
"農" is read "nou". It is easy to confuse with "濃", "脳" and "能", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 5-4|2: The area around the station is always crowded.
"辺" is read "ata-ri" (kun reading). Its on reading is "hen" (e.g. 周辺).
漢字 Unit 5-4|3: "盛" is read "saka-n" (kun reading). Its on readings are "sei" and "jou" (e.g. 盛大).
漢字 Unit 5-4|4: A large field spreads out at the foot of the mountain.
"畑" is a kanji made in Japan, read "hatake". "田" (ta) means a rice paddy, so be careful with the difference.
漢字 Unit 5-4|5: This store has a wide variety of vegetables.
"豊" is read "hou" and "富" is read "fu". It is not voiced ("bu").
漢字 Unit 5-4|6: to be blessed with; to be rich in
We were blessed with good weather during the trip.
"恵" is read "megu-mu" (kun reading). Its on readings are "kei" and "e" (e.g. 恩恵, 知恵).
漢字 Unit 5-4|7: In winter, the trees in the garden wither.
"枯" is read "ka-reru" (kun reading). Its on reading is "ko" (e.g. 枯渇).
漢字 Unit 5-4|8: After plowing the soil, we sow the seeds.
"耕" is read "tagaya-su" (kun reading). Its on reading is "kou" (e.g. 耕作).
漢字 Unit 5-4|9: We feed the livestock at the ranch.
"畜" is read "chiku". It is easy to confuse with "蓄" and "築".
漢字 Unit 5-4|10: The weather was bad this year, so vegetable prices went up.
"候" is read "kou". Be careful with the very similar-looking "侯".
漢字 Unit 5-5|2: In summer, I sit in front of the fan to cool off.
"風" is usually read "fuu", but in "扇風機" it becomes "puu" (semi-voiced).
漢字 Unit 5-5|3: "接" is read "setsu", but in "接近" a small "tsu" is added: "sekkin".
漢字 Unit 5-5|4: The fire is so strong that we cannot get close.
"勢" is read "ikio-i" (kun reading). Its on reading is "sei" (e.g. 勢力). "大勢" is read "oozei".
漢字 Unit 5-5|5: The earthquake caused great damage to the town.
"被" is read "hi". It is easy to confuse with "彼", "披" and "疲".
漢字 Unit 5-5|6: Opinions clash, so the discussion is not progressing.
"衝" is read "shou" and "突" is read "totsu", the same "totsu" as in "突然".
漢字 Unit 5-5|7: A big signboard stands by the road.
"看" is read "kan" and "板" is read "ban". It is not "kanpan".
漢字 Unit 5-5|8: Furniture may fall over in a big earthquake.
"倒れる" means falling by itself; "倒す" means someone knocks something over. The on reading is "tou".
漢字 Unit 5-5|9: After the flood, mud remained on the road.
漢字 Unit 5-5|10: A strong wind warning has been issued, so it is better not to go outside.
"警" is read "kei". It is easy to confuse with "敬", "軽" and "景", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 6-1|1: "予" is read "yo" and "防" is read "bou". Do not confuse it with "予報" (yohou).
漢字 Unit 6-1|2: Japan is said to be a country with many disasters.
"災" is read "sai". Be careful with the similar-looking "炎" and with "裁" and "栽", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 6-1|3: New employees receive three days of training.
"練" is read "ren". It is easy to confuse with "錬", "連" and "陳".
漢字 Unit 6-1|4: When I stand somewhere high, my legs freeze with fear.
"恐" is read "kyou" and "怖" is read "fu". It is not voiced ("bu").
漢字 Unit 6-1|7: The family divided the property my grandfather left.
"財" is read "zai". It is easy to confuse with "材", "在" and "剤", which share the reading.
漢字 Unit 6-1|8: The police ordered the man to stop.
"命" is read "mei" and "令" is read "rei". "inochi" is the kun reading of "命".
漢字 Unit 6-1|9: The wheels got stuck in the snow and the car stopped moving.
"輪" is read "rin"; its kun reading is "wa". "車" is read "sha" here.
漢字 Unit 6-1|10: If you will be late, please contact the teacher.
"絡" is read "raku". It is easy to confuse with "落", "楽" and "格".
漢字 Unit 6-2|1: If you breathe deeply, you feel calm.
“呼” is read “ko” and “吸” is read “kyuu”. It is easy to confuse with “koukyuu” or “kokyou”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|2: I met a friend at a small café.
“喫” is read “kis” with a small tsu. Be careful not to say “kisaten”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|3: Seeing my friend who failed the exam, I felt sorry for him.
漢字 Unit 6-2|4: Smoking is prohibited on the train, so you can't smoke.
“煙” is read “en” (on-reading) here; “kemuri” is the kun-reading. Do not confuse it with “kinnen” or “kinken”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|5: At school, I learned how to escape from a fire.
“逃げる” is read “nigeru”. “逃がす” is read “nigasu” and means “to let something go free”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|6: Tonight's game will be broadcast on TV.
“放” is read “hou” (on-reading) here; “hanasu” is the kun-reading. “送” is read “sou”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|7: You can also enlarge this map when using it.
“拡” is read “kaku”. 確, 核 and 格 are also read “kaku”, so choose by meaning.
漢字 Unit 6-2|8: The power went out at night, so we used candles.
“停” is read “tei”. 定, 底 and 低 are also read “tei”, so choose the one meaning “to stop”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|9: There is an ashtray on the desk.
“灰” is read “hai”. 配 and 肺 are also read “hai”. 炭 looks similar but is read “sumi”.
漢字 Unit 6-2|10: After washing my hands, I disinfect them with alcohol.
“毒” is read “doku”. 独 and 読 are also read “doku”. 毎 looks similar, so be careful.
漢字 Unit 6-3|1: My old computer broke down, so I can't work.
“故” is read “ko” and “障” is read “shou”. Do not lengthen it to “koushou”.
漢字 Unit 6-3|2: There is a convenience store near the intersection.
“交” is read “kou” and “差” is read “sa”. “点” is “ten” and is not voiced.
漢字 Unit 6-3|3: to live; to make a living
Many students live near the university.
“暮” is read “ku” (in “kurasu”). The same character is used in “kureru” (to get dark).
漢字 Unit 6-3|4: I buy my ticket before boarding.
“切” becomes “kip” with a small tsu, and “符” is read “pu”. It is easy to mistake it for “kifu” or “kippu” with a voiced “bu”.
漢字 Unit 6-3|5: The roads in the old town are narrow.
Both “道” (michi) and “幅” (haba) are read with their kun-readings. It is not “douhaba”.
漢字 Unit 6-3|6: When the light turns green, please cross the road.
“号” is voiced: “gou”. Do not read it as “shinkou” without the voicing.
漢字 Unit 6-3|7: I lost my wallet and reported it to the police.
“警” is read “kei”. 敬 and 経 are also read “kei”. 驚 looks similar but is read “kyou” or “odoro(ku)”.
漢字 Unit 6-3|8: There is a big cherry tree in front of the prefectural office.
“庁” is read “chou”. 長, 頂 and 腸 are also read “chou”, so choose the one meaning “government office”.
漢字 Unit 6-3|9: When you go down the slope, you can see the sea.
“坂” is read “saka”. 板, 反 and 返 all contain the part 反 and look similar, so be careful.
漢字 Unit 6-3|10: I took off the price tag and then gave the present.
“札” is read “fuda”. It is also read “satsu”, as in “o-satsu” (banknote). 礼 and 机 look similar.
漢字 Unit 6-4|1: I locked up so that a thief wouldn't get in.
“泥” is read “doro” (kun-reading) and “棒” is read “bou” (on-reading). It is not “deibou”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|2: The culprit in this case was still a young man.
“犯” is read “han” and “人” is read “nin”. “人” is read “jin” in other words such as “gaikokujin”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|3: The arrested man did not say anything.
“逮” is read “tai” and “捕” is read “ho”. It is not “taibo” or “taihou”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|4: With the spread of electronic money, fewer people use cash.
“普” is read “fu” and “及” is read “kyuu”. Do not add a small tsu as in “fukkyuu”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|5: It is better to dispose of old medicine.
“処” is read “sho” and “分” is read “bun”. “処分” can also mean “to punish”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|6: I was pressured into accepting the job.
“強” is read “gou” here (compare “強力” = “kyouryoku”). “引” is read “in”.
漢字 Unit 6-4|7: I bought lottery tickets, but not a single one won.
“宝” is read “takara” (kun) or “hou” (on, as in “houseki”). It is easily confused with 実, 室 and 法.
漢字 Unit 6-4|8: “貨” is read “ka” and relates to money and goods. 貸, 資 and 賀 look similar, so be careful.
漢字 Unit 6-4|9: Stealing things from a shop is a crime.
“盗” is read “nusu(mu)” (kun) or “tou” (on). 投 is also read “tou” but has a different meaning.
漢字 Unit 6-4|10: If you handle things roughly, they break quickly.
“暴” is read “bou” here. It is also read “abare(ru)” and “baku”. 防 and 望 are also read “bou”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|1: The day after the trip, I rested at home.
“翌” is read “yoku”. “翌日” means the day after a certain day. It is not “ashita” (tomorrow).
漢字 Unit 6-5|2: I confirmed the schedule and then made a reservation.
“日” is read “nit” with a small tsu here. It is not “nichitei”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|3: At the end of the letter, I signed my name myself.
“署” is read “sho” and “名” is read “mei”. Do not lengthen it to “shoumei”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|4: I heard that a murder once happened in this town.
“殺” is read “satsu” (on-reading) and “人” is read “jin”. “koro(su)” is the kun-reading.
漢字 Unit 6-5|5: “努” is read “do” and “力” is read “ryoku”. Do not lengthen it to “douryoku”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|6: I want to reflect the students' wishes in the class.
“反” is read “han” and “映” is read “ei”. It is easy to confuse with other “han-” words such as “hanmei” or “hantei”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|7: I explained the current situation to the teacher.
“況” is read “kyou”. 境, 競 and 鏡 are also read “kyou”, so choose the one meaning “state of affairs”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|8: I was surprised by his courage.
“勇” is read “yuu”. 優, 遊 and 湧 are also read “yuu”, so choose by meaning.
漢字 Unit 6-5|9: I let my guard down and forgot my wallet.
“断” is read “dan”. It is also read “kotowa(ru)”. 段, 談 and 団 are also read “dan”.
漢字 Unit 6-5|10: There is only one bakery on this street.
“軒” is read “ken” and counts houses. The reading changes with the number: “ikken”, “niken”, “sangen”.
漢字 Unit 8-1|1: We could see a beautiful view from the top of the mountain.
"頂" can also be read "itadaki". It is also used for the "highest point" of other things.
漢字 Unit 8-1|2: to wish for, to hope for
I wish for my family's happiness.
Used as "~o nozomu". The test word is the te-form of 望む. 望 is also read "bou" (as in 希望).
漢字 Unit 8-1|3: weather of the season; also cheerful
Today the weather feels like spring.
Used for weather as in "spring weather". "陽気な人" means a cheerful person.
漢字 Unit 8-1|5: The sports day was held under a clear sky.
快 is read "kai". It means weather clearer than ordinary "hare" (sunny).
漢字 Unit 8-1|6: They say the Earth looked blue when seen from space.
A writing question for 宇. Often seen in "宇宙飛行士" (astronaut) and "宇宙船" (spaceship).
漢字 Unit 8-1|7: The station is located to the north of the school.
置 is the same character as in 置く. 位置 is a place; 地位 is a social position.
漢字 Unit 8-1|8: It will probably be cloudy from the morning tomorrow.
The noun form is "kumori". The opposite is "hareru" (to clear up).
漢字 Unit 8-2|1: "Fukumareru" is the passive form, often used as "~ni fukumarete iru".
漢字 Unit 8-2|2: Hot and humid days continue during the rainy season.
A compound of "musu" and "atsui". Watch the reading of 蒸 ("mu").
漢字 Unit 8-2|3: The average sleeping time per day is six hours.
Also used as "heikinten" and "heikin shite". 平 is "hei" and 均 is "kin".
漢字 Unit 8-2|4: Close to 予想, but 予測 is often based on data.
漢字 Unit 8-2|5: Used as "sharp question" or "sharp eyes". The opposite is "nibui" (dull).
漢字 Unit 8-2|6: This rule is simple, so you can learn it right away.
A writing question for 純. "単純な人" can sound negative (a person who does not think deeply).
漢字 Unit 8-2|7: Disinfectant is placed at the entrance.
液 is read "eki", as in 液体 and 血液.
漢字 Unit 8-2|8: to fix in place, to secure
I fixed the desk to the wall.
固 can also be read "katai". Used as "kotei suru" and "kotei sareta".
漢字 Unit 8-3|1: I will join this team next month.
"Kuwaeru" is to add something (transitive). "Kuwawaru" is to join by oneself.
漢字 Unit 8-3|2: to be away from, to leave
I left home and began living alone.
"Hanasu" is to let go (transitive). Used as "a place away from the station".
漢字 Unit 8-3|3: That singer retired at the age of fifty.
引 is read "in". Often used for athletes and entertainers. For company workers, "taishoku" is used.
漢字 Unit 8-3|4: We changed the plan because of pressure from others.
Often used as "atsuryoku o kakeru" or "atsuryoku ga kakaru".
漢字 Unit 8-3|5: Today I helped with the work in the garden.
作 is read "sa" here, different from 作る.
漢字 Unit 8-3|6: I will be sure to get up early tomorrow.
Read "kanarazu" including the "zu". It sounds stronger than "kitto".
漢字 Unit 8-3|7: 了 is read "ryou". The opposite is "kaishi" (start).
漢字 Unit 8-3|8: There is a park opposite my house.
Same character as 向く and 向かう. Used as "mukai no ie".
漢字 Unit 8-4|1: The opposite is "shizumu". "Uite" is the te-form of "uku".
漢字 Unit 8-4|2: The ship sank into the sea.
The opposite is "uku". Also used for the sun setting.
漢字 Unit 8-4|3: It began to rain on my way to school.
中 is read "chuu". Used as "~no tochuu de" and "tochuu kara".
漢字 Unit 8-4|4: I had money left over, so I saved it.
"Amaru" is intransitive. Often used as "amatta" for what is left.
漢字 Unit 8-4|5: I open the window now and then to ventilate.
換 is read "kan", the same character as in 換える and 交換.
漢字 Unit 8-4|6: I judged for myself and acted.
判 is read "han". Used as "handanryoku" and "handan suru".
漢字 Unit 8-4|7: I will make a tentative reservation first and tell them the number of people later.
仮 is read "kari". The opposite is "hon-yoyaku" (confirmed reservation).
漢字 Unit 8-4|8: Snow piled up on the mountain.
The transitive verb is "tsumu". Used for snow or dust.
漢字 Unit 8-5|1: I counted the number of participants.
漢字 Unit 8-5|2: I confirmed the time by phone.
Same character as 確か and 確認. "Tashikamete" is the te-form.
漢字 Unit 8-5|3: I added up this month's expenses.
合 is read "gou", as in 合格 and 合計.
漢字 Unit 8-5|4: The clerk worked out the change in his head.
暗 is read "an". In 暗記 and 暗算 it carries the idea of "in the head".
漢字 Unit 8-5|5: Ten divided by two is five.
"Wareru" is for something breaking by itself; "waru" is when someone breaks it.
漢字 Unit 8-5|6: There are books, notebooks, and so on on the desk.
等 is also read "tou". Usually written in hiragana as "nado".
漢字 Unit 8-5|7: Before the trip, I checked the route on a map.
図 is read "zu" here, but "to" in 図書館.
漢字 Unit 8-5|8: "時計" is read "tokei" with 時 as "to". 腕時計 is "udedokei".
漢字 Unit 9-1|1: Recently, vegetable prices tend to go up.
Often used as "~suru keikou ga aru". 傾 can also be read "katamuku".
漢字 Unit 9-1|2: Same reading as 閉める and 締める, but a different character. Often used for ratios.
漢字 Unit 9-1|3: The newspaper is delivered every morning.
配 is read "hai". Used as "haitatsu suru" and "haitatsu sareru".
漢字 Unit 9-1|4: I misunderstood his words and got angry.
誤 is read "go". Also used as "gokai o maneku" and "gokai ga tokeru".
漢字 Unit 9-1|5: Close to "tsuzukeru" but a more formal word.
漢字 Unit 9-1|6: If you go over the time, an extra fee is charged.
超 can also be read "koeru". 超過 means the same as "over".
漢字 Unit 9-1|7: The number of children is decreasing.
The opposite is 増加. Same character as 減る.
漢字 Unit 9-1|8: The number of foreign tourists is increasing.
The opposite is 減少. Same character as 増える.
漢字 Unit 9-2|2: I gave a souvenir to my teacher.
The humble form of "ageru", used when giving to a superior.
漢字 Unit 9-2|3: The bag tore and the things inside came out.
The transitive verb is "yaburu". "敗れる" (to lose) uses a different character.
漢字 Unit 9-2|4: The author of this text writes about environmental problems.
Often seen in reading questions. 筆 becomes "hit-" with a small "tsu".
漢字 Unit 9-2|5: I earned twelve credits this semester.
"Meter" and "yen" are units. At university: "tan-i o toru" (earn credits).
漢字 Unit 9-2|6: I took photos with friends at the graduation ceremony.
A writing question for 式. Also seen in 入学式 and 結婚式.
漢字 Unit 9-2|7: I made a promise to meet a friend.
Used as "yakusoku o mamoru" and "yakusoku o yaburu".
漢字 Unit 9-2|8: I printed the photo with a printer.
印 is "in" and 刷 is "satsu". Used as "insatsu suru" and "insatsuki".
漢字 Unit 9-3|1: I observe the behavior of birds.
観 is read "kan", the same character as in 観光 and 観客.
漢字 Unit 9-3|2: "Hakken" is finding something that already exists; "hatsumei" is creating something new.
漢字 Unit 9-3|3: Often used as "chuumoku o atsumeru" and "chuumoku sareru".
漢字 Unit 9-3|4: Lack of sleep has a bad effect on work.
Used as "akueikyou o ataeru" and "akueikyou ga deru". 悪 is read "aku" here.
漢字 Unit 9-3|5: I was very nervous before the presentation.
Used as "kinchou suru" and "kinchou ga tokeru".
漢字 Unit 9-3|6: I imagine life in the future.
Same reading as 創造 but a different character and meaning. A writing question for 像.
漢字 Unit 9-3|7: I looked for the key, but could not find it.
探 is also read "tan" (as in 探検). It can also be written 捜す.
漢字 Unit 9-3|8: I was stopped by the police for speeding.
Used as "ihan suru" and "kisoku ihan". 違 can also be read "chigau".
漢字 Unit 9-4|1: If you have any questions, please ask.
Used as "gimon o motsu" and "gimon ni omou".
漢字 Unit 9-4|3: 一般 is read "ippan" with a small "tsu".
漢字 Unit 9-4|4: My work was evaluated by my boss.
Often used as "takaku hyouka suru" and "hyouka ga takai".
漢字 Unit 9-4|6: You should not suspect your friends.
Same character as in 疑問. Used as "~o utagau".
漢字 Unit 9-4|7: I lit up the ground at my feet with a light.
The intransitive verb is "teru". Used as "tsuki ga michi o terasu".
漢字 Unit 9-4|8: The opposite is 否定. 肯 is read "kou".
漢字 Unit 9-5|1: I saw the festival notice on the board at the station.
Also used for online message boards. 掲 is read "kei".
漢字 Unit 9-5|2: I cleaned my room on my day off.
掃 is read "sou", as in 掃除機 and 大掃除.
漢字 Unit 9-5|4: I submitted the documents to the office.
A formal way of saying "dasu". Used as "teishutsu kigen".
漢字 Unit 9-5|5: I do office work at a hospital.
Also used as "jimusho" and "jimuin". 事 is read "ji".
漢字 Unit 9-5|6: The teacher's lectures are easy to understand.
Used as "kougi o ukeru" and "kougi o suru".
漢字 Unit 9-5|7: I am a library committee member.
Also used as "iinkai" and "iinchou". 委 is read "i".
漢字 Unit 9-5|8: Thanks to my senior's advice, I passed the exam.
Same meaning as "advice". 助 is read "jo" or "tasukeru".
漢字 Unit 7-1|9: Three names are being mentioned as candidates for the next president.
"Kouhosha" means a person running in an election. "Kouhochi" means a candidate site.
漢字 Unit 7-1|10: customs (the office that checks goods entering a country)
A package sent from abroad is checked at customs.
"税" is read "zei", as in "zeikin" and "shouhizei". It is not read "zeigan".
漢字 Unit 7-2|9: Raw materials went up, so the price of the goods also rose.
A little more formal than "nedan". Often used in economic news.
漢字 Unit 7-2|10: The company provides lunch to its employees for free.
"供" is read "kyou", as in "kyoukyuu". It is not read "teikyuu".
漢字 Unit 7-3|9: Please never let children take this medicine.
There is a small "tsu" in "zettai". "Zettai ni ~ nai" is a strong negative.
漢字 Unit 7-3|10: An international organization is helping refugees.
Often used in forms such as "kinyuu kikan" (financial institution) and "kōtsū kikan" (transport system).
漢字 Unit 7-4|9: She insisted that she knew nothing.
"張" is read "chou", as in "kinchou" and "shucchou". Do not confuse it with "shucchou" (business trip).
漢字 Unit 7-4|10: "詞" is also used in "meishi", "keiyoushi" and "joshi". It is read "shi".
漢字 Unit 7-5|9: I spread butter thinly on bread.
Read "nutte" and "nutta". "Nurigusuri" is a medicine you apply to the skin.
漢字 Unit 7-5|10: I drank too many cold drinks and my stomach feels bad.
One character, read "i". Also used in words like "ichou" and "igusuri".
漢字 Unit 8-1|9: Seen from space, the Earth looks blue.
"球" is read "kyuu", as in "yakyuu" and "denkyuu". It can also be read "tama".
漢字 Unit 8-1|10: The new employee is asking questions actively.
The opposite is "shoukyokuteki". There is a small "tsu" in "sekkyokuteki".
漢字 Unit 8-1|11: I hope to study economics at university.
"望" is read "bou", the same character as "nozomu". Do not confuse it with "忘" (wasureru).
漢字 Unit 8-2|9: This factory tries not to use substances that are bad for the body.
There is a small "tsu" in "busshitsu". It uses the same character "質" as "seishitsu".
漢字 Unit 8-2|10: This liquid is heavier than water.
Learn it together with "kotai" (solid) and "kitai" (gas). "液" is read "eki".
漢字 Unit 8-3|9: The distance from my home to the office is five kilometers.
"離" is the character of "hanareru". Read it short as "kyori", not "kyouri".
漢字 Unit 8-3|10: The wind changed direction and it suddenly got cold.
"向" is read "kou", the same character as "mukau" and "muku". Also used for the direction of an idea.
漢字 Unit 8-4|10: This device keeps the water temperature constant.
"装" is read "sou", as in "fukusou". "置" can also be read "oku".
漢字 Unit 8-5|9: Half a pizza is written as one half in fractions.
"分" is read "bun", not "fun". Learn it together with "shousuu" (decimal).
漢字 Unit 8-5|10: I decide this month's budget and then spend money.
"予" is read "yo", the same character as in "yotei" and "yosou".
漢字 Unit 9-1|9: probability; the chance that something will happen
The chance of rain tomorrow is high.
"率" is read "ritsu". Often used as "kakuritsu ga takai/hikui". "確" is not voiced.
漢字 Unit 9-1|10: procedure; the steps and paperwork you must complete at an office
I did the moving procedures at city hall.
The sound "tsu" comes from 続き (tsuzuki). It is "tetsuzuki", not "tezuzuki". Often used as "tetsuzuki o suru".
漢字 Unit 9-2|9: good and evil; right and wrong
Even small children should be taught the difference between right and wrong.
"善悪" can also be read "yoshiashi", but for N2 learn "zen'aku". Both parts are on-yomi.
漢字 Unit 9-2|10: The cover of this book is very beautiful.
表 is "hyou" and 紙 is "shi" here. 紙 is also read "kami", but not in this word.
漢字 Unit 9-2|11: phenomenon; an event or situation that can be seen or observed
Snow falling in summer is a strange phenomenon.
"現" means "to appear". Do not confuse it with 原 or 限. Used in "shizen genshou" (natural phenomenon).
漢字 Unit 9-3|9: If you look at the two graphs, the difference is obvious.
明 has many readings: あか(るい), あき(らか), めい, みょう. Also used as "akiraka ni naru".
漢字 Unit 9-3|10: Next week I am going to Osaka on a business trip.
出張 has a small "っ": shucchou. 張 is often confused with 帳 and 長.
漢字 Unit 9-4|9: common sense; basic knowledge that everyone is expected to have
Not making loud noises at night is common sense.
常 is read じょう or つね. 識 is しき. The opposite is 非常識 (hijoushiki).
漢字 Unit 9-4|10: wisdom; the ability to think and solve problems well
We shared our wisdom and solved the problem.
Different from 知識 (chishiki). Often used as "chie o dasu" or "chie o shiboru". 恵 is read "e".
漢字 Unit 9-4|11: After coming back from the trip, I returned to daily life.
Used in "nichijou seikatsu" and "nichijou kaiwa". 常 is often confused with 状 and 条.
漢字 Unit 9-5|9: I put the letter in an envelope and stuck on a stamp.
封 has two readings, ふう and ほう. 封筒 is "fuutou".
漢字 Unit 9-5|10: When work is over, I go straight home.
"帰宅する" means going home, a bit formal. Learn it together with 帰国 (kikoku).
漢字 Unit 9-5|11: guidance; showing someone around or telling them how to get somewhere
I was helped by being guided to the station.
案 is read "an". Often confused with 安 and 桜. Used in "annai suru" and "annaijou".
漢字 Unit 10-1|9: Countries near the equator are hot all year.
赤 is read "aka" or "seki". 道 is "dou". It is not "akamichi".
漢字 Unit 10-1|10: Every day I read the morning paper before going to the office.
朝 is read "asa" or "chou". The opposite is 夕刊 (yuukan), the evening edition.
漢字 Unit 10-2|8: When my grandfather was young, he worked as a carpenter.
工 is read "kou" or "ku". 大工 is "daiku", not "daikou".
漢字 Unit 10-2|9: construction; building something large such as a building or road
A new building is being constructed in front of the station.
建 is also read "tateru". Often confused with 健 and 鍵. Used in "kensetsu gaisha" and "kensetsu chuu".
漢字 Unit 10-2|10: sense; sensation; the ability to feel things
It was so cold that I lost the feeling in my fingers.
感覚 uses 感 as in 感じる. 覚 is also read "oboeru". Do not confuse 感 with 観 or 間.
漢字 Unit 10-3|9: I get seven hours of sleep every day.
Often used as "suimin o toru" and "suimin busoku" (lack of sleep). 睡 is read "sui".
漢字 Unit 10-3|10: concentration; how strong or thick a liquid is
I added water and lowered the salt concentration.
濃 is also read "koi". Often confused with 農, 脳, 能. Learn 濃度 and 濃い together.
漢字 Unit 10-4|9: to step back; to retire from a position
I decided to step down from the chairman position I held for many years.
退 is also read "tai" (as in 退職). In the sense of leaving a position, it is "shirizoku".
漢字 Unit 10-4|10: to tie; to connect; to form (a relationship)
Before running, I tie my shoelaces tightly.
"結ぶ" is also used as in "keiyaku o musubu" (sign a contract). 結 is also read "ketsu" and "yuu".
漢字 Unit 10-5|9: I had today's lunch at a shop in front of the station.
飯 is read "meshi", a casual word for rice or a meal. Same for 朝飯 and 晩飯.
漢字 Unit 10-5|10: I am happy to be able to live together with my family.
Often used as "~to tomo ni", and often written in hiragana. 共 looks like 供, so be careful.
漢字 Unit 10-5|11: All of the meeting materials are ready.
"全て" means the same as 全部. 全く (mattaku) also uses 全. 全 is also read "zen".
